searchDocs.title: model​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the path to the object detection model file.  Type: StringDefault: NULLAccess: Read/Write  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctobd model=/usr/share/synap/models/yolov8s-640x384/model.synap ...   note Model changes require pipeline restart to take effect.

searchDocs.title: model-directory​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the directory to scan for available model files.  Type: StringDefault: "/usr/share/synap/models"Access: Read/Write  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctobd model-directory=/custom/models ...

searchDocs.title: available-models​
searchDocs.content: Returns the list of available model files found in the model directory.  Type: String (comma-separated list)Default: NULLAccess: Read-only  Usage:  With APIGST API char *models = api_dctobd_get_available_models(<element_object>); if (models) { printf("Available models: %s\n", models); free(models); }

searchDocs.title: label​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the path to the label/info JSON file containing class labels.  Type: StringDefault: NULL (falls back to /usr/share/synap/models/object_detection/coco/info.json)Access: Read/Write  Usage:  BashGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctobd label=/usr/share/synap/models/object_detection/coco/info.json ...   note Label file changes require pipeline restart to take effect. If not specified, the plugin uses a default label file path.

searchDocs.title: mode​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the post-processing mode for the model output.  Type: StringDefault: NULLAccess: Read/WriteValid values: "detector"  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctobd mode=detector ...

searchDocs.title: threshold​
searchDocs.content: Sets the confidence threshold for detections.  Type: Float (0.0 to 1.0)Default: 0.5Access: Read/Write  Only detections with confidence scores above this threshold will be reported. Lower values produce more detections but may include false positives.  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctobd threshold=0.7 ...

searchDocs.title: numinference​
searchDocs.content: Sets the maximum number of detections per frame.  Type: Integer (Unsigned)Default: 5Access: Read/Write  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctobd numinference=10 ...

searchDocs.title: frameinterval​
searchDocs.content: Sets the number of frames to skip between inferences.  Type: Integer (Unsigned)Default: 0 (process every frame)Access: Read/Write  Use this to reduce processing load by running inference on every Nth frame.  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API # Process every 3rd frame gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctobd frameinterval=3 ...

searchDocs.title: inferstatistics​
searchDocs.content: Enables logging of inference performance statistics.  Type: BooleanDefault: falseAccess: Read/Write  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctobd inferstatistics=true ...

searchDocs.title: detection-enabled​
searchDocs.content: Enables or disables object detection processing.  Type: BooleanDefault: trueAccess: Read/Write  When disabled, frames pass through the element without any detection processing.  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API # Enable detection gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctobd detection-enabled=true ... # Disable detection gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctobd detection-enabled=false ...

searchDocs.title: enabled-classes​
searchDocs.content: Specifies which object classes to detect.  Type: String (comma-separated class names)Default: "person,car,bicycle"Access: Read/Write  Set to a comma-separated list of class names to filter detections. Set to empty string or NULL to enable all classes.  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API # Detect only persons and cars gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctobd enabled-classes="person,car" ... # Detect all vehicle types gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctobd enabled-classes="car,truck,bus,motorcycle" ...   note Class names are case-sensitive and must match exactly as provided by the model.

searchDocs.title: available-classes​
searchDocs.content: Returns the list of classes supported by the loaded model.  Type: String (comma-separated class names)Default: NULLAccess: Read-only  Query this property to see which object classes the current model can detect.  Usage:  With APIGST API char *classes = api_dctobd_get_available_classes(<element_object>); if (classes) { printf("Available classes: %s\n", classes); free(classes); }

searchDocs.title: Overview​
searchDocs.content: This page describes the steps to build Yocto images for SOM_SL1680_Mk1 and EVK_SL1680_Mk1. This guide assumes that the reader already has some familiarity with Yocto concepts. If not please refer Yocto documentation for a quick overview.  info Please make sure that your email id has been registered with Digital Core Technologies so that the complete source code is accessible.

searchDocs.title: Building the image​
searchDocs.content: To ensure proper configuration and clean environment, the build must be performed inside a docker container. Synaptics provides a pre-built container at ghcr.io/synaptics-astra/crops. To start the container, execute the command :  docker run --rm -it -v $(pwd):$(pwd) -v ~/.ssh/:/home/pokyuser/.ssh ghcr.io/synaptics-astra/crops:1.0.0 --workdir=$(pwd)   -v ~/.ssh/:/home/pokyuser/.ssh parameter must be added to let the container access the ssh keys in the system for cloning private repositories for recipes. In order to do so, you must ensure your system has access rights to the private repository.  If SW 1.0.3 or higher version is used, start the container using this command :  docker run --rm -it -v $(pwd):$(pwd) -v ~/.ssh/:/home/pokyuser/.ssh ghcr.io/synaptics-astra/crops:1.1.0 --workdir=$(pwd)   -v ~/.ssh/:/home/pokyuser/.ssh parameter must be added to let the container access the ssh keys in the system for cloning private repositories for recipes. In order to do so, you must ensure your system has access rights to the private repository.  note On Ubuntu 20 and 18 LTS, the seccomp protection feature of Docker has to be disabled when creating the build container by adding the parameter --security-opt "seccomp=unconfined" after the --rm parameter in the docker command.  To build sentinel-media image, execute the following commands from the sdk directory  MACHINE=sentinel-som-sl1680-mk1-rfb-mk1 source meta-dctk-sentinel/setup/setup-environment bitbake sentinel-media  To build sentinel-media-oobe image, execute the following commands from the sdk directory  OOBE=enabled MACHINE=sentinel-som-sl1680-mk1-rfb-mk1 source meta-dctk-sentinel/setup/setup-environment bitbake sentinel-media-oobe  This creates a default folder named build in the sdk directory. You can also specify the name of your build directory by passing it as an argument in the setup command. For example to create the build folder as build-sentinel, modify the command as :  MACHINE=sentinel-som-sl1680-mk1-rfb-mk1 source meta-dctk-sentinel/setup/setup-environment build-sentinel  The build folder will be the parent directory where yocto does its compilations and provide the final image. The final image after the build process will be found in <build-dir>/tmp/deploy/images/sentinel-som-sl1680-mk1-rfb-mk1/SYNAIMG/  If you are rebuilding the same image for the same machine, it is recommended to clean the generated build artifacts of the image before rebuilding. In order to clean, execute the command :  bitbake -c clean <image-name>  note The SDK is based on Synaptics' Astra SDK which is implemented for their Astra Machina Series. The Sentinel series uses the same SOC (SL1680) as Synaptics with some modifications. So, we will have to use Synaptics' SDK for full functionalities. For this, you must accept the End User License Agreement of Synaptics while setting up the environment to build the yocto image.

searchDocs.title: Adding Distro features​
searchDocs.content: Sentinel Yocto SDK supports optional distribution features which can be enabled either in <build-dir>/conf/local.conffile or by passing variables to the setup-environment script.

searchDocs.title: X11 Display server​
searchDocs.content: In Sentinel SDK, Wayland is the default display server. You can set the display server to X11 by passing DISPLAY_SERVERvariable to the setup-environment script.  MACHINE=sentinel-som-sl1680-mk1-rfb-mk1 DISPLAY_SERVER=x11 source meta-dctk-sentinel/setup/setup-environment

searchDocs.title: Virtualization for OOBE​
searchDocs.content: Virtualization feature is added to enable the support for virtual machines and containers. To enable virtualization and OOBE support, you need to pass the OOBE variable to the setup-environment script.  MACHINE=sentinel-som-sl1680-mk1-rfb-mk1 OOBE=enabled source meta-dctk-sentinel/setup/setup-environment

searchDocs.title: Image selection​
searchDocs.content: The user will have to select the class of images he/she is going to use before building an image. The IMAGE_CLASS variable is used to specify the class of images while setting up the environment.  For example, the below command allow users to build the images that belong to the sentinel image class.  MACHINE=sentinel-som-sl1680-mk1-rfb-mk1 OOBE=enabled IMAGE_CLASS=sentinel source meta-dctk-sentinel/setup/setup-environment  note If the user is not providing the IMAGE_CLASS variable, then yocto by default selects the sentinel class.  The following are the image classes into which the images are packed :  Image Class	Imagessentinel	sentinel-media-oobe, sentinel-media

searchDocs.title: Overview​
searchDocs.content: This application creates a GStreamer pipeline with an input-selector element that enables seamless switching between two video sources (USB cameras or test patterns) during runtime. Both sources run continuously, and switching between them is instantaneous without pipeline teardown.

searchDocs.title: Features​
searchDocs.content: Dual Source Support: Switch between two video sources in real-timeFlexible Input: Supports USB cameras (/dev/videoX) and GStreamer test patterns (test0, test1, etc.)Mixed Resolution Support: Handles sources with different resolutions (e.g., 1280x720 and 640x480)Mixed Format Support: Handles sources with different pixel formats (e.g., I420, BGRA, YUYV)Input-Selector Architecture: Both sources run continuously; switching is instant via pad selectionWayland Display: Fullscreen output using waylandsink with automatic scalingCPU Optimized: Minimal pipeline elements for maximum efficiencyUser-Friendly: Simple keyboard controls ('1', '2', 'q')Yocto SDK Compatible: Cross-compilation ready

searchDocs.title: Optimized Pipeline Design​
searchDocs.content: The application uses a CPU-optimized pipeline with minimal elements:  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Video Switcher Pipeline │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ Source 1 (v4l2src/videotestsrc) │ │ Any resolution/format │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ Source 2 (v4l2src/videotestsrc) │ │ │ │ Any resolution/format │ │ │ │ │ │ │ └──────────────> input-selector <──────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ │ │ Active source passes through │ │ ▼ │ │ videoconvert ──────> waylandsink │ │ (format conversion) (auto-scale fullscreen) │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

searchDocs.title: Native Build​
searchDocs.content: make

searchDocs.title: Cross-Compilation with Yocto SDK​
searchDocs.content: source /path/to/environment-setup-<arch> make   The Makefile is Yocto SDK compatible and will automatically use the SDK toolchain when sourced.

searchDocs.title: Basic Usage​
searchDocs.content: ./vswitch [source1] [source2]

searchDocs.title: Examples​
searchDocs.content: Two USB Cameras:  ./vswitch /dev/video0 /dev/video2   Two Test Patterns:  ./vswitch test0 test1   Mixed (USB Camera + Test Pattern):  ./vswitch /dev/video3 test0

searchDocs.title: Test Pattern Options​
searchDocs.content: Test patterns are specified as testN where N is the pattern number:  test0: SMPTE color barstest1: Snow (random)test2: Blacktest3: Whitetest4: Redtest5: Greentest6: Blue... (additional patterns available in videotestsrc)

searchDocs.title: Controls​
searchDocs.content: While the application is running:  1: Switch to Source 12: Switch to Source 2q or Q: Quit application

searchDocs.title: Configuration​
searchDocs.content: The application automatically scales all input to fullscreen using waylandsink. No manual resolution configuration is needed.

searchDocs.title: Handling Different Input Resolutions​
searchDocs.content: The pipeline automatically handles sources with different resolutions and pixel formats:  Example: Mixed resolutions  Source 1: 1280x720 @ I420 formatSource 2: 640x480 @ BGRA formatOutput: Automatically scaled to display's native resolution in fullscreen  The single videoconvert element after the input-selector dynamically handles all format conversions.

searchDocs.title: Pipeline Elements​
searchDocs.content: v4l2src: Video4Linux2 source for USB camerasvideotestsrc: Generate test patternsinput-selector: Select active input pad (the core switching element)videoconvert: Format conversion (single instance handles all sources)waylandsink: Display output on Wayland compositor with automatic scaling

searchDocs.title: Switching Mechanism​
searchDocs.content: The application uses GStreamer's input-selector element for switching:  Both video sources run continuously in the pipelineEach source connects directly to a different sink pad of the input-selectorSwitching changes the active-pad property of the selectorThe single videoconvert after the selector dynamically adapts to the active source's format

searchDocs.title: Dependencies​
searchDocs.content: GStreamer 1.0GStreamer plugins: gst-plugins-base (videoconvert, videotestsrc)gst-plugins-good (v4l2src)gst-plugins-bad (waylandsink, input-selector) pthread library

searchDocs.title: Wayland display issues​
searchDocs.content: If the test is being run on Sentinel platform, then you will have to issue the following commands.  Ensure XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and WAYLAND_DISPLAY are set: export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/var/run/user/0 export WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1

searchDocs.title: Implementations​
searchDocs.content: This application provides two implementations:  vswitch - Element-based pipeline construction Source: vswitch.cppCreates GStreamer elements programmatically using gst_element_factory_make()Full control over element properties and pad connections vswitch_string - String-based pipeline construction Source: vswitch_string.cppUses gst_parse_launch() to create pipeline from string descriptionRetrieves elements by name using gst_bin_get_by_name()More concise pipeline definition  Both implementations provide identical functionality and switching behavior.

searchDocs.title: API Function Summary​
searchDocs.content: Function	Purpose	Related Propertyapi_dctobd_init()	Initialize element from pipeline	- api_dctobd_set_model()	Set model file path	model api_dctobd_set_model_directory()	Set model directory	model-directory api_dctobd_get_available_models()	Get available models	available-models api_dctobd_set_mode()	Set detection mode	mode api_dctobd_set_confidence_threshold()	Set confidence threshold	threshold api_dctobd_set_max_detections()	Set max detections per frame	numinference api_dctobd_set_frame_interval()	Set frame processing interval	frameinterval api_dctobd_set_inference_statistics()	Enable/disable statistics	inferstatistics api_dctobd_set_detection_enabled()	Enable/disable detection	detection-enabled api_dctobd_set_enabled_classes()	Set enabled class names	enabled-classes api_dctobd_get_available_classes()	Get available class names	available-classes api_dctobd_get_model()	Get current model path	model api_dctobd_get_confidence_threshold()	Get current threshold	threshold api_dctobd_get_max_detections()	Get max detections setting	numinference api_dctobd_get_detection_enabled()	Get detection enabled state	detection-enabled

searchDocs.title: Usage Flow​
searchDocs.content: To use the plugin library you will need to follow the below sequence of operations.

searchDocs.title: Step 1: Pipeline Initialization​
searchDocs.content: Initialize a gstreamer pipeline with this plugin.  #include <apidctobd.h> GstElement *pipeline, *dctobd; // Initialize gst_init(&argc, &argv); pipeline = gst_parse_launch("v4l2src ! videoconvert ! ... ! dctobd name=detector ! ...", NULL);   note The plugin must have a name associated with it, which we will use to initialize the plugin api layer.

searchDocs.title: Step 2: Plugin Initialization​
searchDocs.content: Once the pipeline is initialized successfully, call the plugin initialization function to get the plugin element object.  With APIGST API // Initialize dctobd =api_dctobd_init(pipeline, "detector");

searchDocs.title: Step 3: Plugin Configuration​
searchDocs.content: Once the initialization is done, you can use the apis as needed.  With APIGST API // Configure api_dctobd_set_model(dctobd, "/usr/share/synap/models/yolov8s-640x384/model.synap"); api_dctobd_set_mode(dctobd, DCTOBD_MODE_DETECTOR); api_dctobd_set_output_mode(dctobd, OBD_OUTPUT_JSON); api_dctobd_set_confidence_threshold(dctobd, 0.7f); api_dctobd_set_enabled_classes(dctobd, "person,car"); // Optionally set label file (use GStreamer API for properties not in API layer) g_object_set(dctobd, "label", "/path/to/labels.json", NULL); // Start pipeline gst_element_set_state(pipeline, GST_STATE_PLAYING);

searchDocs.title: Dctobd Mode API​
searchDocs.content: Defines the detection mode for the dctobd element.  typedef enum { DCTOBD_MODE_DETECTOR = 0 // Detector mode for object detection } DctobdModeAPI;   Value	DescriptionDCTOBD_MODE_DETECTOR	Object detection mode

searchDocs.title: Functions​
searchDocs.content: These functions provide a C interface for controlling object detection from GStreamer pipelines.

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_init​
searchDocs.content: Initialize and retrieve the dctobd element from a GStreamer pipeline.  GstElement* api_dctobd_init(GstElement *pipeline, const char *element_name);   Parameters:  pipeline - GstElement pipeline containing the dctobd elementelement_name - Name of the dctobd element in the pipeline  Returns:  Pointer to dctobd element on successNULL on failure  Memory Management The caller is responsible for unreferencing the returned element using gst_object_unref() when done.  Example:  GstElement *pipeline = ...; // Your pipeline GstElement *dctobd = api_dctobd_init(pipeline, "detector"); if (dctobd) { // Use the dctobd element gst_object_unref(dctobd); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_model​
searchDocs.content: Set the model file path.  bool api_dctobd_set_model(GstElement *element, const char *model_path);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementmodel_path - Path to the model file (.synap file)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  note Model changes require pipeline restart to take effect.  Example:  api_dctobd_set_model(dctobd, "/usr/share/synap/models/yolov8s-640x384/model.synap");

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_model_directory​
searchDocs.content: Set the model directory for scanning.  bool api_dctobd_set_model_directory(GstElement *element, const char *directory);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementdirectory - Directory path to scan for models  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  api_dctobd_set_model_directory(dctobd, "/custom/models");

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_get_available_models​
searchDocs.content: Get the list of available model files in the configured directory.  char* api_dctobd_get_available_models(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElement  Returns:  Comma-separated list of model paths on success (caller must free())NULL on failure  Memory Management The caller must free() the returned string when done.  Example:  char *models = api_dctobd_get_available_models(dctobd); if (models) { printf("Available models: %s\n", models); free(models); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_mode​
searchDocs.content: Set the detection mode.  bool api_dctobd_set_mode(GstElement *element, DctobdModeAPI mode);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementmode - Detection mode (currently only DCTOBD_MODE_DETECTOR is supported)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  api_dctobd_set_mode(dctobd, DCTOBD_MODE_DETECTOR);

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_confidence_threshold​
searchDocs.content: Set the confidence threshold for detections.  bool api_dctobd_set_confidence_threshold(GstElement *element, float threshold);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementthreshold - Confidence threshold (0.0-1.0)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  // Set threshold to 0.7 (70% confidence) api_dctobd_set_confidence_threshold(dctobd, 0.7f);

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_max_detections​
searchDocs.content: Set the maximum number of detections per frame.  bool api_dctobd_set_max_detections(GstElement *element, int num_inference);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementnum_inference - Maximum number of detections per frame  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  api_dctobd_set_max_detections(dctobd, 10);

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_frame_interval​
searchDocs.content: Set the frame processing interval.  bool api_dctobd_set_frame_interval(GstElement *element, int interval);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementinterval - Process every Nth frame (0 = process all frames)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  // Process every 3rd frame api_dctobd_set_frame_interval(dctobd, 3);

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_inference_statistics​
searchDocs.content: Enable or disable inference statistics.  bool api_dctobd_set_inference_statistics(GstElement *element, bool enable);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementenable - true to enable statistics, false to disable  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  api_dctobd_set_inference_statistics(dctobd, true);

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_detection_enabled​
searchDocs.content: Enable or disable object detection.  bool api_dctobd_set_detection_enabled(GstElement *element, bool enable);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementenable - true to enable detection, false to disable  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  // Disable detection api_dctobd_set_detection_enabled(dctobd, false); // Enable detection api_dctobd_set_detection_enabled(dctobd, true);

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_enabled_classes​
searchDocs.content: Set the enabled class names for filtering.  bool api_dctobd_set_enabled_classes(GstElement *element, const char *classes);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementclasses - Comma-separated list of class names to enable  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  note If NULL or empty, all classes are enabled.  Example:  // Detect only persons and cars api_dctobd_set_enabled_classes(dctobd, "person,car"); // Enable all classes api_dctobd_set_enabled_classes(dctobd, NULL);

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_get_available_classes​
searchDocs.content: Get the available class names from the model.  char* api_dctobd_get_available_classes(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElement  Returns:  Comma-separated list of class names on success (caller must free())NULL on failure  Memory Management The caller must free() the returned string when done.  Example:  char *classes = api_dctobd_get_available_classes(dctobd); if (classes) { printf("Available classes: %s\n", classes); free(classes); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_get_model​
searchDocs.content: Get the current model path.  char* api_dctobd_get_model(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElement  Returns:  Current model path on success (caller must free())NULL on failure  Memory Management The caller must free() the returned string when done.  Example:  char *model = api_dctobd_get_model(dctobd); if (model) { printf("Current model: %s\n", model); free(model); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_get_confidence_threshold​
searchDocs.content: Get the current confidence threshold.  bool api_dctobd_get_confidence_threshold(GstElement *element, float *threshold);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementthreshold - Pointer to store the current threshold  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  float threshold; if (api_dctobd_get_confidence_threshold(dctobd, &threshold)) { printf("Current threshold: %.2f\n", threshold); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_get_max_detections​
searchDocs.content: Get the current maximum number of detections.  bool api_dctobd_get_max_detections(GstElement *element, int *num_inference);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementnum_inference - Pointer to store the current max detections  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  int max_detections; if (api_dctobd_get_max_detections(dctobd, &max_detections)) { printf("Max detections: %d\n", max_detections); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_get_detection_enabled​
searchDocs.content: Get whether detection is enabled.  bool api_dctobd_get_detection_enabled(GstElement *element, bool *enabled);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementenabled - Pointer to store the enabled state  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  bool enabled; if (api_dctobd_get_detection_enabled(dctobd, &enabled)) { printf("Detection enabled: %s\n", enabled ? "yes" : "no"); }

searchDocs.title: Usage Example​
searchDocs.content: Here's a complete example demonstrating the API usage:  #include "apidctobd.h" int main(int argc, char *argv[]) { GstElement *pipeline, *dctobd; // Initialize pipeline gst_init(&argc, &argv); pipeline = gst_parse_launch( "v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! videoscale ! " "video/x-raw,width=640,height=384,format=RGB ! " "dctobd name=detector ! " "dctobdsink location=/tmp/results.txt", NULL); // Get dctobd element dctobd = api_dctobd_init(pipeline, "detector"); if (!dctobd) { fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialize dctobd element\n"); return -1; } // Configure for person detection api_dctobd_set_model(dctobd, "/usr/share/synap/models/yolov8s-640x384/model.synap"); api_dctobd_set_mode(dctobd, DCTOBD_MODE_DETECTOR); api_dctobd_set_output_mode(dctobd, OBD_OUTPUT_JSON); api_dctobd_set_confidence_threshold(dctobd, 0.7f); api_dctobd_set_enabled_classes(dctobd, "person"); api_dctobd_set_frame_interval(dctobd, 3); // Start pipeline gst_element_set_state(pipeline, GST_STATE_PLAYING); // Run main loop... // Later: query available classes char *classes = api_dctobd_get_available_classes(dctobd); if (classes) { g_print("Available classes: %s\n", classes); free(classes); } // Switch to vehicle detection api_dctobd_set_enabled_classes(dctobd, "car,truck,bus,motorcycle"); api_dctobd_set_confidence_threshold(dctobd, 0.6f); // Cleanup gst_object_unref(dctobd); return 0; }

searchDocs.title: See Also​
searchDocs.content: GStreamer DocumentationPlugin PropertiesBuilding the Plugin

searchDocs.title: Overview​
searchDocs.content: The STT Plugin provides a GStreamer sink element (dctstt) that performs real-time speech-to-text conversion on audio streams. It accepts 16kHz mono PCM audio input, runs either Vosk or Whisper speech recognition models, and outputs recognition results through multiple communication backends.  dctstt (Speech-to-Text Sink Element)  The dctstt element is a sink element that terminates an audio pipeline. It accepts audio input, performs speech recognition using either Vosk (S16LE format) or Whisper (F32LE format), and outputs text results through TCP, MQTT, or console output.

searchDocs.title: Key Features​
searchDocs.content: Offline Speech Recognition - No internet connection required, all processing happens locallyDual Engine Support - Vosk for lightweight recognition or Whisper for higher accuracy (compile-time selection)Multiple Communication Backends - TCP JSON server, MQTT publishing, or console output (compile-time selection)Partial Results Support - Real-time streaming of partial recognition results during speech (Vosk only)Grammar Support - Can be configured with custom grammar for improved accuracy on specific vocabulary (Vosk)Voice Activity Detection - Built-in VAD for efficient processing (Whisper only)GStreamer Integration - Standard GStreamer element properties and bus messagesMulti-language Support - Support for multiple languages through different models

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.content: The STT plugin follows a three-layer architecture for modularity and maintainability:

searchDocs.title: 1. GStreamer Layer (gstdctstt.cpp)​
searchDocs.content: Handles GStreamer plugin implementation:  Pipeline integration and audio buffer processingProperty management (model path, communication settings, engine-specific options)Bus message posting for recognition resultsSink pad for receiving audio data

searchDocs.title: 2. Speech Recognition Engine Layer​
searchDocs.content: Two engines are available (compile-time selection):  Vosk Integration:  Vosk API - Lightweight offline speech recognitionSupports S16LE audio format (16-bit PCM)Model loading from directory structureReal-time partial results supportJSON result parsing  Whisper Integration:  Whisper.cpp - Higher accuracy offline speech recognitionSupports F32LE audio format (32-bit float PCM)Model loading from GGML binary filesBuilt-in Voice Activity Detection (VAD)Configurable processing parameters (threads, step-ms, length-ms)

searchDocs.title: 3. Communication Layer (com/)​
searchDocs.content: Platform-specific output implementation with three backends:  TCP (comm_tcp.cpp) - JSON server on configurable portMQTT (comm_mqtt.cpp) - Publish results to MQTT brokerPrintf (comm_printf.cpp) - Console output for debugging  info Both the speech recognition engine and communication backend are selected at compile-time using build options. Only one engine and one backend are compiled into the plugin at a time.

searchDocs.title: Using Vosk (S16LE format)​
searchDocs.content: gst-launch-1.0 alsasrc device=hw:1,0 ! \ audioconvert ! \ audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=S16LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15

searchDocs.title: Using Whisper (F32LE format)​
searchDocs.content: gst-launch-1.0 alsasrc device=hw:1,0 ! \ audioconvert ! \ audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=F32LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/whisper/ggml-tiny.en-q5_1.bin   note Audio Format Requirements: Vosk: S16LE (16-bit signed PCM), 1 channel, 16000 HzWhisper: F32LE (32-bit float PCM), 1 channel, 16000 Hz Use audioconvert and audioresample to convert from other formats.

searchDocs.title: Vosk Engine​
searchDocs.content: Audio Format: S16LE (16-bit signed little-endian PCM)Sample Rate: 16000 HzChannels: 1 (mono)Layout: Interleaved

searchDocs.title: Whisper Engine​
searchDocs.content: Audio Format: F32LE (32-bit float little-endian PCM)Sample Rate: 16000 HzChannels: 1 (mono)Layout: Interleaved  tip Use audioconvert and audioresample to convert stereo or different format audio to the required format for your chosen engine.

searchDocs.title: Requirements​
searchDocs.content: To use the STT Plugin, you will need the following dependencies installed on Sentinel SoM:

searchDocs.title: Runtime Dependencies​
searchDocs.content: GStreamer 1.0 runtime librariesALSA libraries (for audio capture)  For Vosk Engine:  Vosk library (libvosk.so) version 0.3.45 or compatiblePre-trained Vosk speech recognition model (directory structure)  For Whisper Engine:  Whisper.cpp libraryPre-trained Whisper model in GGML format (.bin file)

searchDocs.title: Communication Backend Dependencies​
searchDocs.content: Depending on the compiled backend:  TCP Backend: No additional dependenciesMQTT Backend: libmosquitto (MQTT client library)Printf Backend: No additional dependencies

searchDocs.title: Speech Recognition Models​
searchDocs.content: Vosk Models:  Installed Location: /home/root/models/stt/vosk/Small Model: vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 (~40MB)Large Model: vosk-model-en-us-0.22-lgraph (~128MB)Other Languages: Available at https://alphacephei.com/vosk/modelsModel directory structure: /home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15/ ├── am/ ├── conf/ ├── graph/ ├── ivector/ └── README   Whisper Models:  Installed Location: /home/root/models/stt/whisper/Default Model: ggml-tiny.en-q5_1.bin (Tiny model, quantized)Available Sizes: tiny, base, small, medium, largeDownload from Whisper.cpp repository or Hugging Face

searchDocs.title: TCP Backend​
searchDocs.content: Runs a JSON server that clients can connect to and receive recognition results in real-time.  # VOSK with TCP backend gst-launch-1.0 alsasrc device=hw:1,0 ! audioconvert ! audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=S16LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 tcp-port=9999 # WHISPER with TCP backend gst-launch-1.0 alsasrc device=hw:1,0 ! audioconvert ! audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=F32LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/whisper/ggml-tiny.en-q5_1.bin tcp-port=9999 # Connect to receive results nc localhost 9999

searchDocs.title: MQTT Backend​
searchDocs.content: Publishes recognition results to an MQTT topic for distributed processing.  # VOSK with MQTT backend gst-launch-1.0 alsasrc device=hw:1,0 ! audioconvert ! audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=S16LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 \ mqtt-broker=localhost \ mqtt-topic=stt/vosk # WHISPER with MQTT backend gst-launch-1.0 alsasrc device=hw:1,0 ! audioconvert ! audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=F32LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/whisper/ggml-tiny.en-q5_1.bin \ mqtt-broker=localhost \ mqtt-topic=stt/whisper # Subscribe to results mosquitto_sub -h localhost -t stt/vosk

searchDocs.title: Printf Backend​
searchDocs.content: Outputs recognition results to console/stdout for debugging.  # VOSK with Printf backend gst-launch-1.0 alsasrc device=hw:1,0 ! audioconvert ! audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=S16LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 # WHISPER with Printf backend gst-launch-1.0 alsasrc device=hw:1,0 ! audioconvert ! audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=F32LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/whisper/ggml-tiny.en-q5_1.bin

searchDocs.title: Output Format​
searchDocs.content: Recognition results are provided in JSON format:  Final Result:  { "text": "hello world" }   Partial Result:  { "partial": "hello wo" }

searchDocs.title: Bus Messages​
searchDocs.content: The plugin posts GStreamer bus messages for integration with applications:  Message Name: stt-final  Structure Fields:  text (string): The recognized textjson (string): Complete JSON result from the speech recognition engine  Example (C):  GstBus *bus = gst_element_get_bus(pipeline); GstMessage *msg = gst_bus_timed_pop_filtered(bus, GST_CLOCK_TIME_NONE, GST_MESSAGE_ELEMENT); if (msg && gst_message_has_name(msg, "stt-final")) { const GstStructure *s = gst_message_get_structure(msg); const gchar *text = gst_structure_get_string(s, "text"); g_print("Recognized: %s\n", text); }

searchDocs.title: Property Summary Table​
searchDocs.content: Property	Type	Range/Values	Default	Descriptiontrack-thresh	float	0.0 - 1.0	0.5	Minimum confidence to start tracking high-thresh	float	0.0 - 1.0	0.6	High confidence threshold for first association match-thresh	float	0.0 - 1.0	0.8	IoU threshold for matching track-buffer	int	1 - 1000	30	Frames to keep lost tracks frame-rate	int	1 - 240	30	Expected video frame rate (fps) output	string	none/text/mqtt/both	text	Output mode output-format	string	tracking/detection	tracking	Output JSON format mqtt-broker	string	any	localhost	MQTT broker address mqtt-port	int	1 - 65535	1883	MQTT broker port mqtt-topic	string	any	tracking/results	MQTT publish topic track-statistics	boolean	true/false	false	Enable statistics logging

searchDocs.title: track-thresh​
searchDocs.content: Description: Minimum confidence threshold for starting a new track.  Type: floatRange: 0.0 - 1.0Default: 0.5  Detections with confidence below this threshold will not be used to initialize new tracks. However, they may still be used to update existing tracks (see high-thresh).  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack track-thresh=0.6 ! ...

searchDocs.title: high-thresh​
searchDocs.content: Description: High confidence threshold for first-stage association.  Type: floatRange: 0.0 - 1.0Default: 0.6  In the ByteTrack algorithm, detections are separated into high and low confidence. High-confidence detections (above this threshold) are matched first to existing tracks. Low-confidence detections are then used to recover lost tracks.  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack high-thresh=0.7 ! ...

searchDocs.title: match-thresh​
searchDocs.content: Description: IoU (Intersection over Union) threshold for matching detections to tracks.  Type: floatRange: 0.0 - 1.0Default: 0.8  When a detection and a predicted track position have an IoU above this threshold, they are considered as a potential match. Higher values require more overlap for matching.  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack match-thresh=0.75 ! ...

searchDocs.title: track-buffer​
searchDocs.content: Description: Number of frames to keep lost tracks before removing them permanently.  Type: intRange: 1 - 1000Default: 30  When a track is not matched to any detection, it enters the "Lost" state. If it remains unmatched for more frames than this buffer size, it will be permanently removed. Increase this value for scenarios with frequent occlusions.  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack track-buffer=50 ! ...

searchDocs.title: frame-rate​
searchDocs.content: Description: Expected frame rate of the video source in frames per second (fps).  Type: intRange: 1 - 240Default: 30  This value is used by the Kalman filter for motion prediction. Set it to match your actual video frame rate for accurate prediction.  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack frame-rate=60 ! ...

searchDocs.title: output​
searchDocs.content: Description: Output mode for tracking results.  Type: stringValid Values: "none", "text", "mqtt", "both"Default: "text"  none: Silent mode, no output generatedtext: JSON output to stdout (human-readable)mqtt: Publish results to MQTT brokerboth: Text + MQTT simultaneously  gst-launchC APIGObject Property # Text output gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output=text ! ... # MQTT output gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output=mqtt ! ... # Both outputs gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output=both ! ... # No output (silent) gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output=none ! ...

searchDocs.title: output-format​
searchDocs.content: Description: Format of the output JSON structure.  Type: stringValid Values: "tracking", "detection"Default: "tracking"  tracking: Separate tracks array with track_id, state, and detection info {"timestamp": X, "tracks": [{track_id, class, confidence, bbox, state}, ...]} detection: Detection format with track_id merged into each detection {"timestamp": X, "detections": [{class, confidence, bbox, track_id}, ...]}   gst-launchC APIGObject Property # Tracking format gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output-format=tracking ! ... # Detection format gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output-format=detection ! ...

searchDocs.title: MQTT Configuration​
searchDocs.content: These properties are only relevant when output is set to "mqtt" or "both".

searchDocs.title: mqtt-broker​
searchDocs.content: Description: MQTT broker hostname or IP address.  Type: stringDefault: "localhost"  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output=mqtt mqtt-broker=192.168.1.100 ! ...

searchDocs.title: mqtt-port​
searchDocs.content: Description: MQTT broker port number.  Type: intRange: 1 - 65535Default: 1883  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output=mqtt mqtt-port=8883 ! ...

searchDocs.title: mqtt-topic​
searchDocs.content: Description: MQTT topic to publish tracking results.  Type: stringDefault: "tracking/results"  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output=mqtt mqtt-topic=camera1/tracking ! ...

searchDocs.title: track-statistics​
searchDocs.content: Description: Enable detailed tracking statistics logging.  Type: booleanDefault: false  When enabled, the plugin logs detailed statistics about track states, counts, and processing metrics to the console.  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack track-statistics=true ! ...

searchDocs.title: Querying Properties at Runtime​
searchDocs.content: You can inspect current property values using gst-inspect-1.0:  # List all properties gst-inspect-1.0 dctotrack # Query specific property via pipeline gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack name=tracker ! ... & # Then use gst-launch-1.0 with --gst-debug to see property values   Using C API:  float track_thresh; api_dctotrack_get_track_thresh(element, &track_thresh); printf("Current track-thresh: %.2f\n", track_thresh);   Using GObject:  gfloat track_thresh; g_object_get(G_OBJECT(element), "track-thresh", &track_thresh, NULL); g_print("Current track-thresh: %.2f\n", track_thresh);

searchDocs.title: Tips for Tuning​
searchDocs.content: track-thresh vs high-thresh: Keep high-thresh ≥ track-threshLarger gap allows more recovery of lost tracks from low-confidence detections match-thresh: Lower values (0.6-0.7): Better for fast-moving objects with imperfect detectionHigher values (0.8-0.9): Better for static/slow scenes with accurate detection track-buffer: Short buffer (10-20): Fast removal of disappeared objectsLong buffer (50-100): Better recovery from occlusions frame-rate: Always match your actual video FPS for accurate motion predictionIncorrect value leads to poor prediction and ID switches output modes: Use none when tracking data is consumed internally (metadata passing)Use mqtt for multi-system integration and real-time monitoringUse both during development/debugging

searchDocs.title: Features​
searchDocs.content: Offline Speech Recognition: No internet connection required, all processing happens locally using VoskWake Word Detection: Trigger phrase ("Mantis") activation for command listeningFuzzy Matching: Tolerant command matching using Levenshtein distance algorithmMultiple Communication Backends: Send commands via TCP, MQTT, or console outputConfigurable Commands: JSON-based command definitions with multiple phrase variantsGrammar Support: Custom keyword grammar for improved recognition accuracyHot Reload: Reload command definitions without restarting (SIGUSR2)Low Latency: Real-time audio processing with ALSA integrationResource Efficient: Suitable for embedded ARM64 systems

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.content: The application follows a multi-threaded architecture with two main components:

searchDocs.title: 1. ALSA Capture Thread​
searchDocs.content: Captures audio from microphone at 16kHz stereoConverts stereo to monoBuffers audio in thread-safe queueHandles PCM underruns and errors

searchDocs.title: 2. Vosk Processing Thread​
searchDocs.content: Consumes audio from queuePerforms speech recognition using Vosk modelDetects trigger phrase ("Mantis")Matches commands using fuzzy logicSends commands via TCP socket

searchDocs.title: Communication Flow​
searchDocs.content: ┌─────────────┐ │ Microphone │ └──────┬──────┘ │ ALSA Capture (16kHz Stereo) ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Audio Queue │ (Thread-safe) └──────┬──────────┘ │ Mono PCM ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Vosk Engine │ └──────┬──────────┘ │ JSON Results ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Trigger Monitor │ (5-second window) └──────┬──────────┘ │ Wake word detected ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Command Matcher │ (Fuzzy matching) └──────┬──────────┘ │ Matched command ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ TCP Client │ → Send to device (localhost:6975) └─────────────────┘

searchDocs.title: commands.json​

searchDocs.title: Voice Command Workflow​
searchDocs.content: Start Application ./voice_command # Output: VOICE COMMAND SYSTEM RUNNING Say Wake Word You: "Mantis" App: *** MANTIS DETECTED - 5s WINDOW ACTIVE *** Give Command (within 5 seconds) You: "Zoom in" App: [MATCH] ✓ Exact: "zoom in" App: [COMMAND] ✓ Sending: zoom_in App: [COMMAND] ✓ Success Window Expires (if no command given) App: *** WINDOW EXPIRED ***

searchDocs.title: Example Session​

searchDocs.title: Hot Reload Commands​
searchDocs.content: Reload command definitions without restarting:  # Get PID cat /tmp/voice_command.pid # Send reload signal kill -USR2 $(cat /tmp/voice_command.pid) # Or directly killall -USR2 voice_command   The application will reload commands.json and keywords.txt and rebuild the grammar.

searchDocs.title: Command Matching Algorithm​
searchDocs.content: The application uses a two-stage matching process:

searchDocs.title: Stage 1: Exact Match​
searchDocs.content: Normalize input (lowercase, trim)Remove filler words ("the", "a", "please", etc.)Compare with all command phrasesReturn match if found

searchDocs.title: Stage 2: Fuzzy Match (Levenshtein Distance)​
searchDocs.content: Calculate edit distance for all phrasesAllow up to 20% differenceReturn best match within tolerance  Example:  Input: "zom in pleas" Normalized: "zom in" Best Match: "zoom in" (distance: 1) Threshold: 20% of 7 chars = 1.4 Result: MATCH ✓

searchDocs.title: Command Server Implementation​
searchDocs.content:
The voice command app sends commands to localhost:6975 by default. Implement a TCP server in your application to receive commands:  Python Example:  import socket import threading def command_handler(conn, addr): print(f"Connection from {addr}") while True: data = conn.recv(1024) if not data: break command = data.decode('utf-8').strip() print(f"Received command: {command}") # Process command if command == "zoom_in": print("Executing: Zoom In") elif command == "zoom_out": print("Executing: Zoom Out") elif command == "set_mode_black_hot": print("Executing: Black Hot Mode") elif command == "set_mode_white_hot": print("Executing: White Hot Mode") conn.close() # Start server server = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) server.bind(('127.0.0.1', 6975)) server.listen(5) print("Command server listening on port 6975") while True: conn, addr = server.accept() threading.Thread(target=command_handler, args=(conn, addr)).start()   C Example:  #include <sys/socket.h> #include <netinet/in.h> #include <stdio.h> #include <string.h> #include <unistd.h> int start_command_server(int port) { int server_fd, client_fd; struct sockaddr_in addr; char buffer[256]; server_fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0); addr.sin_family = AF_INET; addr.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY; addr.sin_port = htons(port); bind(server_fd, (struct sockaddr*)&addr, sizeof(addr)); listen(server_fd, 5); printf("Command server listening on port %d
", port); while (1) { client_fd = accept(server_fd, NULL, NULL); ssize_t n = recv(client_fd, buffer, sizeof(buffer)-1, 0); if (n > 0) { buffer[n] = '\0'; printf("Received command: %s
", buffer); // Process command if (strcmp(buffer, "zoom_in
") == 0) { // Execute zoom in } else if (strcmp(buffer, "zoom_out
") == 0) { // Execute zoom out } } close(client_fd); } return 0; }

searchDocs.title: Systemd Service​
searchDocs.content: Create /etc/systemd/system/voice-command.service:  [Unit] Description=Voice Command Service After=network.target sound.target [Service] Type=simple User=root WorkingDirectory=/usr/share/sentinel-sdk/voice_command ExecStart=/usr/share/sentinel-sdk/voice_command/voice_command \ --vosk-model /home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 \ --device default \ --command-host 127.0.0.1 \ --command-port 6975 Restart=on-failure RestartSec=5 [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target   Enable and start:  sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl enable voice-command sudo systemctl start voice-command sudo systemctl status voice-command

searchDocs.title: Auto-Start on Boot​

searchDocs.title: Required Pipeline Elements​
searchDocs.content: For proper operation, your pipeline should include:  videoconvert - Converts any video format (YUV, NV12, BGRA, etc.) to RGBvideoscale - Resizes video to match model's expected resolutionCaps filter - Explicitly specify video/x-raw,format=RGB,width=W,height=H  Example pipeline structure:  [source] ! videoconvert ! videoscale ! \ video/x-raw,format=RGB,width=640,height=384 ! \ dctobd model=/path/to/model.synap mode=detector ! \ [sink]

searchDocs.title: Basic Detection​
searchDocs.content: To run object detection with default settings, execute the following pipeline:  gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! videoscale ! \ video/x-raw,width=640,height=384,format=RGB ! \ dctobd model=/usr/share/synap/models/object_detection/coco/model/yolov8s-640x384/model.synap \ mode=detector frameinterval=3 ! \ dctobdsink location=results.txt   This pipeline captures video from /dev/video8, converts it to RGB format, and runs object detection. Results are written to results.txt in JSON format.

searchDocs.title: Class-Specific Detection​
searchDocs.content: To detect only specific object classes, use the enabled-classes property:  gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! videoscale ! \ video/x-raw,width=640,height=384,format=RGB ! \ dctobd model=/usr/share/synap/models/object_detection/coco/model/yolov8s-640x384/model.synap \ mode=detector enabled-classes="person,car,bicycle" frameinterval=3 ! \ dctobdsink location=results.txt   This configuration will only detect persons, cars, and bicycles, ignoring all other object classes.

searchDocs.title: Adjusting Detection Threshold​
searchDocs.content: To use a higher confidence threshold for more accurate detections, set the threshold property:  gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! videoscale ! \ video/x-raw,width=640,height=384,format=RGB ! \ dctobd model=/usr/share/synap/models/object_detection/coco/model/yolov8s-640x384/model.synap \ mode=detector threshold=0.75 frameinterval=3 ! \ dctobdsink location=results.txt   A threshold of 0.75 means only detections with 75% or higher confidence will be reported.

searchDocs.title: Application Examples​
searchDocs.content: The following examples demonstrate how to use the Object Detection plugin in C applications.

searchDocs.title: Configuring Detection at Runtime​
searchDocs.content: GstElement *dctobd = gst_element_factory_make("dctobd", "detector"); // Set the model path g_object_set(dctobd, "model", "/usr/share/synap/models/object_detection/coco/model/yolov8s-640x384/model.synap", NULL); // Configure detection parameters g_object_set(dctobd, "mode", "detector", NULL); g_object_set(dctobd, "enabled-classes", "person,car", NULL); g_object_set(dctobd, "threshold", 0.7f, NULL);

searchDocs.title: Querying Available Classes​
searchDocs.content: // After the model is loaded, query available classes gchar *available_classes = NULL; g_object_get(dctobd, "available-classes", &available_classes, NULL); g_print("Available classes: %s\n", available_classes); g_free(available_classes);

searchDocs.title: Person Detection​
searchDocs.content: This configuration optimizes for detecting people with high confidence:  gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! videoscale ! \ video/x-raw,width=640,height=384,format=RGB ! \ dctobd model=/usr/share/synap/models/object_detection/coco/model/yolov8s-640x384/model.synap \ mode=detector enabled-classes="person" threshold=0.7 frameinterval=3 ! \ dctobdsink location=person_detection.txt

searchDocs.title: Vehicle Detection​
searchDocs.content: This configuration detects multiple vehicle types:  gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! videoscale ! \ video/x-raw,width=640,height=384,format=RGB ! \ dctobd model=/usr/share/synap/models/object_detection/coco/model/yolov8s-640x384/model.synap \ mode=detector enabled-classes="car,truck,bus,motorcycle" threshold=0.6 frameinterval=5 ! \ dctobdsink location=vehicle_detection.txt   note Adjust the frameinterval parameter based on your performance requirements. Higher values reduce CPU usage but may miss rapid changes in the scene.

searchDocs.content: gst-launch-1.0 filesrc location=video.mp4 ! decodebin ! \ videoconvert ! videoscale ! \ video/x-raw,format=RGB,width=640,height=384 ! \ dctobd model=/usr/share/synap/models/object_detection/coco/model/yolov8s-640x384/model.synap \ mode=detector frameinterval=3 ! \ fakesink

searchDocs.title: Enable Debug Logging​
searchDocs.content: To see detailed plugin logs, set the GST_DEBUG environment variable:  # Show only DCTOBD plugin debug messages (recommended) GST_DEBUG=dctobd:4,dctobdsink:4 gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! videoscale ! \ video/x-raw,width=640,height=384,format=RGB ! \ dctobd model=/usr/share/synap/models/object_detection/coco/model/yolov8s-640x384/model.synap \ mode=detector frameinterval=3 ! \ dctobdsink location=/tmp/results.txt # Show all GStreamer debug messages (very verbose) GST_DEBUG=*:3 gst-launch-1.0 ...   Debug levels:  0: No output1: ERROR2: WARNING3: INFO4: DEBUG5: LOG (verbose)

searchDocs.title: Enable Inference Statistics​
searchDocs.content: Monitor inference performance:  gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! videoscale ! \ video/x-raw,width=640,height=384,format=RGB ! \ dctobd model=/usr/share/synap/models/object_detection/coco/model/yolov8s-640x384/model.synap \ mode=detector inferstatistics=true frameinterval=3 ! \ dctobdsink location=results.txt   This will log average inference time when the pipeline stops.

searchDocs.title: Dynamic Property Changes​
searchDocs.content: You can change detection parameters at runtime using GStreamer's property system:  GstElement *dctobd = gst_element_factory_make("dctobd", "detector"); // Start with person detection g_object_set(dctobd, "enabled-classes", "person", NULL); g_object_set(dctobd, "threshold", 0.7f, NULL); // Run pipeline... gst_element_set_state(pipeline, GST_STATE_PLAYING); // Later, switch to vehicle detection g_object_set(dctobd, "enabled-classes", "car,truck,bus,motorcycle", NULL); g_object_set(dctobd, "threshold", 0.6f, NULL); // Temporarily disable detection g_object_set(dctobd, "detection-enabled", FALSE, NULL); // Re-enable with new settings g_object_set(dctobd, "detection-enabled", TRUE, NULL); g_object_set(dctobd, "threshold", 0.8f, NULL);

searchDocs.title: Issue: "Unsupported video format" Error​
searchDocs.content: Cause: The plugin only accepts RGB format input.  Solution: Add videoconvert before the dctobd element:  ... ! videoconvert ! video/x-raw,format=RGB ! dctobd...

searchDocs.title: Issue: "Resolution mismatch" Error​
searchDocs.content: Cause: Video resolution doesn't match model's expected input.  Solution: Add videoscale and specify correct resolution:  ... ! videoscale ! video/x-raw,format=RGB,width=640,height=384 ! dctobd...

searchDocs.title: Issue: No Detections Appearing​
searchDocs.content: Possible Solutions:  Lower the threshold: threshold=0.3Check detection is enabled: detection-enabled=trueVerify enabled classes match scene objectsCheck frame interval isn't too highEnable debug logging to see format/resolution info

searchDocs.title: Issue: Class Filtering Not Working​
searchDocs.content: Possible Solutions:  Ensure label file exists (set via label property)Check class name spelling and case sensitivityQuery available classes first:  gchar *available = NULL; g_object_get(dctobd, "available-classes", &available, NULL); g_print("Available: %s\n", available); g_free(available);

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.content: The plugin library is organized into different layers.    GST Layer - The GST layer has the main Gstreamer related functionalities. However, the functional tasks which can be offloaded to different hardware is kept in the machine layer. Machine Layer - This is the layer where machine specific operations are implemented. This is done to port the plugin easily to different platforms. API Layer (Optional) - The API layer is a wrapper layer using which the user can configure the gstreamer plugin. This is not part of the gstreamer framework. Instead of the API layer, the user can use gstreamer's APIs directly too. Communication Layer (Optional) - This layer the communication of the plugin to the external world or other plugins. Currently only MQTT is supported.

searchDocs.title: Folder Structure​
searchDocs.content: The corresponding folder structure is as follows:  inc/ # Header files ├── gst/ # GStreamer layer (plugin interface) ├── mach/ # Machine layer (processing & conversion) ├── comm/ # Communication layer (data recv & transmit) └── api/ # API layer (C interface) src/ # Source files ├── gst/ # GStreamer implementation ├── mach/ # Machine implementations (generic, hw, etc.) ├── comm/ # Communication layer └── api/ # API implementation test/ # Test applications ├── gst/ # GStreamer-based tests ├── mqtt/ # Mqtt based tests. └── api/ # API-based tests

searchDocs.title: Features​
searchDocs.content: This gstreamer plugin has the following features/functionalities:  Different Capture Modes: Manual Mode: The user can trigger a frame capture via setting a property or calling an API.Periodic Mode: The user can configure the plugin to capture the frames automatically at a specified time interval (1 to 3600 secs).Automatic Mode: The user can communicate to receive events from the external world and capture based on these events. Timestamp-based Filenames: The frames are saved in the following format <PREFIX>_YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.jpg. The <PREFIX> is user-configurable. With prefix: <PREFIX>_YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.jpgWithout prefix: YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.jpg Save Location: The user can configure the directory where the images needs to be saved.

searchDocs.title: Common Properties​
searchDocs.content: These properties are available for both Vosk and Whisper engines.

searchDocs.title: model​
searchDocs.content: Description: Path to the speech recognition model.  Type: stringDefault:  Vosk: "/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15"Whisper: "/home/root/models/stt/whisper/ggml-tiny.en-q5_1.bin"  For Vosk: Path to model directory containing am/, conf/, graph/, and ivector/ subdirectories.  For Whisper: Path to GGML model file (.bin format).  gst-launchGObject Property # Vosk gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 ! ... # Whisper gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/whisper/ggml-tiny.en-q5_1.bin ! ...   Available Models:  Vosk:  Small: /home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 (~40MB, faster)Large: /home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-en-us-0.22-lgraph (~1.8GB, more accurate)  Whisper:  Tiny: /home/root/models/stt/whisper/ggml-tiny.en-q5_1.bin (~75MB, fastest)Additional models can be installed from Whisper.cpp or Hugging Face

searchDocs.title: Vosk Engine Properties​
searchDocs.content: These properties are only available when using the Vosk engine (compile-time selection).

searchDocs.title: partials​
searchDocs.content: Description: Enable or disable partial recognition results during speech processing.  Type: booleanDefault: trueAvailability: Vosk engine only  When enabled, the plugin sends intermediate recognition results as speech is being processed. When disabled, only final results (on speech pause) are sent.  note This property is not available with the Whisper engine. Whisper only produces final results.  gst-launchGObject Property # Enable partial results (default) gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt partials=true ! ... # Disable partial results (only finals) gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt partials=false ! ...   Use Cases:  Enabled: Real-time transcription, live captions, voice command confirmationDisabled: Final transcription only, reduced output, simpler result handling

searchDocs.title: Whisper Engine Properties​
searchDocs.content: These properties are only available when using the Whisper engine (compile-time selection).

searchDocs.title: threads​
searchDocs.content: Description: Number of CPU threads to use for processing.  Type: intRange: 1 - 32Default: 4  Higher thread counts can improve performance on multi-core systems but increase CPU usage. Adjust based on your hardware and performance requirements.  gst-launchGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt threads=8 ! ...

searchDocs.title: step-ms​
searchDocs.content: Description: Step size in milliseconds for audio processing window.  Type: intRange: 100 - 10000 msDefault: 3000 ms  Controls how often Whisper processes audio chunks. Smaller values give more frequent updates but higher CPU usage. Larger values reduce CPU usage but increase latency.  gst-launchGObject Property # Process every 2 seconds gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt step-ms=2000 ! ... # Process every 5 seconds gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt step-ms=5000 ! ...

searchDocs.title: length-ms​
searchDocs.content: Description: Length of audio buffer in milliseconds.  Type: intRange: 1000 - 30000 msDefault: 10000 ms  Defines the size of the audio buffer for processing. Larger buffers provide more context for better accuracy but increase latency. Should be >= step-ms.  gst-launchGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt length-ms=8000 ! ...

searchDocs.title: use-vad​
searchDocs.content: Description: Enable Voice Activity Detection.  Type: booleanDefault: false  When enabled, Whisper only processes audio when speech is detected, reducing CPU usage during silence periods. Recommended for continuous streaming applications.  gst-launchGObject Property # Enable VAD gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt use-vad=true ! ...

searchDocs.title: vad-threshold​
searchDocs.content: Description: VAD sensitivity threshold.  Type: floatRange: 0.0 - 1.0Default: 0.01  Lower values make VAD more sensitive (detect quieter speech), higher values require louder speech to trigger. Only effective when use-vad=true.  gst-launchGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt use-vad=true vad-threshold=0.02 ! ...

searchDocs.title: TCP Backend Properties​
searchDocs.content: Available only when compiled with -Dcomm_backend=tcp.

searchDocs.title: tcp-port​
searchDocs.content: Description: TCP port number for the JSON server.  Type: intRange: 1 - 65535Default: 9999  The plugin starts a TCP server on this port that clients can connect to for receiving recognition results in real-time.  gst-launchGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt tcp-port=8888 ! ...   Connect to TCP Server:  nc localhost 9999 # or telnet localhost 9999   JSON Output Format:  // Vosk - Final result { "text": "hello world" } // Vosk - Partial result (if partials=true) { "partial": "hello wor" } // Whisper - Result { "text": "hello world" }
