searchDocs.title: Design​
searchDocs.content: The pipeline implemented by this application is shown below :    On the USB camera pipeline, a main pipeline will be running which will acquire the frames from USB camera and pass it to an encoder. The encoded frames from encoder element is passed to a shared memory sink.  These frames are then accessed by an RTSP shmsrc element via usbcam.socket (shared memory) and is streamed into the specific mount point in the port specified by the user.  This same implementation is recreated for MIPI camera pipeline.  note The main camera pipeline will run when the application starts (as per CAM macro definition). The RTSP pipeline is configured only when an RTSP client requests the video from the specified port at the specified mount point. Therefore, without a client, shmsrc will not be created to retrieve the buffer from the shared memory.  The user can configure the camera to be streamed by setting the CAM definition in the application's source code. The value of CAM can be set to 3 states :  Value	Description0	To enable MIPI camera implementation 1	To enable USB camera implementation Any other value	To enable both  note The application currently uses v4l2h264enc hardware encoder which is supported in sentinel board only. To test it generally in other platforms, replace v4l2h264enc element in pipeline with x264enc tune=zerolatency bitrate=2000. Keep in mind that the properties might differ between the two elements.

searchDocs.title: Implementation​
searchDocs.content: In order to obtain the executable of the sample application, you will have to initially setup the toolchain environment. Please refer to the toolchain section to do the setup.  After setting up the environment, go to the directory where the sample application is present and execute the below command :  ${CC} rtsp_sample.c -o rtsp_server `pkg-config --cflags --libs gstreamer-1.0 gstreamer-rtsp-server-1.0`   An executable file rtsp_server will be created. Copy this file into the Sentinel SoM and execute the command :  ./rtsp_server   While running the application, the currently used rtsp_url will be obtained in the terminal. To obtain the stream at the client side, run the below command on a host machine connected to the same network as that of the Sentinel SoM.  gst-launch-1.0 rtspsrc location=<rtsp_url> ! rtpjitterbuffer ! rtph264depay ! h264parse ! avdec_h264 ! videoconvert ! autovideosink sync=false   note Make sure the required gstreamer dependencies are installed on the host machine to facilitate the rtsp client execution.

searchDocs.title: Overview​
searchDocs.content: This application creates a GStreamer pipeline with an input-selector element that enables seamless switching between two video sources (USB cameras or test patterns) during runtime. Both sources run continuously, and switching between them is instantaneous without pipeline teardown.

searchDocs.title: Features​
searchDocs.content: Dual Source Support: Switch between two video sources in real-timeFlexible Input: Supports USB cameras (/dev/videoX) and GStreamer test patterns (test0, test1, etc.)Mixed Resolution Support: Handles sources with different resolutions (e.g., 1280x720 and 640x480)Mixed Format Support: Handles sources with different pixel formats (e.g., I420, BGRA, YUYV)Input-Selector Architecture: Both sources run continuously; switching is instant via pad selectionWayland Display: Fullscreen output using waylandsink with automatic scalingCPU Optimized: Minimal pipeline elements for maximum efficiencyUser-Friendly: Simple keyboard controls ('1', '2', 'q')Yocto SDK Compatible: Cross-compilation ready

searchDocs.title: Optimized Pipeline Design​
searchDocs.content: The application uses a CPU-optimized pipeline with minimal elements:  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ Video Switcher Pipeline │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ Source 1 (v4l2src/videotestsrc) │ │ Any resolution/format │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ │ Source 2 (v4l2src/videotestsrc) │ │ │ │ Any resolution/format │ │ │ │ │ │ │ └──────────────> input-selector <──────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ │ │ Active source passes through │ │ ▼ │ │ videoconvert ──────> waylandsink │ │ (format conversion) (auto-scale fullscreen) │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

searchDocs.title: Native Build​
searchDocs.content: make

searchDocs.title: Cross-Compilation with Yocto SDK​
searchDocs.content: source /path/to/environment-setup-<arch> make   The Makefile is Yocto SDK compatible and will automatically use the SDK toolchain when sourced.

searchDocs.title: Basic Usage​
searchDocs.content: ./vswitch [source1] [source2]

searchDocs.title: Examples​
searchDocs.content: Two USB Cameras:  ./vswitch /dev/video0 /dev/video2   Two Test Patterns:  ./vswitch test0 test1   Mixed (USB Camera + Test Pattern):  ./vswitch /dev/video3 test0

searchDocs.title: Test Pattern Options​
searchDocs.content: Test patterns are specified as testN where N is the pattern number:  test0: SMPTE color barstest1: Snow (random)test2: Blacktest3: Whitetest4: Redtest5: Greentest6: Blue... (additional patterns available in videotestsrc)

searchDocs.title: Controls​
searchDocs.content: While the application is running:  1: Switch to Source 12: Switch to Source 2q or Q: Quit application

searchDocs.title: Configuration​
searchDocs.content: The application automatically scales all input to fullscreen using waylandsink. No manual resolution configuration is needed.

searchDocs.title: Handling Different Input Resolutions​
searchDocs.content: The pipeline automatically handles sources with different resolutions and pixel formats:  Example: Mixed resolutions  Source 1: 1280x720 @ I420 formatSource 2: 640x480 @ BGRA formatOutput: Automatically scaled to display's native resolution in fullscreen  The single videoconvert element after the input-selector dynamically handles all format conversions.

searchDocs.title: Pipeline Elements​
searchDocs.content: v4l2src: Video4Linux2 source for USB camerasvideotestsrc: Generate test patternsinput-selector: Select active input pad (the core switching element)videoconvert: Format conversion (single instance handles all sources)waylandsink: Display output on Wayland compositor with automatic scaling

searchDocs.title: Switching Mechanism​
searchDocs.content: The application uses GStreamer's input-selector element for switching:  Both video sources run continuously in the pipelineEach source connects directly to a different sink pad of the input-selectorSwitching changes the active-pad property of the selectorThe single videoconvert after the selector dynamically adapts to the active source's format

searchDocs.title: Dependencies​
searchDocs.content: GStreamer 1.0GStreamer plugins: gst-plugins-base (videoconvert, videotestsrc)gst-plugins-good (v4l2src)gst-plugins-bad (waylandsink, input-selector) pthread library

searchDocs.title: Wayland display issues​
searchDocs.content: If the test is being run on Sentinel platform, then you will have to issue the following commands.  Ensure XDG_RUNTIME_DIR and WAYLAND_DISPLAY are set: export XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/var/run/user/0 export WAYLAND_DISPLAY=wayland-1

searchDocs.title: Implementations​
searchDocs.content: This application provides two implementations:  vswitch - Element-based pipeline construction Source: vswitch.cppCreates GStreamer elements programmatically using gst_element_factory_make()Full control over element properties and pad connections vswitch_string - String-based pipeline construction Source: vswitch_string.cppUses gst_parse_launch() to create pipeline from string descriptionRetrieves elements by name using gst_bin_get_by_name()More concise pipeline definition  Both implementations provide identical functionality and switching behavior.

searchDocs.title: Features​
searchDocs.content: Dual Video Pipeline Management: Switch between two independent GStreamer video pipelines in real-timeRTSP Streaming Server: Stream video from multiple sources via RTSP protocolObject Tracking Integration: PID-based object tracking with MQTT communicationInteractive Controls: Runtime control via keyboard commandsFlexible Pipeline Configuration: Support for custom GStreamer pipelines from files or command-lineAutomatic Device Detection: Video device numbers are automatically extracted from pipeline filesAuto-Link Mode: Automatically synchronize PID tracking source with video source switchingShared Memory Transport: Uses shared memory sockets for efficient inter-process communication

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.content: The application consists of three main components:  MantisVideoSwitcher: Manages dual video pipelines with input-selector for seamless switchingRTSPServer: Provides RTSP streaming capability for video distributionObject Tracking Integration: PID controller for camera pan/tilt based on object detection (optional)

searchDocs.title: Prerequisites​
searchDocs.content: Build Dependencies Before building mantis_test_app, you must first build the PID Object Tracker library (pid_otrack). The application depends on libpid_otrack.so which needs to be compiled separately. Build order: Build pid_otrack library (see PID Object Tracker documentation)Build mantis_test_app For Yocto builds, the recipe handles this automatically. For standalone SDK builds, ensure the pid_otrack library is built in ../../sentinal_sdk/image/pid_otrack/build/ before running make. See the Toolchain Setup documentation for instructions on creating and installing the SDK toolchain. # Source the SDK environment source /path/to/sdk/environment-setup-<arch>-poky-linux # Then proceed with building cd apps/mantis_test_app make   Required Dependencies:  GStreamer 1.0 development libraries gstreamer-1.0gstreamer-rtsp-server-1.0 PID Object Tracker library (pid_otrack) - Must be built firstlibmosquitto (MQTT client library)libcjson (JSON parsing)C++11 compatible compilerpthread support

searchDocs.title: Before Running​
searchDocs.content: Required Setup Before running the application, complete the following setup steps: 1. Create required directories: mkdir -p /tmp/videos /tmp/images These directories are used by: dctvrecord plugin: Saves recorded video files to /tmp/videos/dctfcapture plugin: Saves captured frame images to /tmp/images/ 2. Configure MQTT Broker IP in Pipeline Files: The example pipeline files contain a default MQTT broker IP (169.254.1.222) in the dctotrack and dctoverlay GStreamer elements. You must update this to match your board's actual IP address for MQTT communication to work properly. # On target device - update all pipeline files sed -i 's/mqtt-broker=169.254.1.222/mqtt-broker=192.168.1.100/g' \ /usr/share/sentinel-sdk/mantis_test_app/*.txt # During development - update pipeline files sed -i 's/mqtt-broker=169.254.1.222/mqtt-broker=192.168.1.100/g' \ example_pipelines/*.txt Or manually edit the pipeline files and change: mqtt-broker=169.254.1.222 to your board's IP address, for example: mqtt-broker=192.168.1.100 info The --mqtt-broker command-line option only configures the PID tracker module's MQTT client, not the GStreamer pipeline's MQTT settings. You must edit the pipeline files to change the MQTT broker IP used by dctotrack and dctoverlay plugins.

searchDocs.title: What are Pipeline Files?​
searchDocs.content: Pipeline files are text files containing GStreamer pipeline definitions. Each file describes a complete video processing pipeline from source to output, including optional AI features like object detection, tracking, video recording, and frame capture.  The application loads two pipeline files at startup - one for each video source that can be switched between during runtime.

searchDocs.title: Pipeline File Format​
searchDocs.content: Pipeline files use standard GStreamer pipeline syntax with the following requirements:  Required Components:  Video Source: Typically v4l2src device=/dev/videoN (the application auto-detects N)Shared Memory Output: Must end with shmsink socket-path=/tmp/videoN.socket (N must match device number)H.264 Encoding: Required for RTSP streaming with format video/x-h264,stream-format=byte-stream,alignment=auProper Queuing: Use queue elements for smooth playback  important The device number N must be consistent across device=/dev/videoN, socket-path=/tmp/videoN.socket, and mqtt-topic="tracking/videoN" within each pipeline file. The application automatically extracts this number to configure RTSP streaming.  Optional Components:  Object Detection: dctobd or obd elementsObject Tracking: dctotrack element (publishes to MQTT)Visual Overlay: dctoverlay element (subscribes from MQTT)Video Recording: dctvrecord element (triggered by detections)Frame Capture: dctfcapture element (periodic or triggered)Tee Elements: For branching pipeline to multiple outputs

searchDocs.title: Basic Pipeline Structure​
searchDocs.content: v4l2src device=/dev/videoN ↓ [videoconvert + videoscale] ↓ [tee: split to detection path and display path] ↓ ↓ [obd/dctobd] [dctoverlay] ↓ ↓ [dctotrack → MQTT] [videoconvert] ↓ [h264 encode] ↓ [tee: split to recording and streaming] ↓ ↓ [dctvrecord] [shmsink] ↓ [dctfcapture]

searchDocs.title: Pipeline File Location​
searchDocs.content: Example pipelines are located at different paths depending on your environment:  On Target Device (Yocto Image):  /usr/share/sentinel-sdk/mantis_test_app/   Development Environment (Source Tree):  apps/mantis_test_app/example_pipelines/   tip When running on the target device, use the absolute path /usr/share/sentinel-sdk/mantis_test_app/ to access the pre-installed pipeline files. During development with the SDK, use the relative path example_pipelines/ from the application directory.

searchDocs.title: How to Use Pipeline Files​
searchDocs.content: Method 1: Using --file flag (Recommended)  On target device:  mantis_test_app --file /usr/share/sentinel-sdk/mantis_test_app/pipeline_video4_rtsp_vrec.txt \ /usr/share/sentinel-sdk/mantis_test_app/pipeline_video8_rtsp_vrec.txt   During development:  ./mantis_test_app --file example_pipelines/pipeline_video4_rtsp_vrec.txt \ example_pipelines/pipeline_video8_rtsp_vrec.txt   Method 2: Direct pipeline strings  ./mantis_test_app "v4l2src device=/dev/video4 ! ... ! shmsink socket-path=/tmp/video4.socket" \ "v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! ... ! shmsink socket-path=/tmp/video8.socket"   note Using pipeline files is recommended as they're easier to maintain and modify.

searchDocs.title: Creating Custom Pipelines​
searchDocs.content: To create a custom pipeline file:  Copy an existing pipeline as a template: On target device: cp /usr/share/sentinel-sdk/mantis_test_app/pipeline_video4_rtsp_vrec.txt my_custom_pipeline.txt During development: cp example_pipelines/pipeline_video4_rtsp_vrec.txt my_custom_pipeline.txt Modify key parameters (ensure device number N is consistent): Video device: Change device=/dev/videoNSocket path: Update socket-path=/tmp/videoN.socket (N must match device number)MQTT topic: Change mqtt-topic="tracking/videoN" (N should match device number)Resolution: Modify width= and height= valuesMQTT broker: Update mqtt-broker= and mqtt-port=Detection classes: Modify enabled-classes="bottle,person,car"Recording location: Change location=/tmp/videos warning The device number must be consistent throughout the pipeline (e.g., if using /dev/video4, use /tmp/video4.socket and tracking/video4) Test the pipeline: gst-launch-1.0 $(cat my_custom_pipeline.txt) Use in application: ./mantis_test_app --file my_custom_pipeline.txt <pipeline2.txt>

searchDocs.title: RTSP Streaming​
searchDocs.content: RTSP streams are automatically created based on the video device numbers detected from your pipeline files. The device numbers are extracted from the device=/dev/videoN parameter in your pipeline configuration.  For example, if your pipelines use:  Pipeline 1: device=/dev/video4 → Stream available at rtsp://<ip-address>:6000/video4Pipeline 2: device=/dev/video8 → Stream available at rtsp://<ip-address>:6000/video8

searchDocs.title: Accessing RTSP Streams​
searchDocs.content: Using VLC Player:  vlc rtsp://192.168.1.100:6000/video4 vlc rtsp://192.168.1.100:6000/video8   Using GStreamer:  gst-launch-1.0 rtspsrc location=rtsp://192.168.1.100:6000/video4 ! \ rtpjitterbuffer ! rtph264depay ! h264parse ! avdec_h264 ! \ videoconvert ! autovideosink sync=false   note The video device numbers (4, 8, etc.) are automatically detected from your pipeline files. You can use any video device number your system supports, and the RTSP URLs will adjust accordingly.

searchDocs.title: Runtime Controls​
searchDocs.content: During execution, the following keyboard commands are available:  Key	Function	Description1	Switch VIDEO to Source 1	Displays pipeline 1 output 2	Switch VIDEO to Source 2	Displays pipeline 2 output P	Switch PID input source	Toggle PID tracking between sources A	Toggle auto-link mode	Enable/disable PID-to-video source synchronization T	Toggle object tracking	Enable/disable tracking ON/OFF I	Set target object ID	Configure which object ID to track S	Show tracking status	Display current configuration and status H	Show help	Display control menu Q	Quit	Exit application cleanly

searchDocs.title: Object Tracking Workflow​
searchDocs.content: Start application with --enable-trackingPress S to view available object IDsPress I to set target ID to trackPress T to enable trackingPress P to manually switch PID input sourcePress A to enable auto-link (PID follows video switching)

searchDocs.title: Status Information​
searchDocs.content: Press S to display:  Current video source (1 or 2)Current PID source and MQTT topicAuto-link mode status (ON/OFF)Tracking enabled/disabledMQTT connection statusCurrent target IDList of available object IDs

searchDocs.title: Pipeline Fails to Start​
searchDocs.content: Check that video devices exist: ls /dev/video*Verify GStreamer elements are installed: gst-inspect-1.0 <element>Check pipeline syntax in configuration filesEnsure custom GStreamer plugins (dctobd, dctotrack, etc.) are installed

searchDocs.title: RTSP Stream Not Available​
searchDocs.content: Verify shared memory sockets exist: ls /tmp/video*.socketCheck firewall allows port 6000Ensure pipelines are outputting to correct socket pathsCheck GStreamer pipeline is running without errors

searchDocs.title: Object Tracking Not Working​
searchDocs.content: Verify MQTT broker is accessible: mosquitto_sub -h <broker> -t "#"Check MQTT topics in pipeline configuration match tracking configVerify PID object tracker library is built and installedPress S to check MQTT connection statusEnable debug logging: GST_DEBUG=3 ./mantis_test_app ...

searchDocs.title: Cleanup Issues on Exit​
searchDocs.content: First Ctrl+C initiates graceful shutdown (waits for EOS)Second Ctrl+C forces immediate exitThird Ctrl+C performs emergency terminationSocket files are automatically cleaned up on proper exit

searchDocs.title: Performance Issues​
searchDocs.content: Reduce frame rate in pipeline configurationIncrease detection frameinterval to process fewer framesLower video resolutionDisable recording or frame capture features if not needed

searchDocs.title: PID Object Tracker API​
searchDocs.content: The application integrates with the PID object tracker library (lib-pid-otrack.h):  // Initialize tracker DctotrackPID::MQTTObjectTracker tracker(model_res, display_res); tracker.getTracker()->initializeWithConfig("mantis_app"); tracker.getTracker()->ai_obj_trk_enable(); // Calculate pan/tilt commands auto command = tracker.getTracker()->calculatePanTiltCommand(); if (command.valid) { // Use command.pan_delta and command.tilt_delta for camera control }   For full API documentation, see PID Object Tracker.

searchDocs.title: Signal Handling​
searchDocs.content: The application handles signals gracefully:  SIGINT/SIGTERM: Initiates graceful shutdown with EOS propagationMultiple signals: Progressively forces faster shutdownEmergency exit: Three consecutive signals perform immediate termination

searchDocs.title: Performance Notes​
searchDocs.content: Shared memory transport minimizes CPU overheadRTSP streaming uses minimal buffering for low latencyPID tracking runs at ~10Hz in separate threadVideo switching is seamless without frame drops

searchDocs.title: Custom GStreamer Plugins​
searchDocs.content: The application expects the following custom plugins:  dctobd: Object detection elementdctotrack: Object tracking elementdctoverlay: Visualization overlay elementdctvrecord: Video recording elementdctfcapture: Frame capture element

searchDocs.title: Basic Build (Without MQTT)​
searchDocs.content: # Remove any build directory if already present: rm -rf builddir/ # Setup build directory (default: MACH_GENERIC, comm=none) meson setup builddir # Compile ninja -C builddir   Once the compilation is done, the following files among other should be generated in the builddir.  builddir/ # Build directory ├── libapidctfcapture.a # Plugin API library ├── libgstdctfcapture.so # GStreamer plugin (plugin interface) ├── test_dctfcapture # Test application for Gstreamer APIs ├── test_api_dctfcapture # Test application for Custom APIs └── selftest # Self test application

searchDocs.title: Build with MQTT Support​
searchDocs.content: To enable MQTT communication framework and AUTO mode functionality:  # Setup build directory with MQTT support meson setup builddir -Dcomm=mqtt # Compile ninja -C builddir   With MQTT enabled, additional files are generated:  builddir/ # Build directory ├── libapidctfcapture.a # Plugin API library ├── libgstdctfcapture.so # GStreamer plugin (with MQTT support) ├── test_dctfcapture # Test application for Gstreamer APIs ├── test_api_dctfcapture # Test application for Custom APIs ├── mqtt_publisher # MQTT publisher test utility ├── test_mqtt_auto_mode # Test application for AUTO mode with MQTT ├── test_mode_change # Test application for runtime mode switching └── selftest # Self test application

searchDocs.title: Build Options​
searchDocs.content: The plugin supports multiple build configuration options:  Machine Layer Selection​  Since this plugin is implemented in a layered architecture, support for additional machines can be added in mach/ layer of the plugin source. To build the plugin and library for a specific machine, issue the following command:  # Explicitly specify machine layer meson setup builddir -Dmach=<machine-name>   Machine Layer Options:  MACH_GENERIC (default): Software implementation using OpenCV  You can find steps to add support for additional machine here.  Communication Framework Selection​  The communication framework determines whether MQTT support is included:  # Build without communication framework (default) meson setup builddir -Dcomm=none # Build with MQTT communication framework meson setup builddir -Dcomm=mqtt   Communication Framework Options:  none (default): No communication framework, MQTT dependencies not requiredmqtt: Enables MQTT communication layer for AUTO mode functionality  Combined Build Options​  You can combine multiple build options:  # Example: Machine-specific build with MQTT support meson setup builddir -Dmach=MACH_GENERIC -Dcomm=mqtt # Example: Reconfigure existing build to enable MQTT meson configure builddir -Dcomm=mqtt ninja -C builddir

searchDocs.title: Running the examples​
searchDocs.content: The examples can be run in 2 ways. It can be run in the platform where the plugin and its test code were compiled. Or else, if the compilation was done for a different target platform, then you will have to load the plugins and the examples to that target machine.

searchDocs.title: 1. Run the example/test in the machine where it was compiled​
searchDocs.content: The plugins and the test code are output in the builddir directory. So provide the plugin path to Gstreamer before the test and the example pipeline are run.  # Pipeline GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir gst-launch-1.0 ... # Test app. GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/<test-app>

searchDocs.title: 2. Run the example/test in a target machine​
searchDocs.content: Upload the plugin and test app to the target platform. Here, we use the adb utility.  # Push the plugin to the plugin directory adb push builddir/libgstobd.so <plugin directory> # Eg: /usr/lib/gstreamer-1.0/ # Push the test apps to the execution directory adb push builddir/<test-app> # Enter the adb shell and execute them adb shell shell# ./<test-app>   note The examples shown here are run on the Host PC itself, where the compilation was done.

searchDocs.title: Manual Mode with Prefix​
searchDocs.content: The following example runs in Manual mode and captures 1 frame as the capture flag which is set true captures the first frame and will then be set to false state. Also, the file name will have a prefix appended to it.  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir gst-launch-1.0 videotestsrc num-buffers=10 ! \ video/x-raw,format=I420,width=640,height=480 ! \ dctfcapture mode=0 location=/tmp prefix=frame capture=true ! \ fakesink   Output: /tmp/frame_2025_10_03_18_03_59_226.jpg

searchDocs.title: Manual Mode without Prefix​
searchDocs.content: The following example runs in Manual mode and captures 1 frame as the capture flag which is set true captures the first frame and will then be set to false state.  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir gst-launch-1.0 videotestsrc num-buffers=10 ! \ video/x-raw,format=I420,width=640,height=480 ! \ dctfcapture mode=0 location=/tmp capture=true ! \ fakesink   Output: /tmp/2025_10_03_18_04_16_008.jpg

searchDocs.title: Periodic Mode​
searchDocs.content: The following example runs in Periodic mode and captures a frame every 3 seconds as the time-period is set to 3 seconds.  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir gst-launch-1.0 videotestsrc ! \ video/x-raw,format=I420,width=640,height=480 ! \ dctfcapture mode=1 time-period=3 location=/tmp prefix=capture ! \ videoconvert ! autovideosink   Captures every 3 seconds with timestamped filenames:  /tmp/capture_2025_10_03_18_03_59_226.jpg/tmp/capture_2025_10_03_18_04_02_312.jpg/tmp/capture_2025_10_03_18_04_05_401.jpg

searchDocs.title: AUTO Mode (MQTT-based Object Detection)​
searchDocs.content: note AUTO mode requires the plugin to be built with MQTT support: meson setup builddir -Dcomm=mqtt  The following example runs in AUTO mode and captures frames when object detection messages arrive via MQTT:  # Start MQTT broker (in separate terminal) mosquitto -v # Run pipeline with AUTO mode GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir gst-launch-1.0 videotestsrc ! \ video/x-raw,format=I420,width=640,height=480 ! \ dctfcapture mode=2 mqtt-topic=object/detection \ mqtt-host=localhost mqtt-port=1883 time-skip=100 \ location=/tmp prefix=detected ! \ videoconvert ! autovideosink   note Requires a running MQTT broker (Mosquitto) and a publisher sending object detection messages to the configured topic.  MQTT Message Format (JSON):  { "objects_detected": true, "count": 2, "objects": [ {"class": "person", "confidence": 0.95}, {"class": "car", "confidence": 0.87} ] }   Captures on object detection with timestamped filenames:  /tmp/detected_2025_10_09_14_30_45_123.jpg/tmp/detected_2025_10_09_14_30_45_678.jpg

searchDocs.title: AUTO Mode with Remote Broker​
searchDocs.content: Connect to a remote MQTT broker:  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir gst-launch-1.0 videotestsrc ! \ video/x-raw,format=I420,width=640,height=480 ! \ dctfcapture mode=2 mqtt-topic=camera/detection \ mqtt-host=192.168.1.100 mqtt-port=1883 time-skip=0 \ location=/tmp prefix=remote ! \ videoconvert ! autovideosink

searchDocs.title: 1. Self-Test (Automated Comprehensive Tests)​
searchDocs.content: Automated test suite that validates all plugin functionality:  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/selftest   Test Coverage:  Manual mode capture with prefixManual mode capture without prefixPeriodic mode capture (time-based intervals)API getter functionsRuntime property modification  Exit code 0 indicates all tests passed.

searchDocs.title: 2. GStreamer-based Test (test_dctfcapture)​
searchDocs.content: Interactive test using direct GStreamer API:  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/test_dctfcapture

searchDocs.title: 3. API-based Test (test_api_dctfcapture)​
searchDocs.content: Interactive test using the simplified C API:  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/test_api_dctfcapture   The interactive tests provide prompts to:  Select capture mode (Manual/Periodic)Set time period (for Periodic mode)Automatically test the selected configuration

searchDocs.title: 4. MQTT AUTO Mode Test (test_mqtt_auto_mode)​
searchDocs.content: note Requires build with MQTT support: meson setup builddir -Dcomm=mqtt  Test AUTO mode with MQTT object detection:  # Start MQTT broker first mosquitto -v # Run AUTO mode test (captures for 10 seconds) GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/test_mqtt_auto_mode 10   What it tests:  MQTT connection to broker (localhost:1883)Subscription to "object/detection" topicFrame capture on object detection messagesThrottling with time-skip configurationAuto-reconnection on broker restart  Usage:  ./builddir/test_mqtt_auto_mode <duration_seconds>

searchDocs.title: 5. Mode Change Test (test_mode_change)​
searchDocs.content: note Requires build with MQTT support: meson setup builddir -Dcomm=mqtt  Test runtime mode switching and MQTT connection management:  # Start MQTT broker first mosquitto -v # Run mode change test GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/test_mode_change   What it tests:  MANUAL → AUTO mode switching (MQTT connects)AUTO → PERIODIC mode switching (MQTT disconnects)PERIODIC → AUTO mode switching (MQTT reconnects)Resource cleanup during mode transitionsRuntime property reconfiguration

searchDocs.title: Core Dependencies (Always Required)​
searchDocs.content: GStreamer >= 1.0GStreamer Base >= 1.0GStreamer Video >= 1.0OpenCV 4 (for MACH_GENERIC)Meson >= 0.54  Install on Ubuntu/Debian:  sudo apt-get install libgstreamer1.0-dev libgstreamer-plugins-base1.0-dev \ libopencv-dev meson ninja-build

searchDocs.title: MQTT Communication Dependencies (Optional)​
searchDocs.content: Only required when building with -Dcomm=mqtt option:  Mosquitto MQTT client library (libmosquitto-dev)Mosquitto broker (for testing)  Install on Ubuntu/Debian:  sudo apt-get install libmosquitto-dev mosquitto mosquitto-clients   note MQTT dependencies are only required if you build with -Dcomm=mqtt to enable AUTO mode (mode=2) for event-driven capture. If you don't need MQTT functionality, you can build without these dependencies using the default build configuration.

searchDocs.title: Property Summary Table​
searchDocs.content: Property	Type	Range/Values	Default	Descriptiontrack-thresh	float	0.0 - 1.0	0.5	Minimum confidence to start tracking high-thresh	float	0.0 - 1.0	0.6	High confidence threshold for first association match-thresh	float	0.0 - 1.0	0.8	IoU threshold for matching track-buffer	int	1 - 1000	30	Frames to keep lost tracks frame-rate	int	1 - 240	30	Expected video frame rate (fps) output	string	none/text/mqtt/both	text	Output mode output-format	string	tracking/detection	tracking	Output JSON format mqtt-broker	string	any	localhost	MQTT broker address mqtt-port	int	1 - 65535	1883	MQTT broker port mqtt-topic	string	any	tracking/results	MQTT publish topic track-statistics	boolean	true/false	false	Enable statistics logging

searchDocs.title: track-thresh​
searchDocs.content: Description: Minimum confidence threshold for starting a new track.  Type: floatRange: 0.0 - 1.0Default: 0.5  Detections with confidence below this threshold will not be used to initialize new tracks. However, they may still be used to update existing tracks (see high-thresh).  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack track-thresh=0.6 ! ...

searchDocs.title: high-thresh​
searchDocs.content: Description: High confidence threshold for first-stage association.  Type: floatRange: 0.0 - 1.0Default: 0.6  In the ByteTrack algorithm, detections are separated into high and low confidence. High-confidence detections (above this threshold) are matched first to existing tracks. Low-confidence detections are then used to recover lost tracks.  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack high-thresh=0.7 ! ...

searchDocs.title: match-thresh​
searchDocs.content: Description: IoU (Intersection over Union) threshold for matching detections to tracks.  Type: floatRange: 0.0 - 1.0Default: 0.8  When a detection and a predicted track position have an IoU above this threshold, they are considered as a potential match. Higher values require more overlap for matching.  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack match-thresh=0.75 ! ...

searchDocs.title: track-buffer​
searchDocs.content: Description: Number of frames to keep lost tracks before removing them permanently.  Type: intRange: 1 - 1000Default: 30  When a track is not matched to any detection, it enters the "Lost" state. If it remains unmatched for more frames than this buffer size, it will be permanently removed. Increase this value for scenarios with frequent occlusions.  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack track-buffer=50 ! ...

searchDocs.title: frame-rate​
searchDocs.content: Description: Expected frame rate of the video source in frames per second (fps).  Type: intRange: 1 - 240Default: 30  This value is used by the Kalman filter for motion prediction. Set it to match your actual video frame rate for accurate prediction.  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack frame-rate=60 ! ...

searchDocs.title: output​
searchDocs.content: Description: Output mode for tracking results.  Type: stringValid Values: "none", "text", "mqtt", "both"Default: "text"  none: Silent mode, no output generatedtext: JSON output to stdout (human-readable)mqtt: Publish results to MQTT brokerboth: Text + MQTT simultaneously  gst-launchC APIGObject Property # Text output gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output=text ! ... # MQTT output gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output=mqtt ! ... # Both outputs gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output=both ! ... # No output (silent) gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output=none ! ...

searchDocs.title: output-format​
searchDocs.content: Description: Format of the output JSON structure.  Type: stringValid Values: "tracking", "detection"Default: "tracking"  tracking: Separate tracks array with track_id, state, and detection info {"timestamp": X, "tracks": [{track_id, class, confidence, bbox, state}, ...]} detection: Detection format with track_id merged into each detection {"timestamp": X, "detections": [{class, confidence, bbox, track_id}, ...]}   gst-launchC APIGObject Property # Tracking format gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output-format=tracking ! ... # Detection format gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output-format=detection ! ...

searchDocs.title: MQTT Configuration​
searchDocs.content: These properties are only relevant when output is set to "mqtt" or "both".

searchDocs.title: mqtt-broker​
searchDocs.content: Description: MQTT broker hostname or IP address.  Type: stringDefault: "localhost"  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output=mqtt mqtt-broker=192.168.1.100 ! ...

searchDocs.title: mqtt-port​
searchDocs.content: Description: MQTT broker port number.  Type: intRange: 1 - 65535Default: 1883  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output=mqtt mqtt-port=8883 ! ...

searchDocs.title: mqtt-topic​
searchDocs.content: Description: MQTT topic to publish tracking results.  Type: stringDefault: "tracking/results"  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack output=mqtt mqtt-topic=camera1/tracking ! ...

searchDocs.title: track-statistics​
searchDocs.content: Description: Enable detailed tracking statistics logging.  Type: booleanDefault: false  When enabled, the plugin logs detailed statistics about track states, counts, and processing metrics to the console.  gst-launchC APIGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack track-statistics=true ! ...

searchDocs.title: Surveillance System (High Accuracy)​
searchDocs.content: gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src ! videoconvert ! video/x-raw,format=RGB \ ! dctobd model-path=/path/to/model.synap \ ! dctotrack \ track-thresh=0.6 \ high-thresh=0.7 \ match-thresh=0.85 \ track-buffer=50 \ frame-rate=30 \ output=mqtt \ mqtt-broker=192.168.1.100 \ mqtt-topic=surveillance/tracking \ ! videoconvert ! autovideosink

searchDocs.title: Real-time Processing (Performance Optimized)​
searchDocs.content: gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src ! videoconvert ! video/x-raw,format=RGB \ ! dctobd model-path=/path/to/model.synap \ ! dctotrack \ track-thresh=0.4 \ high-thresh=0.5 \ match-thresh=0.7 \ track-buffer=20 \ frame-rate=60 \ output=none \ ! videoconvert ! autovideosink

searchDocs.title: Crowded Scene (Frequent Occlusions)​
searchDocs.content: gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src ! videoconvert ! video/x-raw,format=RGB \ ! dctobd model-path=/path/to/model.synap \ ! dctotrack \ track-thresh=0.5 \ high-thresh=0.6 \ match-thresh=0.75 \ track-buffer=100 \ frame-rate=30 \ output=both \ mqtt-broker=localhost \ mqtt-topic=crowd/tracking \ track-statistics=true \ ! videoconvert ! autovideosink

searchDocs.title: Querying Properties at Runtime​
searchDocs.content: You can inspect current property values using gst-inspect-1.0:  # List all properties gst-inspect-1.0 dctotrack # Query specific property via pipeline gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctotrack name=tracker ! ... & # Then use gst-launch-1.0 with --gst-debug to see property values   Using C API:  float track_thresh; api_dctotrack_get_track_thresh(element, &track_thresh); printf("Current track-thresh: %.2f\n", track_thresh);   Using GObject:  gfloat track_thresh; g_object_get(G_OBJECT(element), "track-thresh", &track_thresh, NULL); g_print("Current track-thresh: %.2f\n", track_thresh);

searchDocs.title: Tips for Tuning​
searchDocs.content: track-thresh vs high-thresh: Keep high-thresh ≥ track-threshLarger gap allows more recovery of lost tracks from low-confidence detections match-thresh: Lower values (0.6-0.7): Better for fast-moving objects with imperfect detectionHigher values (0.8-0.9): Better for static/slow scenes with accurate detection track-buffer: Short buffer (10-20): Fast removal of disappeared objectsLong buffer (50-100): Better recovery from occlusions frame-rate: Always match your actual video FPS for accurate motion predictionIncorrect value leads to poor prediction and ID switches output modes: Use none when tracking data is consumed internally (metadata passing)Use mqtt for multi-system integration and real-time monitoringUse both during development/debugging

searchDocs.title: Usage Flow​
searchDocs.content: To use the plugin library you will need to follow the below sequence of operations.

searchDocs.title: Step 1: Pipeline Initialization​
searchDocs.content: Initialize a gstreamer pipeline with this plugin.  #include <apidctobd.h> GstElement *pipeline, *dctobd; // Initialize gst_init(&argc, &argv); pipeline = gst_parse_launch("v4l2src ! videoconvert ! ... ! dctobd name=detector ! ...", NULL);   note The plugin must have a name associated with it, which we will use to initialize the plugin api layer.

searchDocs.title: Step 2: Plugin Initialization​
searchDocs.content: Once the pipeline is initialized successfully, call the plugin initialization function to get the plugin element object.  With APIGST API // Initialize dctobd =api_dctobd_init(pipeline, "detector");

searchDocs.title: Step 3: Plugin Configuration​
searchDocs.content: Once the initialization is done, you can use the apis as needed.  With APIGST API // Configure api_dctobd_set_model(dctobd, "/usr/share/synap/models/yolov8s-640x384/model.synap"); api_dctobd_set_mode(dctobd, DCTOBD_MODE_DETECTOR); api_dctobd_set_output_mode(dctobd, OBD_OUTPUT_JSON); api_dctobd_set_confidence_threshold(dctobd, 0.7f); api_dctobd_set_enabled_classes(dctobd, "person,car"); // Optionally set label file (use GStreamer API for properties not in API layer) g_object_set(dctobd, "label", "/path/to/labels.json", NULL); // Start pipeline gst_element_set_state(pipeline, GST_STATE_PLAYING);

searchDocs.title: Dctobd Mode API​
searchDocs.content: Defines the detection mode for the dctobd element.  typedef enum { DCTOBD_MODE_DETECTOR = 0 // Detector mode for object detection } DctobdModeAPI;   Value	DescriptionDCTOBD_MODE_DETECTOR	Object detection mode

searchDocs.title: Functions​
searchDocs.content: These functions provide a C interface for controlling object detection from GStreamer pipelines.

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_init​
searchDocs.content: Initialize and retrieve the dctobd element from a GStreamer pipeline.  GstElement* api_dctobd_init(GstElement *pipeline, const char *element_name);   Parameters:  pipeline - GstElement pipeline containing the dctobd elementelement_name - Name of the dctobd element in the pipeline  Returns:  Pointer to dctobd element on successNULL on failure  Memory Management The caller is responsible for unreferencing the returned element using gst_object_unref() when done.  Example:  GstElement *pipeline = ...; // Your pipeline GstElement *dctobd = api_dctobd_init(pipeline, "detector"); if (dctobd) { // Use the dctobd element gst_object_unref(dctobd); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_model​
searchDocs.content: Set the model file path.  bool api_dctobd_set_model(GstElement *element, const char *model_path);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementmodel_path - Path to the model file (.synap file)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  note Model changes require pipeline restart to take effect.  Example:  api_dctobd_set_model(dctobd, "/usr/share/synap/models/yolov8s-640x384/model.synap");

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_model_directory​
searchDocs.content: Set the model directory for scanning.  bool api_dctobd_set_model_directory(GstElement *element, const char *directory);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementdirectory - Directory path to scan for models  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  api_dctobd_set_model_directory(dctobd, "/custom/models");

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_get_available_models​
searchDocs.content: Get the list of available model files in the configured directory.  char* api_dctobd_get_available_models(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElement  Returns:  Comma-separated list of model paths on success (caller must free())NULL on failure  Memory Management The caller must free() the returned string when done.  Example:  char *models = api_dctobd_get_available_models(dctobd); if (models) { printf("Available models: %s\n", models); free(models); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_mode​
searchDocs.content: Set the detection mode.  bool api_dctobd_set_mode(GstElement *element, DctobdModeAPI mode);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementmode - Detection mode (currently only DCTOBD_MODE_DETECTOR is supported)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  api_dctobd_set_mode(dctobd, DCTOBD_MODE_DETECTOR);

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_confidence_threshold​
searchDocs.content: Set the confidence threshold for detections.  bool api_dctobd_set_confidence_threshold(GstElement *element, float threshold);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementthreshold - Confidence threshold (0.0-1.0)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  // Set threshold to 0.7 (70% confidence) api_dctobd_set_confidence_threshold(dctobd, 0.7f);

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_max_detections​
searchDocs.content: Set the maximum number of detections per frame.  bool api_dctobd_set_max_detections(GstElement *element, int num_inference);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementnum_inference - Maximum number of detections per frame  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  api_dctobd_set_max_detections(dctobd, 10);

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_frame_interval​
searchDocs.content: Set the frame processing interval.  bool api_dctobd_set_frame_interval(GstElement *element, int interval);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementinterval - Process every Nth frame (0 = process all frames)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  // Process every 3rd frame api_dctobd_set_frame_interval(dctobd, 3);

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_inference_statistics​
searchDocs.content: Enable or disable inference statistics.  bool api_dctobd_set_inference_statistics(GstElement *element, bool enable);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementenable - true to enable statistics, false to disable  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  api_dctobd_set_inference_statistics(dctobd, true);

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_detection_enabled​
searchDocs.content: Enable or disable object detection.  bool api_dctobd_set_detection_enabled(GstElement *element, bool enable);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementenable - true to enable detection, false to disable  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  // Disable detection api_dctobd_set_detection_enabled(dctobd, false); // Enable detection api_dctobd_set_detection_enabled(dctobd, true);

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_set_enabled_classes​
searchDocs.content: Set the enabled class names for filtering.  bool api_dctobd_set_enabled_classes(GstElement *element, const char *classes);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementclasses - Comma-separated list of class names to enable  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  note If NULL or empty, all classes are enabled.  Example:  // Detect only persons and cars api_dctobd_set_enabled_classes(dctobd, "person,car"); // Enable all classes api_dctobd_set_enabled_classes(dctobd, NULL);

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_get_available_classes​
searchDocs.content: Get the available class names from the model.  char* api_dctobd_get_available_classes(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElement  Returns:  Comma-separated list of class names on success (caller must free())NULL on failure  Memory Management The caller must free() the returned string when done.  Example:  char *classes = api_dctobd_get_available_classes(dctobd); if (classes) { printf("Available classes: %s\n", classes); free(classes); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_get_model​
searchDocs.content: Get the current model path.  char* api_dctobd_get_model(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElement  Returns:  Current model path on success (caller must free())NULL on failure  Memory Management The caller must free() the returned string when done.  Example:  char *model = api_dctobd_get_model(dctobd); if (model) { printf("Current model: %s\n", model); free(model); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_get_confidence_threshold​
searchDocs.content: Get the current confidence threshold.  bool api_dctobd_get_confidence_threshold(GstElement *element, float *threshold);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementthreshold - Pointer to store the current threshold  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  float threshold; if (api_dctobd_get_confidence_threshold(dctobd, &threshold)) { printf("Current threshold: %.2f\n", threshold); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_get_max_detections​
searchDocs.content: Get the current maximum number of detections.  bool api_dctobd_get_max_detections(GstElement *element, int *num_inference);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementnum_inference - Pointer to store the current max detections  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  int max_detections; if (api_dctobd_get_max_detections(dctobd, &max_detections)) { printf("Max detections: %d\n", max_detections); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctobd_get_detection_enabled​
searchDocs.content: Get whether detection is enabled.  bool api_dctobd_get_detection_enabled(GstElement *element, bool *enabled);   Parameters:  element - dctobd GstElementenabled - Pointer to store the enabled state  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  bool enabled; if (api_dctobd_get_detection_enabled(dctobd, &enabled)) { printf("Detection enabled: %s\n", enabled ? "yes" : "no"); }

searchDocs.title: Usage Example​
searchDocs.content: Here's a complete example demonstrating the API usage:  #include "apidctobd.h" int main(int argc, char *argv[]) { GstElement *pipeline, *dctobd; // Initialize pipeline gst_init(&argc, &argv); pipeline = gst_parse_launch( "v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! videoscale ! " "video/x-raw,width=640,height=384,format=RGB ! " "dctobd name=detector ! " "dctobdsink location=/tmp/results.txt", NULL); // Get dctobd element dctobd = api_dctobd_init(pipeline, "detector"); if (!dctobd) { fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialize dctobd element\n"); return -1; } // Configure for person detection api_dctobd_set_model(dctobd, "/usr/share/synap/models/yolov8s-640x384/model.synap"); api_dctobd_set_mode(dctobd, DCTOBD_MODE_DETECTOR); api_dctobd_set_output_mode(dctobd, OBD_OUTPUT_JSON); api_dctobd_set_confidence_threshold(dctobd, 0.7f); api_dctobd_set_enabled_classes(dctobd, "person"); api_dctobd_set_frame_interval(dctobd, 3); // Start pipeline gst_element_set_state(pipeline, GST_STATE_PLAYING); // Run main loop... // Later: query available classes char *classes = api_dctobd_get_available_classes(dctobd); if (classes) { g_print("Available classes: %s\n", classes); free(classes); } // Switch to vehicle detection api_dctobd_set_enabled_classes(dctobd, "car,truck,bus,motorcycle"); api_dctobd_set_confidence_threshold(dctobd, 0.6f); // Cleanup gst_object_unref(dctobd); return 0; }

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.content: The plugin library is organized into different layers.    GST Layer - The GST layer has the main Gstreamer related functionalities. However, the functional tasks which can be offloaded to different hardware is kept in the machine layer. Machine Layer - This is the layer where machine specific operations are implemented. This is done to port the plugin easily to different platforms. API Layer (Optional) - The API layer is a wrapper layer using which the user can configure the gstreamer plugin. This is not part of the gstreamer framework. Instead of the API layer, the user can use gstreamer's APIs directly too. Communication Layer (Optional) - This layer the communication of the plugin to the external world or other plugins. Currently only MQTT is supported.

searchDocs.title: Folder Structure​
searchDocs.content: The corresponding folder structure is as follows:  inc/ # Header files ├── gst/ # GStreamer layer (plugin interface) ├── mach/ # Machine layer (processing & conversion) ├── comm/ # Communication layer (data recv & transmit) └── api/ # API layer (C interface) src/ # Source files ├── gst/ # GStreamer implementation ├── mach/ # Machine implementations (generic, hw, etc.) ├── comm/ # Communication layer └── api/ # API implementation test/ # Test applications ├── gst/ # GStreamer-based tests ├── mqtt/ # Mqtt based tests. └── api/ # API-based tests

searchDocs.title: Features​
searchDocs.content: This gstreamer plugin has the following features/functionalities:  Different Capture Modes: Manual Mode: The user can trigger a frame capture via setting a property or calling an API.Periodic Mode: The user can configure the plugin to capture the frames automatically at a specified time interval (1 to 3600 secs).Automatic Mode: The user can communicate to receive events from the external world and capture based on these events. Timestamp-based Filenames: The frames are saved in the following format <PREFIX>_YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.jpg. The <PREFIX> is user-configurable. With prefix: <PREFIX>_YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.jpgWithout prefix: YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.jpg Save Location: The user can configure the directory where the images needs to be saved.

searchDocs.title: Basic Speech Recognition​
searchDocs.content: From Microphone (USB)​  # Basic USB microphone gst-launch-1.0 alsasrc device=hw:1,0 ! \ audioconvert ! \ audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=S16LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15   From DMIC​  # Digital microphone (DMIC) gst-launch-1.0 alsasrc device=hw:0,2 ! \ audioconvert ! \ audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=S16LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15   From Audio File​  # WAV file gst-launch-1.0 filesrc location=test.wav ! \ wavparse ! \ audioconvert ! \ audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=S16LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15

searchDocs.title: Vosk with TCP Backend​
searchDocs.content: Live Microphone​  # USB Microphone with TCP gst-launch-1.0 alsasrc device=hw:1,0 ! \ audioconvert ! \ audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=S16LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 tcp-port=9999 # DMIC with TCP gst-launch-1.0 alsasrc device=hw:0,2 ! \ audioconvert ! \ audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=S16LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 tcp-port=8888 # Without partials gst-launch-1.0 alsasrc device=hw:1,0 ! \ audioconvert ! \ audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=S16LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 tcp-port=9999 partials=false   Audio File​  # Basic gst-launch-1.0 filesrc location=test.wav ! \ wavparse ! \ audioconvert ! \ audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=S16LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 tcp-port=9999 # Custom port gst-launch-1.0 filesrc location=audio.wav ! \ wavparse ! \ audioconvert ! \ audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=S16LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-en-us-0.22-lgraph tcp-port=7777   Monitor TCP Output​  # Terminal 1: Run pipeline gst-launch-1.0 alsasrc device=hw:1,0 ! audioconvert ! audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=S16LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 tcp-port=9999 # Terminal 2: Listen to results nc localhost 9999

searchDocs.title: Vosk with MQTT Backend​

searchDocs.title: No Recognition Output​
searchDocs.content: Check that:  Microphone is working: arecord -d 5 test.wav && aplay test.wavModel path is correct: ls models/vosk_model or ls models/ggml-model-q8_0.binAudio format is correct: Vosk: S16LE, mono, 16kHzWhisper: F32LE, mono, 16kHz

searchDocs.title: Poor Recognition Accuracy​
searchDocs.content: Vosk:  Use a larger model for better accuracyEnsure clean audio input (reduce background noise)Update grammar file with specific vocabulary  Whisper:  Use a larger model (base → small → medium)Adjust threads for better performanceEnable VAD with use-vad=trueAdjust step-ms and length-ms for your use case

searchDocs.title: High CPU Usage​
searchDocs.content: Vosk:  Use smaller model (vosk-model-small-*)Disable partial results (partials=false)  Whisper:  Use smaller model (tiny or base)Reduce thread count (threads=2)Enable VAD (use-vad=true)Increase step-ms value

searchDocs.title: Transcribe Multiple Files​
searchDocs.content: #!/bin/bash # Using Vosk for file in *.wav; do echo "Processing: $file" gst-launch-1.0 filesrc location="$file" ! \ wavparse ! \ audioconvert ! \ audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=S16LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 \ tcp-port=9999 > "${file%.wav}.txt" done # Using Whisper for file in *.wav; do echo "Processing: $file" gst-launch-1.0 filesrc location="$file" ! \ wavparse ! \ audioconvert ! \ audioresample ! \ audio/x-raw,format=F32LE,channels=1,rate=16000 ! \ dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/whisper/ggml-tiny.en-q5_1.bin \ tcp-port=9999 > "${file%.wav}.txt" done

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.content: The plugin library is organized into different layers.    GST Layer - The GST layer has the main Gstreamer related functionalities. However, the functional tasks which can be offloaded to different hardware is kept in the machine layer. Machine Layer - This is the layer where machine specific operations are implemented. This is done to port the plugin easily to different platforms. API Layer (Optional) - The API layer is a wrapper layer using which the user can configure the gstreamer plugin. This is not part of the gstreamer framework. Instead of the API layer, the user can use gstreamer's APIs directly too. Communication Layer (Optional) - This layer handles the communication of the plugin to the external world or other plugins. Currently only MQTT is supported for receiving object detection messages in AUTO mode.

searchDocs.title: Folder Structure​
searchDocs.content: The corresponding folder structure is as follows:  inc/ # Header files ├── gst/ # GStreamer layer (plugin interface) ├── mach/ # Machine layer (processing & conversion) ├── comm/ # Communication layer (MQTT support) └── api/ # API layer (C interface) src/ # Source files ├── gst/ # GStreamer implementation ├── mach/ # Machine implementations (generic, hw, etc.) ├── comm/ # Communication layer (MQTT) └── api/ # API implementation test/ # Test applications ├── gst/ # GStreamer-based tests ├── api/ # API-based tests ├── mqtt_publisher.c # API-based tests └── selftest.c # Automated testing suite of the plugin

searchDocs.title: Features​
searchDocs.content: This gstreamer plugin has the following features/functionalities:  Different Recording Modes: Manual Mode: The user can start/stop recording via setting a property or calling an API.Automatic Mode: The user can configure the plugin to automatically start/stop recording based on MQTT object detection messages. MQTT-Based Automatic Recording: In AUTO mode, the plugin subscribes to an MQTT topic and automatically starts recording when detections are received, stops when no detections arrive for a configurable timeout.Connection Loss Handling: Automatically stops recording after 5 seconds of MQTT connection loss or no messages.Timestamp-based Filenames: The video files are saved in the following format <PREFIX>_YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.mp4. The <PREFIX> is user-configurable. With prefix: <PREFIX>_YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.mp4Without prefix: YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.mp4 Save Location: The user can configure the directory where the MP4 files needs to be saved. The files are stored in a date based structure.H.264/AVC Video Support: Accepts H.264 video streams with AVC format and AU alignment.

searchDocs.title: location​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the directory path where the MP4 video files need to be saved. This property is mandatory to be set before running the element in a pipeline.  Type: StringDefault: NULLAccess: Read/Write  If /home/user/videos is the target location , then :  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctvrecord location=/home/user/videos ...   warning The user must verify that the location value passed is an actual existing directory. If the directory doesn't exist, then dctvrecord will fail to start the recording operation.

searchDocs.title: prefix​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the prefix that needs to be prepended to the file names.  Type: StringDefault: NULLAccess: Read/Write  If CAM1 is the prefix, then :  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctvrecord prefix=CAM1 ...   The files will be saved as follows:  With prefix: <PREFIX>_YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.mp4Without prefix: YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.mp4

searchDocs.title: recording​
searchDocs.content: In MANUAL mode, writing true to this property will start recording, false will stop recording.  Type: BooleanDefault: falseAccess: Read/Write (MANUAL mode), Read-only (AUTO mode)  note This property is only valid in MANUAL mode. In AUTO mode, recording property has no role in controlling the video recording.  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API # Start recording (Manual mode) gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctvrecord mode=0 recording=true ...

searchDocs.title: mode​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the recording mode. This plugin can record in 2 modes:  Mode	DescriptionManual (0)	User manually controls recording via API Auto (1)	Automatic recording based on MQTT object detection messages  Type: Integer [0/1]Default: 0Access: Read/Write  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API # Manual mode gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctvrecord mode=0 ... # AUTO mode gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctvrecord mode=1 ...

searchDocs.title: auto-enable​
searchDocs.content: Enables or disables the automatic recording feature in Auto mode. When enabled, the plugin connects to MQTT broker and starts monitoring for detection messages.  Type: BooleanDefault: trueAccess: Read/Write  note This property is only effective in Auto mode. Setting this to true initiates MQTT connection. Setting to false disconnects from MQTT and stops recording.  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API # Enable automatic recording gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctvrecord mode=1 auto-enable=true mqtt-topic=detections/camera1 ...   note Before setting auto-enable property to true, ensure that the properties location, mqtt-topicand mode are set correctly.

searchDocs.title: host​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the MQTT broker host address to connect to in Auto mode.  Type: StringDefault: "localhost"Access: Read/Write  note This property is protocol-agnostic and will be used for future TCP and Kafka support. Currently only MQTT is supported.  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctvrecord mode=1 host=192.168.1.100 port=1883 ...

searchDocs.title: port​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the MQTT broker port to connect to in Auto mode.  Type: IntegerDefault: 1883Range: 1-65535Access: Read/Write  note This property is protocol-agnostic and will be used for future TCP and Kafka support. Currently only MQTT is supported (default port: 1883).  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctvrecord mode=1 host=192.168.1.100 port=1883 ...

searchDocs.title: mqtt-topic​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the MQTT topic to subscribe for object detection messages in Auto mode. When detections are received on this topic, recording automatically starts. If auto-enable is true.  Type: StringDefault: NULLAccess: Read/Write  note This property is only effective in Auto mode. Setting this property when auto-enable is true will automatically connect to the broker.  If camera/detections is the topic name, then :  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctvrecord mode=1 host=192.168.1.100 port=1883 \ auto-enable=true mqtt-topic=camera/detections ...   MQTT Message Format (JSON):  The plugin expects JSON messages with the following structure:  { "timestamp": 1760334623.003448, "detections": [ {"class": "person", "class_index":56, "confidence": 0.95, "bbox":{"x":0.703,"y":0.469,"width":0.292,"height":0.474}}, {"class": "car", "class_index":56, "confidence": 0.95, "bbox":{"x":0.703,"y":0.469,"width":0.292,"height":0.474}} ] }   When detections contain a class, Recording startsWhen detections is empty, waits for det-timeout and then stops recording.If no messages received for det-timeout seconds, recording stops

searchDocs.title: det-timeout​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the timeout period after which the recording is supposed to stop if no detections are present.  Type: Double (Floating point)Default: 10.0Range: > 0.0 secondsAccess: Read/Write  note This property is effective only in Auto mode.  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API # Stop recording after 7 seconds of no detections gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctvrecord mode=1 det-timeout=7.0 ...

searchDocs.title: mqtt-client-id​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the client id with which the element is going to establish connection with the mqtt broker  Type: StringDefault: <element-name>-<pid>Access: Read/Write  note This property is useful only in Auto mode.  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctvrecord mode=1 mqtt-client-id="newelement" ...   note Apart from the specified properties, this plugin also contains some extra properties that are related to the sink architecture in gstreamer. All of them are not tested.

searchDocs.title: Common Properties​
searchDocs.content: These properties are available for both Vosk and Whisper engines.

searchDocs.title: model​
searchDocs.content: Description: Path to the speech recognition model.  Type: stringDefault:  Vosk: "/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15"Whisper: "/home/root/models/stt/whisper/ggml-tiny.en-q5_1.bin"  For Vosk: Path to model directory containing am/, conf/, graph/, and ivector/ subdirectories.  For Whisper: Path to GGML model file (.bin format).  gst-launchGObject Property # Vosk gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 ! ... # Whisper gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt model=/home/root/models/stt/whisper/ggml-tiny.en-q5_1.bin ! ...   Available Models:  Vosk:  Small: /home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 (~40MB, faster)Large: /home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-en-us-0.22-lgraph (~1.8GB, more accurate)  Whisper:  Tiny: /home/root/models/stt/whisper/ggml-tiny.en-q5_1.bin (~75MB, fastest)Additional models can be installed from Whisper.cpp or Hugging Face

searchDocs.title: Vosk Engine Properties​
searchDocs.content: These properties are only available when using the Vosk engine (compile-time selection).

searchDocs.title: partials​
searchDocs.content: Description: Enable or disable partial recognition results during speech processing.  Type: booleanDefault: trueAvailability: Vosk engine only  When enabled, the plugin sends intermediate recognition results as speech is being processed. When disabled, only final results (on speech pause) are sent.  note This property is not available with the Whisper engine. Whisper only produces final results.  gst-launchGObject Property # Enable partial results (default) gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt partials=true ! ... # Disable partial results (only finals) gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt partials=false ! ...   Use Cases:  Enabled: Real-time transcription, live captions, voice command confirmationDisabled: Final transcription only, reduced output, simpler result handling

searchDocs.title: Whisper Engine Properties​
searchDocs.content: These properties are only available when using the Whisper engine (compile-time selection).

searchDocs.title: threads​
searchDocs.content: Description: Number of CPU threads to use for processing.  Type: intRange: 1 - 32Default: 4  Higher thread counts can improve performance on multi-core systems but increase CPU usage. Adjust based on your hardware and performance requirements.  gst-launchGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt threads=8 ! ...

searchDocs.title: step-ms​
searchDocs.content: Description: Step size in milliseconds for audio processing window.  Type: intRange: 100 - 10000 msDefault: 3000 ms  Controls how often Whisper processes audio chunks. Smaller values give more frequent updates but higher CPU usage. Larger values reduce CPU usage but increase latency.  gst-launchGObject Property # Process every 2 seconds gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt step-ms=2000 ! ... # Process every 5 seconds gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt step-ms=5000 ! ...

searchDocs.title: length-ms​
searchDocs.content: Description: Length of audio buffer in milliseconds.  Type: intRange: 1000 - 30000 msDefault: 10000 ms  Defines the size of the audio buffer for processing. Larger buffers provide more context for better accuracy but increase latency. Should be >= step-ms.  gst-launchGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt length-ms=8000 ! ...

searchDocs.title: use-vad​
searchDocs.content: Description: Enable Voice Activity Detection.  Type: booleanDefault: false  When enabled, Whisper only processes audio when speech is detected, reducing CPU usage during silence periods. Recommended for continuous streaming applications.  gst-launchGObject Property # Enable VAD gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt use-vad=true ! ...

searchDocs.title: vad-threshold​
searchDocs.content: Description: VAD sensitivity threshold.  Type: floatRange: 0.0 - 1.0Default: 0.01  Lower values make VAD more sensitive (detect quieter speech), higher values require louder speech to trigger. Only effective when use-vad=true.  gst-launchGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt use-vad=true vad-threshold=0.02 ! ...

searchDocs.title: TCP Backend Properties​
searchDocs.content: Available only when compiled with -Dcomm_backend=tcp.

searchDocs.title: tcp-port​
searchDocs.content: Description: TCP port number for the JSON server.  Type: intRange: 1 - 65535Default: 9999  The plugin starts a TCP server on this port that clients can connect to for receiving recognition results in real-time.  gst-launchGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt tcp-port=8888 ! ...   Connect to TCP Server:  nc localhost 9999 # or telnet localhost 9999   JSON Output Format:  // Vosk - Final result { "text": "hello world" } // Vosk - Partial result (if partials=true) { "partial": "hello wor" } // Whisper - Result { "text": "hello world" }

searchDocs.title: MQTT Backend Properties​
searchDocs.content: Available only when compiled with -Dcomm_backend=mqtt.

searchDocs.title: mqtt-broker​
searchDocs.content: Description: MQTT broker hostname or IP address.  Type: stringDefault: "localhost"  gst-launchGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt mqtt-broker=192.168.1.100 ! ...

searchDocs.title: mqtt-port​
searchDocs.content: Description: MQTT broker port number.  Type: intRange: 1 - 65535Default: 1883  gst-launchGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt mqtt-port=1883 ! ...

searchDocs.title: mqtt-topic​
searchDocs.content: Description: MQTT topic to publish recognition results.  Type: stringDefault: "stt/results"  gst-launchGObject Property gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctstt mqtt-topic=camera1/stt ! ...   Subscribe to MQTT Results:  mosquitto_sub -h localhost -t stt/results -v

searchDocs.title: Whisper Engine Tuning​
searchDocs.content: For Real-time Applications:  threads=4 step-ms=2000 use-vad=true   For High Accuracy:  threads=8 length-ms=10000 step-ms=3000   For Low CPU Usage:  threads=2 use-vad=true vad-threshold=0.02

searchDocs.title: Vosk Engine Tuning​
searchDocs.content: For Low Latency:  Use partials=true for immediate feedbackUse small model for faster processing  For High Accuracy:  Use large model (vosk-model-en-us-0.22-lgraph)Set partials=false for cleaner final results
