searchDocs.content: # Remove any build directory if already present: rm -rf builddir/ # Setup build directory (default: MACH=opencv) meson setup builddir # Compile ninja -C builddir   Once the compilation is done, the following files among others should be generated in the builddir.  builddir/ # Build directory └── libgstdctoverlay.so # GStreamer plugin

searchDocs.title: Build Options​
searchDocs.content: The plugin supports multiple build configuration options:  Machine Layer Selection​  Since this plugin is implemented in a layered architecture, support for additional rendering backends can be added in mach/ layer of the plugin source. To build the plugin for a specific machine, issue the following command:  # Explicitly specify machine layer meson setup builddir -DMACH=<machine-name>

searchDocs.title: Running the examples​
searchDocs.content: The examples can be run in 2 ways. It can be run in the platform where the plugin and its test code were compiled. Or else, if the compilation was done for a different target platform, then you will have to load the plugins to that target machine.

searchDocs.title: 1. Run the example in the machine where it was compiled​
searchDocs.content: The plugins are output in the builddir directory. So provide the plugin path to Gstreamer before the example pipeline is run.  # Pipeline GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir gst-launch-1.0 ...

searchDocs.title: 2. Run the example in a target machine​
searchDocs.content: Upload the plugin to the target platform. Here, we use the adb utility.  # Push the plugin to the plugin directory adb push builddir/libgstdctoverlay.so /usr/lib/gstreamer-1.0/ # Verify installation adb shell gst-inspect-1.0 dctoverlay   note The examples shown here demonstrate usage on both host and target platforms.

searchDocs.title: Basic Detection Overlay​
searchDocs.content: The following example displays detection overlays with default styling.  # Start MQTT broker (in separate terminal) mosquitto -v # Run pipeline with overlay gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! \ video/x-raw,format=BGR ! \ dctoverlay mqtt-host=localhost mqtt-topic=detections ! \ videoconvert ! autovideosink   What it does:  Captures video from /dev/video8Converts to BGR formatReceives detection data via MQTT from detections topicDraws bounding boxes and labelsDisplays video with overlays

searchDocs.title: Custom Box and Font Styling​
searchDocs.content: The following example uses green boxes with yellow text.  gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! \ video/x-raw,format=BGR ! \ dctoverlay \ mqtt-host=localhost \ mqtt-topic=detections \ box-color-r=0 box-color-g=255 box-color-b=0 \ box-thickness=2 \ font-scale=0.6 \ font-color-r=255 font-color-g=255 font-color-b=0 \ font-thickness=2 ! \ videoconvert ! autovideosink   What it does:  Green bounding boxes (RGB: 0, 255, 0)Yellow text (RGB: 255, 255, 0)Box thickness: 2 pixelsFont scale: 0.6

searchDocs.title: Label Background Customization​
searchDocs.content: The following example adds semi-transparent black backgrounds to labels.  gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! \ video/x-raw,format=BGR ! \ dctoverlay \ mqtt-host=localhost \ mqtt-topic=detections \ draw-label-background=true \ label-bg-color-r=0 label-bg-color-g=0 label-bg-color-b=0 \ label-bg-alpha=0.7 \ label-position=0 ! \ videoconvert ! autovideosink   What it does:  Black label background (RGB: 0, 0, 0)70% opacity (alpha: 0.7)Labels positioned at top-left of boxes

searchDocs.title: Confidence Display Configuration​
searchDocs.content: The following example shows confidence scores with 2 decimal places.  gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! \ video/x-raw,format=BGR ! \ dctoverlay \ mqtt-host=localhost \ mqtt-topic=detections \ show-confidence=true \ confidence-decimals=2 ! \ videoconvert ! autovideosink   What it does:  Displays confidence scores in labelsShows 2 decimal places (e.g., "0.95")

searchDocs.title: ROI Visualization​
searchDocs.content: The following example draws a Region of Interest rectangle.  gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! \ video/x-raw,format=BGR ! \ dctoverlay \ mqtt-host=localhost \ mqtt-topic=detections \ enable-roi=true \ roi-x=100 roi-y=100 roi-width=400 roi-height=300 \ roi-color-r=255 roi-color-g=255 roi-color-b=0 \ roi-thickness=2 ! \ videoconvert ! autovideosink   What it does:  Draws yellow ROI rectangle (RGB: 255, 255, 0)ROI position: (100, 100) with 400x300 sizeROI thickness: 2 pixels

searchDocs.title: Class Filtering​
searchDocs.content: The following example only displays specific object classes.  gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! \ video/x-raw,format=BGR ! \ dctoverlay \ mqtt-host=localhost \ mqtt-topic=detections \ enable-class-filter=true \ filter-class-ids="0,1,2,5" ! \ videoconvert ! autovideosink   What it does:  Only draws detections for class IDs 0, 1, 2, and 5Filters out all other classes

searchDocs.title: Complete Configuration Example​
searchDocs.content: The following example demonstrates all customization options.  gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! \ video/x-raw,format=BGR ! \ dctoverlay \ mqtt-host=localhost \ mqtt-port=1883 \ mqtt-topic=detections \ mqtt-qos=1 \ box-color-r=0 box-color-g=255 box-color-b=0 \ box-thickness=2 \ font-type=0 \ font-scale=0.6 \ font-color-r=255 font-color-g=255 font-color-b=0 \ font-thickness=2 \ draw-label-background=true \ label-bg-color-r=0 label-bg-color-g=0 label-bg-color-b=0 \ label-bg-alpha=0.7 \ label-position=0 \ show-confidence=true \ confidence-decimals=2 \ enable-roi=true \ roi-x=100 roi-y=100 roi-width=400 roi-height=300 \ roi-color-r=255 roi-color-g=255 roi-color-b=0 \ roi-thickness=2 \ enable-class-filter=true \ filter-class-ids="0,1,2" ! \ videoconvert ! autovideosink

searchDocs.title: Publishing Detection Data via MQTT​
searchDocs.content: To test the overlay plugin, you need to publish detection data to MQTT. Here's an example Python script:  #!/usr/bin/env python3 import paho.mqtt.client as mqtt import json import time # Create MQTT client client = mqtt.Client() client.connect("localhost", 1883, 60) # Sample detection data detections = { "detections": [ { "bbox": {"x": 100, "y": 50, "width": 200, "height": 150}, "label": "person", "confidence": 0.95, "class_id": 0 }, { "bbox": {"x": 400, "y": 200, "width": 150, "height": 180}, "label": "car", "confidence": 0.87, "class_id": 2 } ] }

searchDocs.title: Debugging​
searchDocs.content: To enable detailed debug output from the plugin, set the GST_DEBUG environment variable before running the pipeline:  export GST_DEBUG=dctoverlay:5   After setting the debug level, run your pipeline to see detailed log messages:  GST_DEBUG=dctoverlay:5 gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! \ video/x-raw,format=BGR ! \ dctoverlay mqtt-host=localhost mqtt-topic=detections ! \ videoconvert ! autovideosink   Debug levels range from 0 (no output) to 5 (verbose logging). Level 5 provides the most detailed information for troubleshooting.  note If you encounter issues with the plugin: Verify MQTT broker is running: mosquitto -vCheck MQTT connection: mosquitto_sub -h localhost -t detectionsVerify video format is BGR (not RGB)Ensure all dependencies are properly installed

searchDocs.title: Verifying Installation​
searchDocs.content: # Check if plugin is installed gst-inspect-1.0 dctoverlay # Verify properties gst-inspect-1.0 dctoverlay | grep -A 5 "Plugin Details"

searchDocs.title: API Function Summary​
searchDocs.content: Function	Purpose	Modeapi_dctfcapture_init()	Initialize element from pipeline	All api_dctfcapture_set_mode()	Set capture mode	All api_dctfcapture_set_location()	Set output directory	All api_dctfcapture_set_prefix()	Set filename prefix	All api_dctfcapture_trigger()	Trigger single capture	MANUAL api_dctfcapture_set_time_period()	Set capture interval (seconds)	PERIODIC api_dctfcapture_set_mqtt_topic()	Set MQTT topic	AUTO api_dctfcapture_set_mqtt_host()	Set MQTT broker host	AUTO api_dctfcapture_set_mqtt_port()	Set MQTT broker port	AUTO api_dctfcapture_set_time_skip()	Set throttling (milliseconds)	AUTO api_dctfcapture_get_*()	Get current settings	All

searchDocs.title: Mode Comparison​
searchDocs.content: Feature	MANUAL	PERIODIC	AUTOCapture Trigger	API call	Periodic timer	MQTT message based Frequency	On-demand	Fixed interval (min 1 sec)	Event-driven

searchDocs.title: Usage Flow​
searchDocs.content: To use the plugin library you will need to follow the below sequence of operations.

searchDocs.title: Step 1: Pipeline Initialization​
searchDocs.content: Initialize a gstreamer pipeline with this plugin.  #include <apidctfcapture.h> GstElement *pipeline, *capture; // Initialize gst_init(&argc, &argv); pipeline = gst_parse_launch("videotestsrc ! ... ! dctfcapture name=cap ! ...", NULL);   note The plugin must have a name associated with it, which we will use to initialize the plugin api layer.

searchDocs.title: Step 2: Plugin Initialization​
searchDocs.content: Once the pipeline is initialized successfully, call the plugin initialization function to get the plugin element object.  With APIGST API // Initialize capture = api_dctfcapture_init(pipeline, "cap");

searchDocs.title: Step 3: Plugin Configuration​
searchDocs.content: Once the initialization is done, you can use the apis as needed.  With APIGST API // Configure api_dctfcapture_set_location(capture, "/tmp"); api_dctfcapture_set_prefix(capture, "dct_test"); api_dctfcapture_set_mode(capture, DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_PERIODIC); api_dctfcapture_set_time_period(capture, 5); // Start pipeline gst_element_set_state(pipeline, GST_STATE_PLAYING); // Manual trigger (in manual mode) api_dctfcapture_trigger(capture);

searchDocs.title: DctFCaptureModeAPI​
searchDocs.content: Defines the capture mode for the dctfcapture element.  typedef enum { DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_MANUAL = 0, // Manual capture mode DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_PERIODIC = 1 // Periodic capture mode DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_AUTO = 2 // Automatic capture mode } DctFCaptureModeAPI;   Value	DescriptionDCTFCAPTURE_MODE_MANUAL	Trigger capture manually via api_dctfcapture_trigger() DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_PERIODIC	Periodic capture at specified time intervals DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_AUTO	Automatic capture for specified reasons

searchDocs.title: Functions​
searchDocs.content: These functions provide a C interface for controlling frame capture from GStreamer pipelines. It supports both manual and periodic capture modes, allowing you to save JPEG images with configurable filenames and intervals.

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_init​
searchDocs.content: Initialize and retrieve the dctfcapture element from a GStreamer pipeline.  GstElement* api_dctfcapture_init(GstElement *pipeline, const char *element_name);   Parameters:  pipeline - GstElement pipeline containing the dctfcapture elementelement_name - Name of the dctfcapture element in the pipeline  Returns:  Pointer to dctfcapture element on successNULL on failure  Memory Management The caller is responsible for unreferencing the returned element using gst_object_unref() when done.  Example:  GstElement *pipeline = ...; // Your pipeline GstElement *capture = api_dctfcapture_init(pipeline, "mycapture"); if (capture) { // Use the capture element gst_object_unref(capture); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_set_mode​
searchDocs.content: Set the capture mode (manual, periodic or auto).  bool api_dctfcapture_set_mode(GstElement *element, DctFCaptureModeAPI mode);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElementmode - Capture mode (DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_MANUAL, DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_PERIODIC or DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_AUTO)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  // Set to manual mode api_dctfcapture_set_mode(capture, DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_MANUAL); // Set to periodic mode api_dctfcapture_set_mode(capture, DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_PERIODIC); // Set to auto mode api_dctfcapture_set_mode(capture, DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_AUTO);

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_set_location​
searchDocs.content: Set the directory where captured JPEG images will be saved.  bool api_dctfcapture_set_location(GstElement *element, const char *location);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElementlocation - Directory path for saving images  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  info Filenames are automatically generated with timestamps in the format: [prefix_]YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.jpg  Example:  api_dctfcapture_set_location(capture, "/home/user/captures");

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_set_prefix​
searchDocs.content: Set a prefix for captured image filenames.  bool api_dctfcapture_set_prefix(GstElement *element, const char *prefix);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElementprefix - Prefix string for filenames (optional, can be NULL)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Filename Format:  With prefix: <prefix>_YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.jpgWithout prefix: YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.jpg  Example:  api_dctfcapture_set_prefix(capture, "camera1"); // Results in: camera1_2025_10_07_14_30_25_123.jpg

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_set_time_period​
searchDocs.content: Set the time interval for periodic capture mode.  bool api_dctfcapture_set_time_period(GstElement *element, uint32_t time_period);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElementtime_period - Time period in seconds (valid range: 1-3600)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  note This setting only takes effect in DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_PERIODIC mode.  Example:  // Capture every 5 seconds api_dctfcapture_set_time_period(capture, 5);

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_set_mqtt_topic​
searchDocs.content: Set the MQTT topic to subscribe for object detection messages.  bool api_dctfcapture_set_mqtt_topic(GstElement *element, const char *mqtt_topic);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElementmqtt_topic - MQTT topic to subscribe for messages  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  note This setting only takes effect in DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_AUTO mode.  Example:  // Set the MQTT topic name to "object/detection" api_dctfcapture_set_mqtt_topic(capture, "object/detection");

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_set_mqtt_host​
searchDocs.content: Set the MQTT broker hostname or IP address.  bool api_dctfcapture_set_mqtt_host(GstElement *element, const char *mqtt_host);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElementmqtt_host - MQTT broker hostname or IP address (e.g., "192.168.1.100", "mqtt.example.com")  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  note This setting only takes effect in DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_AUTO mode. Default is "localhost". If already connected in AUTO mode, will automatically reconnect to the new host.  Example:  // Connect to remote MQTT broker api_dctfcapture_set_mqtt_host(capture, "192.168.1.100");

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_set_mqtt_port​
searchDocs.content: Set the MQTT broker port number.  bool api_dctfcapture_set_mqtt_port(GstElement *element, uint32_t mqtt_port);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElementmqtt_port - MQTT broker port number (valid range: 1-65535)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  note This setting only takes effect in DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_AUTO mode. Default is 1883. If already connected in AUTO mode, will automatically reconnect to the new port.  Example:  // Use default MQTT port api_dctfcapture_set_mqtt_port(capture, 1883);

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_set_time_skip​
searchDocs.content: Set the minimum time between captures in AUTO mode (throttling).  bool api_dctfcapture_set_time_skip(GstElement *element, uint32_t time_skip);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElementtime_skip - Minimum time between captures in milliseconds (valid range: 0-60000)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  note This setting only takes effect in DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_AUTO mode. Use 0 for no throttling (per-frame detection). Default is 500ms.  Example:  // Capture at most once every 100ms (10 fps max) api_dctfcapture_set_time_skip(capture, 100); // No throttling - capture every frame api_dctfcapture_set_time_skip(capture, 0);

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_trigger​
searchDocs.content: Manually trigger a single frame capture.  bool api_dctfcapture_trigger(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElement  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Mode Requirement This function only works in DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_MANUAL. The capture automatically resets after capturing the frame.  Example:  // Ensure manual mode is set api_dctfcapture_set_mode(capture, DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_MANUAL); // Trigger capture if (api_dctfcapture_trigger(capture)) { printf("Frame captured successfully\n"); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_get_mode​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current capture mode.  bool api_dctfcapture_get_mode(GstElement *element, DctFCaptureModeAPI *mode);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElementmode - Pointer to store the current mode  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  DctFCaptureModeAPI current_mode; if (api_dctfcapture_get_mode(capture, &current_mode)) { if (current_mode == DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_MANUAL) { printf("Manual mode\n"); } else { printf("Periodic mode\n"); } }

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_get_location​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current save directory location.  char* api_dctfcapture_get_location(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElement  Returns:  Current location string on successNULL on failure  Memory Management The caller must free() the returned string when done.  Example:  char *location = api_dctfcapture_get_location(capture); if (location) { printf("Save location: %s\n", location); free(location); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_get_prefix​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current filename prefix.  char* api_dctfcapture_get_prefix(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElement  Returns:  Current prefix string on successNULL if not set or on failure  Memory Management The caller must free() the returned string when done.  Example:  char *prefix = api_dctfcapture_get_prefix(capture); if (prefix) { printf("Filename prefix: %s\n", prefix); free(prefix); } else { printf("No prefix set\n"); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_get_time_period​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current time period for periodic capture.  bool api_dctfcapture_get_time_period(GstElement *element, uint32_t *time_period);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElementtime_period - Pointer to store the current time period  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  uint32_t period; if (api_dctfcapture_get_time_period(capture, &period)) { printf("Capture interval: %u seconds\n", period); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_get_mqtt_topic​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current MQTT topic.  bool api_dctfcapture_get_mqtt_topic(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElement  Returns:  Current topic string on successNULL if not set or on failure  Memory Management The caller must free() the returned string when done.  Example:  char *topic = api_dctfcapture_get_mqtt_topic(capture); if (prefix) { printf("MQTT Topic: %s\n", topic); free(topic); } else { printf("No topic set\n"); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_get_time_period​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current time period for periodic capture.  bool api_dctfcapture_get_time_period(GstElement *element, uint32_t *time_period);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElementtime_period - Pointer to store the current time period  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  uint32_t period; if (api_dctfcapture_get_time_period(capture, &period)) { printf("Capture interval: %u seconds\n", period); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_get_mqtt_host​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current MQTT broker hostname.  char* api_dctfcapture_get_mqtt_host(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElement  Returns:  Current MQTT host string on successNULL on failure  Memory Management The caller must free() the returned string when done.  Example:  char *host = api_dctfcapture_get_mqtt_host(capture); if (host) { printf("MQTT Broker Host: %s\n", host); free(host); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_get_mqtt_port​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current MQTT broker port number.  bool api_dctfcapture_get_mqtt_port(GstElement *element, uint32_t *mqtt_port);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElementmqtt_port - Pointer to store the current port number  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  uint32_t port; if (api_dctfcapture_get_mqtt_port(capture, &port)) { printf("MQTT Broker Port: %u\n", port); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctfcapture_get_time_skip​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current time skip (throttling) value for AUTO mode.  bool api_dctfcapture_get_time_skip(GstElement *element, uint32_t *time_skip);   Parameters:  element - dctfcapture GstElementtime_skip - Pointer to store the current time skip in milliseconds  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  uint32_t skip; if (api_dctfcapture_get_time_skip(capture, &skip)) { printf("Time skip: %u ms\n", skip); }

searchDocs.title: Usage Example​
searchDocs.content: Here's an example demonstrating the API usage:  #include "api_dctfcapture.h" int main(void) { GstElement *pipeline, *capture; // Initialize pipeline (your GStreamer pipeline setup) gst_init(&argc, &argv); pipeline = gst_parse_launch("videotestsrc ! ... ! dctfcapture name=mycapture ... ! ...", NULL); // Get capture element *capture = api_dctfcapture_init(pipeline, "mycapture"); if (!capture) { fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialize capture element\n"); return -1; } // Configure for periodic capture api_dctfcapture_set_mode(capture, DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_PERIODIC); api_dctfcapture_set_location(capture, "/tmp/captures"); api_dctfcapture_set_prefix(capture, "frame"); api_dctfcapture_set_time_period(capture, 10); // Every 10 seconds // Start pipeline... // Later: switch to manual mode api_dctfcapture_set_mode(capture, DCTFCAPTURE_MODE_MANUAL); // Capture on demand api_dctfcapture_trigger(capture); // Cleanup gst_object_unref(capture); return 0; }

searchDocs.content: GStreamer DocumentationPlugin Property

searchDocs.title: Basic Build (With MQTT Support)​
searchDocs.content: The dctvrecord plugin requires MQTT support to function properly for AUTO mode:  # Remove any build directory if already present: rm -rf builddir/ # Setup build directory with MQTT support meson setup builddir # Compile meson compile -C builddir   Once the compilation is done, the following files among other should be generated in the builddir.  builddir/ # Build directory ├── libapidctvrecord.a # Plugin API library ├── libgstdctvrecord.so # GStreamer plugin ├── selftest # Comprehensive automated test suite ├── test_api_dctvrecord # Interactive API test application (uses API wrapper) ├── test_gst_dctvrecord # Interactive GStreamer test application (uses g_object_set/get) └── mqtt_publisher # MQTT publisher utility for AUTO mode testing

searchDocs.title: Running the examples​
searchDocs.content: The examples can be run in 2 ways. It can be run in the platform where the plugin and its test code were compiled. Or else, if the compilation was done for a different target platform, then you will have to load the plugins and the examples to that target machine.

searchDocs.title: 1. Run the example/test in the machine where it was compiled​
searchDocs.content: The plugins and the test code are output in the builddir directory. So provide the plugin path to Gstreamer before the test and the example pipeline are run.  # Pipeline GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir gst-launch-1.0 ... # Test app GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/<test-app>

searchDocs.title: 2. Run the example/test in a target machine​
searchDocs.content: Upload the plugin and test app to the target platform. Here, we use the adb utility.  # Push the plugin to the plugin directory adb push builddir/libgstdctvrecord.so <plugin directory> # Eg: /usr/lib/gstreamer-1.0/ # Push the test apps to the execution directory adb push builddir/<test-app> /tmp/ # Enter the adb shell and execute them adb shell shell# /tmp/<test-app>   note The examples shown here are run on the Host PC itself, where the compilation was done. In order to build on a different target machine, you will need to cross compile after setting up the respective toolchain.

searchDocs.title: Usage Examples​
searchDocs.content: warning It is recommended to use dctvrecord inside a gstreamer application than using as a gst-launch argument in bash. Using it in application gives more user control to recording feature. If executing via gst-launch-1.0, ensure -eargument is added in pipeline to ensure EOS signal is passed into the pipeline when ctrl-C is pressed to stop the execution.

searchDocs.title: Manual Mode - Basic Recording​
searchDocs.content: Start and stop recording manually via property:  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir gst-launch-1.0 videotestsrc ! \ video/x-raw,format=I420,width=640,height=480,framerate=30/1 ! \ x264enc tune=zerolatency bitrate=2000 ! \ h264parse config-interval=-1 ! \ video/x-h264,stream-format=avc,alignment=au ! \ dctvrecord mode=0 location=/tmp/videos prefix=test recording=true -e   Output: /tmp/videos/test_2025_10_13_15_45_23_456.mp4  note Setting recording=true in the pipeline command-line starts recording immediately. To control recording dynamically, use the API or modify the property at runtime.

searchDocs.title: Manual Mode - Without Prefix​
searchDocs.content: GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir gst-launch-1.0 videotestsrc ! \ video/x-raw,format=I420,width=640,height=480,framerate=30/1 ! \ x264enc tune=zerolatency bitrate=2000 ! \ h264parse config-interval=-1 ! \ video/x-h264,stream-format=avc,alignment=au ! \ dctvrecord mode=0 location=/tmp/videos recording=true -e   Output: /tmp/videos/2025_10_13_15_46_12_789.mp4

searchDocs.title: AUTO Mode (MQTT-based Automatic Recording)​
searchDocs.content: note AUTO mode requires an MQTT broker running and a publisher sending detection messages. If using a remote MQTT broker, ensure that the broker has the capability to send messages to all ports (not just localhost as by default).  The following example runs in AUTO mode and automatically starts/stops recording based on object detection messages via MQTT:  # Start MQTT broker (in separate terminal) mosquitto -v # Run pipeline with AUTO mode (default broker: localhost:1883) GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir gst-launch-1.0 videotestsrc ! \ video/x-raw,format=I420,width=640,height=480,framerate=30/1 ! \ x264enc tune=zerolatency bitrate=2000 ! \ h264parse config-interval=-1 ! \ video/x-h264,stream-format=avc,alignment=au ! \ dctvrecord mode=1 mqtt-topic=detections/camera1 \ det-timeout=7.0 location=/tmp/videos prefix=auto auto-enable=true -e   To connect to a remote MQTT broker, specify host and port properties:  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir gst-launch-1.0 videotestsrc ! \ video/x-raw,format=I420,width=640,height=480,framerate=30/1 ! \ x264enc tune=zerolatency bitrate=2000 ! \ h264parse config-interval=-1 ! \ video/x-h264,stream-format=avc,alignment=au ! \ dctvrecord mode=1 host=192.168.1.100 port=1883 \ mqtt-topic=detections/camera1 det-timeout=7.0 \ location=/tmp/videos prefix=auto auto-enable=true -e   How it works:  Plugin connects to MQTT broker (default: localhost:1883, or specified host:port)Subscribes to topic: detections/camera1When detection messages arrive with objects in detections array: Recording startsWhen no detections for 7 seconds (det-timeout): Recording stopsIf MQTT connection lost for 5 seconds: Recording stops  MQTT Message Format (JSON):  { "timestamp": 1234567890.123456, "detections": [ { "class": "person", "class_index": 0, "confidence": 0.952, "bbox": {"x": 0.345, "y": 0.223, "width": 0.156, "height": 0.445} }, { "class": "car", "class_index": 2, "confidence": 0.874, "bbox": {"x": 0.678, "y": 0.512, "width": 0.234, "height": 0.167} } ] }   Output Files:  /tmp/videos/auto_2025_10_13_16_10_45_123.mp4 (recording 1)/tmp/videos/auto_2025_10_13_16_15_22_456.mp4 (recording 2)... (one file per recording session)

searchDocs.title: AUTO Mode - With Real Camera​
searchDocs.content: For production use with a real camera (e.g., v4l2):  # Using default localhost:1883 broker GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video0 ! \ video/x-raw,format=YUY2,width=1920,height=1080,framerate=30/1 ! \ videoconvert ! \ x264enc tune=zerolatency bitrate=5000 speed-preset=fast ! \ h264parse config-interval=-1 ! \ video/x-h264,stream-format=avc,alignment=au ! \ dctvrecord mode=1 mqtt-topic=detections/camera1 \ det-timeout=10.0 location=/home/user/recordings prefix=cam1 auto-enable=true -e # Using remote broker GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir gst-launch-1.0 v4l2src device=/dev/video0 ! \ video/x-raw,format=YUY2,width=1920,height=1080,framerate=30/1 ! \ videoconvert ! \ x264enc tune=zerolatency bitrate=5000 speed-preset=fast ! \ h264parse config-interval=-1 ! \ video/x-h264,stream-format=avc,alignment=au ! \ dctvrecord mode=1 host=192.168.1.50 port=1883 \ mqtt-topic=detections/camera1 det-timeout=10.0 \ location=/home/user/recordings prefix=cam1 auto-enable=true -e

searchDocs.title: Test Applications​
searchDocs.content: The plugin provides four test applications to validate functionality:

searchDocs.title: 1. Comprehensive Self-Test (selftest)​
searchDocs.content: Automated test suite that validates all plugin functionalities:  # Using Meson build GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/selftest   What it tests:  Manual mode recording with prefixManual mode multiple recording cyclesAuto mode recording with MQTT (with configurable host/port)Auto mode with auto-enable controlAuto mode multiple recording cyclesAPI get/set functions for all propertiesRuntime property modification  Requirements:  mosquitto broker must be running for AUTO mode tests: mosquitto -vTest files created in /tmp/dctvrecord_selftest/  MQTT Configuration:By default, the selftest connects to localhost:1883. To test with a different broker:  Modify the mqtt_broker and mqtt_port variables in the selftest source codeOr ensure your MQTT broker is accessible at localhost:1883  Output:The test suite provides detailed pass/fail results for each test case with color-coded output showing test progress and final summary.

searchDocs.title: 2. Interactive API Test (test_api_dctvrecord)​
searchDocs.content: Interactive test application demonstrating the API usage in both MANUAL and AUTO modes. This test uses the API wrapper functions.  # Using Meson build - with command-line arguments GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/test_api_dctvrecord [location] [prefix] [mode] # Using Meson build - interactive prompts GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/test_api_dctvrecord   Arguments:  location - Directory to save recordings (default: /tmp/dctvrecord_apitest)prefix - Filename prefix (default: apitest)mode - Recording mode: 0=MANUAL, 1=AUTO (default: 0)  MANUAL Mode Example:  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/test_api_dctvrecord /tmp/test cam1 0   Commands:  r - Start recordings - Stop recordingi - Show status (Shows the property values related to manual mode)h - Show helpq - Quit  AUTO Mode Example:  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/test_api_dctvrecord /tmp/test cam1 1   When started in AUTO mode, the application will interactively prompt for:  MQTT broker host (default: localhost)MQTT broker port (default: 1883)MQTT topic to subscribe to (no default - must be provided)Detection timeout in seconds (default: 10.0)  Commands:  e - Enable auto-recordingd - Disable auto-recordingi - Show status (Shows the property values related to AUTO mode including MQTT configuration)h - Show helpq - Quit  AUTO Mode Requirements:  mosquitto broker running: mosquitto -vMQTT publisher sending detections to the configured topicEnsure broker host and port are accessible

searchDocs.title: 3. Interactive GStreamer Test (test_gst_dctvrecord)​
searchDocs.content: Interactive test application demonstrating GStreamer API usage (g_object_set/g_object_get) in both MANUAL and AUTO modes. This test uses GStreamer's native property functions directly without the API wrapper layer.  # Using Meson build - with command-line arguments GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/test_gst_dctvrecord [location] [prefix] [mode] # Using Meson build - interactive prompts GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/test_gst_dctvrecord   Arguments:  location - Directory to save recordings (default: /tmp/dctvrecord_gsttest)prefix - Filename prefix (default: gsttest)mode - Recording mode: 0=MANUAL, 1=AUTO (default: 0)  MANUAL Mode Example:  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/test_gst_dctvrecord /tmp/test cam1 0   Commands:  r - Start recordings - Stop recordingi - Show status (Shows the property values related to manual mode)h - Show helpq - Quit  AUTO Mode Example:  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/test_gst_dctvrecord /tmp/test cam1 1   When started in AUTO mode, the application will interactively prompt for:  MQTT broker host (default: localhost)MQTT broker port (default: 1883)MQTT topic to subscribe to (no default - must be provided)Detection timeout in seconds (default: 10.0)  Commands:  e - Enable auto-recordingd - Disable auto-recordingi - Show status (Shows the property values related to AUTO mode including MQTT configuration)h - Show helpq - Quit  AUTO Mode Requirements:  mosquitto broker running: mosquitto -vMQTT publisher sending detections to the configured topicEnsure broker host and port are accessible  Key Difference from test_api_dctvrecord:  Uses g_object_set() and g_object_get() directlyDemonstrates how to use the plugin without the API wrapperShows GStreamer function calls in log messagesUseful for understanding low-level GStreamer property manipulation

searchDocs.title: 4. MQTT Publisher Utility (mqtt_publisher)​
searchDocs.content: Interactive MQTT publisher that simulates object detection messages for testing AUTO mode:  # Using Meson build ./builddir/mqtt_publisher <topic> [broker_host] [broker_port]   Examples:  # For test_api_dctvrecord in AUTO mode ./builddir/mqtt_publisher apitest/detections # Custom broker and port ./builddir/mqtt_publisher mytest/detections localhost 1883   Controls:  SPACE - Toggle detections ON/OFFCtrl+C - Quit  Message Format:Publishes JSON messages every 1 second:  { "timestamp": 1234567890.123456, "detections": [ { "class": "person", "class_index": 0, "confidence": 0.952, "bbox": {"x": 0.345, "y": 0.223, "width": 0.156, "height": 0.445} }, { "class": "car", "class_index": 2, "confidence": 0.874, "bbox": {"x": 0.678, "y": 0.512, "width": 0.234, "height": 0.167} } ] }   When detections are ON: dctvrecord with AUTO mode enabled will START recording. When detections are OFF (empty array): dctvrecord will STOP recording after det-timeout expires.

searchDocs.title: Complete AUTO Mode Testing Workflow​
searchDocs.content: Terminal 1: Start the test application in AUTO mode (using API wrapper)  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/test_api_dctvrecord /tmp/test apitest 1 # When prompted, enter: # - MQTT broker host: localhost (or press Enter for default) # - MQTT broker port: 1883 (or press Enter for default) # - MQTT topic: apitest/detections # - Detection timeout: 5.0 (or press Enter for default 10.0) # Press 'e' to enable auto-recording   Alternative - Using GStreamer API directly:  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/test_gst_dctvrecord /tmp/test gsttest 1 # Enter the same MQTT configuration when prompted # Press 'e' to enable auto-recording   Terminal 2: Run the MQTT publisher  # For test_api_dctvrecord ./builddir/mqtt_publisher apitest/detections # For test_gst_dctvrecord ./builddir/mqtt_publisher gsttest/detections # Press SPACE to start sending detections   Expected Behavior:  When detections are published (non-empty detections array), recording starts automaticallyWhen no detections are published (empty detections array), recording stops after det-timeout secondsFiles are saved in /tmp/test/ with respective prefix: apitest_YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.mp4 (for test_api_dctvrecord)gsttest_YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.mp4 (for test_gst_dctvrecord)

searchDocs.title: MQTT Communication Dependencies (Required)​
searchDocs.content: The dctvrecord plugin requires MQTT support for AUTO mode functionality:  Mosquitto MQTT client library (libmosquitto-dev)Mosquitto broker (for testing)  Install on Ubuntu/Debian:  sudo apt-get install libmosquitto-dev mosquitto mosquitto-clients   note MQTT dependencies are required for AUTO mode (mode=1) which enables event-driven automatic recording based on object detection messages.

searchDocs.title: Plugin Not Found​
searchDocs.content: If you get "no such element 'dctvrecord'" error:  # Check if plugin is in the path export GST_PLUGIN_PATH=/path/to/builddir:$GST_PLUGIN_PATH # Or for Makefile build export GST_PLUGIN_PATH=/path/to/build/lib:$GST_PLUGIN_PATH # Verify plugin is loaded gst-inspect-1.0 dctvrecord

searchDocs.title: MQTT Connection Issues​
searchDocs.content: If AUTO mode fails to connect:  Ensure mosquitto broker is running: mosquitto -v Check broker logs for connection attempts Verify topic name matches between publisher and plugin Check firewall settings if using remote broker

searchDocs.title: Recording Not Starting​
searchDocs.content: For AUTO mode:  Verify auto-enable=true is setEnsure mqtt-topic is configuredCheck that detection messages are being publishedVerify JSON message format matches expected structure  For MANUAL mode:  Ensure mode=0 is setSet recording=true to start

searchDocs.title: Permission Issues​
searchDocs.content: If files can't be written:  # Ensure directory exists and is writable mkdir -p /tmp/videos chmod 777 /tmp/videos # Or use a directory you own dctvrecord location=$HOME/videos ...

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.content: The plugin library is organized into different layers.  GST Layer - The GST layer has the main Gstreamer related functionalities. However, the functional tasks which can be offloaded to different hardware is kept in the machine layer. Machine Layer - This is the layer where machine specific operations are implemented. This is done to port the plugin easily to different platforms. Currently supports OpenCV rendering backends. API Layer - The API layer is a wrapper layer using which the user can configure the gstreamer plugin. This is not part of the gstreamer framework. Instead of the API layer, the user can use gstreamer's APIs directly too. Communication Layer - This layer handles the communication of the plugin to the external world. It receives object detection data via MQTT and forwards it to the rendering layer.

searchDocs.title: Folder Structure​
searchDocs.content: The corresponding folder structure is as follows:  inc/ # Header files ├── gst/ # GStreamer layer (plugin interface) ├── mach/ # Machine layer (rendering backends) ├── comm/ # Communication layer (MQTT integration) └── api/ # API layer (C interface) src/ # Source files ├── gst/ # GStreamer implementation ├── mach/ # Machine implementations ├── comm/ # Communication implementation └── api/ # API implementation

searchDocs.title: dctoverlay (Detection Overlay Transform)​

Capabilities:  Input: video/x-raw, format={ RGB, BGR }Output: video/x-raw, format={ RGB, BGR }  Key Functions:  Receives detection data via MQTTDraws bounding boxes with customizable colors and thicknessRenders labels with configurable fonts and backgroundsSupports ROI (Region of Interest) visualization with multiple display modesDisplays tracking IDs for tracked objectsShows coordinate system origin markerOptional bounding box background fill with transparency

searchDocs.title: Overview​
searchDocs.content: The dctfcapture plugin uses a multi-layer architecture:   ┌─────────────────────────────────────┐ │ API Layer (C API) │ - Public C interface │ inc/api/ + src/api/ │ - Application-friendly functions └─────────────────+───────────────────┘ │ ┌─────────────────+───────────────────┐ │ GST Layer (GStreamer) │ - GStreamer plugin interface │ inc/gst/ + src/gst/ │ - Property management └─────────────────+───────────────────┘ - Pipeline integration │ .---------------------+----------------------. | | ┌─────────────────+───────────────────┐ ┌───────────────────+─────────────────┐ │ COMM Layer (Communication) │ │ MACH Layer (Processing) │ │ inc/comm/ + src/comm/ │ │ inc/mach/ + src/mach/ │ └─────────────────────────────────────┘ └─────────────────────────────────────┘ - Communication - Format conversion - MQTT - JPEG encoding - Platform-specific   The MACH layer is designed to be modular and swappable, allowing different implementations for:  Software implementation (MACH_GENERIC): Uses OpenCV for conversionHardware acceleration (MACH_HW, MACH_NVJPEG, etc.): Uses platform-specific APIs

searchDocs.title: Prerequisites​
searchDocs.content: Before adding a new machine layer, ensure you understand:  Machine Layer Interface: All implementations must follow the interface defined in inc/mach/mach_generic.hGStreamer Video Formats: RGB, I420, UYVY supportJPEG Encoding: Your platform's JPEG encoding APIBuild System: Meson build configuration

searchDocs.title: Step 1: Choose a Machine Name​
searchDocs.content: Pick a descriptive name for your machine implementation. Examples:  MACH_GENERIC - Software implementation (already exists)MACH_HW - Generic hardware accelerationMACH_NVJPEG - NVIDIA NVJPEG accelerationMACH_VAAPI - Intel VAAPI accelerationMACH_V4L2 - V4L2 hardware encoding  For this guide, we'll use MACH_HW as an example.

searchDocs.title: Step 2: Create Header File​
searchDocs.content: Create a new header file in inc/mach/ that follows the same interface as mach_generic.h.  File: inc/mach/mach_hw.h  #ifndef __MACH_HW_H__ #define __MACH_HW_H__ #ifdef MACH_HW #include <gst/video/video.h> #include <stdint.h> #include <stdbool.h> #ifdef __cplusplus extern "C" { #endif /** * @brief Machine layer context structure for fcapture (HW implementation) * * This is opaque to the GST layer. Add platform-specific handles here. */ typedef struct _MachFCaptureContext MachFCaptureContext; /** * @brief Initialize machine layer context for fcapture * * @return MachFCaptureContext* Pointer to machine context, or NULL on failure */ MachFCaptureContext* machfcapture_init(void); /** * @brief Cleanup machine layer context for fcapture * * @param ctx Machine context */ void machfcapture_cleanup(MachFCaptureContext *ctx); /** * @brief Convert and save frame as JPEG using hardware acceleration * * This function handles: * - Format conversion (RGB/I420/UYVY to required format) * - Hardware-accelerated JPEG encoding * - File writing * * @param ctx Machine context * @param video_info GStreamer video info structure * @param buffer GStreamer buffer containing the frame * @param output_path Output file path for JPEG * @param quality JPEG quality (1-100) * @return bool true on success, false on failure */ bool machfcapture_convert_and_save_jpeg( MachFCaptureContext *ctx, GstVideoInfo *video_info, GstBuffer *buffer, const char *output_path, int quality ); /** * @brief Get machine layer implementation name for fcapture * * @return const char* Implementation name (e.g., "Hardware-NVJPEG") */ const char* machfcapture_get_implementation_name(void); /** * @brief Check if hardware acceleration is available for fcapture * * @return bool true if HW acceleration is used, false for software */ bool machfcapture_is_hw_accelerated(void); #ifdef __cplusplus } #endif #endif /* MACH_HW */ #endif /* __MACH_HW_H__ */   Key Points:  Keep the same function signatures as mach_generic.hWrap everything in #ifdef MACH_HW guardsThe context structure can contain platform-specific handles internally

searchDocs.title: Step 3: Create Implementation File​
searchDocs.content:
Create the implementation file in src/mach/.  File: src/mach/mach_hw.cpp (or .c if pure C)  #include "mach_hw.h" #ifdef MACH_HW #include <gst/video/video.h> #include <stdio.h> #include <string.h> // Include your platform-specific headers here // #include <nvjpeg.h> // #include <cuda_runtime.h> /* Machine layer log tag */ #define MACH_LOG_TAG "[FCAPTURE_MACH_HW]" /* Machine context for hardware implementation */ struct _MachFCaptureContext { // Add platform-specific handles here // Example for NVJPEG: // nvjpegHandle_t nvjpeg_handle; // cudaStream_t stream; int initialized; }; /** * Initialize machine layer context for hardware acceleration */ MachFCaptureContext* machfcapture_init(void) { MachFCaptureContext *ctx = (MachFCaptureContext*)malloc(sizeof(MachFCaptureContext)); if (!ctx) { fprintf(stderr, "%s Error: Failed to allocate context
", MACH_LOG_TAG); return NULL; } // Initialize your hardware acceleration here // Example: // nvjpegStatus_t status = nvjpegCreateSimple(&ctx->nvjpeg_handle); // if (status != NVJPEG_STATUS_SUCCESS) { // fprintf(stderr, "%s Error: Failed to create NVJPEG handle
", MACH_LOG_TAG); // free(ctx); // return NULL; // } ctx->initialized = 1; fprintf(stderr, "%s Info: Hardware acceleration initialized
", MACH_LOG_TAG); return ctx; } /** * Cleanup machine layer context */ void machfcapture_cleanup(MachFCaptureContext *ctx) { if (ctx) { if (ctx->initialized) { // Cleanup hardware resources // Example: // nvjpegDestroy(ctx->nvjpeg_handle); } free(ctx); } } /** * Convert GStreamer frame to JPEG using hardware acceleration */ bool machfcapture_convert_and_save_jpeg( MachFCaptureContext *ctx, GstVideoInfo *video_info, GstBuffer *buffer, const char *output_path, int quality) { GstVideoFrame frame; if (!ctx || !ctx->initialized) { fprintf(stderr, "%s Error: Context not initialized
", MACH_LOG_TAG); return false; } if (!video_info || !buffer || !output_path) { fprintf(stderr, "%s Error: NULL parameter
", MACH_LOG_TAG); return false; } /* Map the GStreamer video frame */ if (!gst_video_frame_map(&frame, video_info, buffer, GST_MAP_READ)) { fprintf(stderr, "%s Error: Failed to map video frame
", MACH_LOG_TAG); return false; } int width = GST_VIDEO_FRAME_WIDTH(&frame); int height = GST_VIDEO_FRAME_HEIGHT(&frame); GstVideoFormat format = GST_VIDEO_FRAME_FORMAT(&frame); // TODO: Implement your hardware-accelerated conversion and encoding here // // General steps: // 1. Convert GStreamer format to your HW-required format // 2. Upload data to hardware (if needed, e.g., GPU) // 3. Perform JPEG encoding using HW API // 4. Download result (if needed) // 5. Write to file // // Example pseudocode for NVJPEG: // - Convert I420/RGB/UYVY to the format NVJPEG expects // - Call nvjpegEncode() // - Write encoded data to output_path bool result = false; // Your implementation here fprintf(stderr, "%s Error: Hardware encoding not yet implemented
", MACH_LOG_TAG); gst_video_frame_unmap(&frame); return result; } /** * Get implementation name */ const char* machfcapture_get_implementation_name(void) { return "Hardware-Accelerated"; // Customize based on your platform } /** * Check if hardware accelerated */ bool machfcapture_is_hw_accelerated(void) { return true; // Hardware implementation } #endif /* MACH_HW */   Implementation Guidelines:  Error Handling: Use MACH_LOG_TAG for consistent loggingFormat Support: Handle RGB, I420, and UYVY formatsQuality Parameter: Map the 1-100 quality to your HW APIMemory Management: Clean up all resources in machfcapture_cleanup()Thread Safety: Consider if your HW API requires thread protection

searchDocs.title: Step 4: Update Machine Layer Header Selector​
searchDocs.content: Update inc/mach/mach_fcapture.h to include your new header.  File: inc/mach/mach_fcapture.h  #ifndef __MACH_FCAPTURE_H__ #define __MACH_FCAPTURE_H__ /** * @file mach_fcapture.h * @brief Machine layer abstraction for fcapture * * This header includes the appropriate machine-specific implementation * based on the MACH macro defined at build time. * * Supported MACH values: * - MACH_GENERIC: Generic software implementation using OpenCV (default) * - MACH_HW: Hardware-accelerated implementation */ /* Include machine-specific implementation based on MACH macro */ #if defined(MACH_GENERIC) #include "mach_generic.h" #elif defined(MACH_HW) #include "mach_hw.h" #else #error "No MACH type defined. Please define MACH_GENERIC or MACH_HW" #endif #endif /* __MACH_FCAPTURE_H__ */

searchDocs.title: Step 5: Update Meson Build Configuration​
searchDocs.content: Modify meson.build to support building with your new machine layer.  File: meson.build  # Machine layer selection option valid_mach_options = [ 'MACH_GENERIC', 'MACH_HW', # Add your new option here ] # Add new machine types here   And update the machine sources section:  # Plugin sources mach_sources = [ 'src/mach/mach_generic.cpp', 'src/mach/mach_hw.cpp', # Add your new source file ] # Add new machine types' source here   Optional: Add platform-specific dependencies if needed:  # Get dependencies based on machine type mach_option = get_option('mach') mach_deps = [] if mach_option == 'MACH_HW' # Add hardware-specific dependencies # Example: NVJPEG # nvjpeg_dep = dependency('nvjpeg', required: true) # mach_deps += nvjpeg_dep # Or custom library paths # mach_deps += declare_dependency( # link_args: ['-L/usr/local/cuda/lib64', '-lnvjpeg'], # include_directories: include_directories('/usr/local/cuda/include') # ) endif   Then update the plugin library build section:  # Build the plugin as a shared library gstdctfcapture = library(plugin_name, plugin_sources, include_directories : inc_dirs, cpp_args : plugin_cpp_args, dependencies : [gst_dep, gst_base_dep, gst_video_dep, opencv_dep] + mach_deps, # Add mach_deps install : true, install_dir : get_option('libdir') / 'gstreamer-1.0', )

searchDocs.title: Step 6: Update Meson Options (Optional)​
searchDocs.content: If you want to add specific build options for your machine layer, update meson_options.txt:  option('mach', type : 'string', value : 'MACH_GENERIC', description : 'Machine layer implementation (MACH_GENERIC, MACH_HW ...)') # Optional: Add hardware-specific options option('hw_encoder_path', type : 'string', value : '', description : 'Custom path to hardware encoder library')

searchDocs.title: Step 7: Build and Test​
searchDocs.content: Now build your new machine layer:  # Clean previous build rm -rf builddir # Configure with your new machine layer meson setup builddir -Dmach=MACH_HW # Compile meson compile -C builddir # Publish the executable and libraries to the target device. # This will be machine/platform specific. # In the target device, run self-test GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir ./builddir/selftest

searchDocs.title: Step 8: Verify Integration​
searchDocs.content: Test your implementation with different scenarios:  1. Manual Mode Test​  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir gst-launch-1.0 videotestsrc num-buffers=1 ! \ video/x-raw,format=I420,width=640,height=480 ! \ dctfcapture location=/tmp prefix=hw_test mode=0 capture=true ! \ fakesink   2. Periodic Mode Test​  GST_PLUGIN_PATH=builddir gst-launch-1.0 videotestsrc ! \ video/x-raw,format=I420,width=640,height=480 ! \ dctfcapture mode=1 time-period=2 location=/tmp prefix=hw_periodic ! \ fakesink   3. All Formats Test​  Test with RGB, I420, and UYVY formats to ensure your implementation handles all supported formats.

searchDocs.title: 1. Format Conversion Issues​
searchDocs.content: Problem: Hardware encoders may not support all GStreamer formats directlySolution: Implement format conversion in software before hardware encoding, or use hardware-accelerated converters if available

searchDocs.title: 2. Memory Management​
searchDocs.content: Problem: Leaking hardware resources (GPU memory, encoder handles)Solution: Ensure machfcapture_cleanup() frees ALL allocated resources

searchDocs.title: 3. Threading​
searchDocs.content: Problem: Hardware APIs may not be thread-safeSolution: Add mutex protection if needed, or ensure single-threaded access

searchDocs.title: 4. Error Handling​
searchDocs.content: Problem: Silent failures make debugging difficultSolution: Always use MACH_LOG_TAG for error messages and return false on failure

searchDocs.title: 5. Build Dependencies​
searchDocs.content: Problem: Missing platform-specific libraries at build timeSolution: Document all required dependencies and update meson.build accordingly

searchDocs.title: Features​
searchDocs.content: Offline Speech Recognition: No internet connection required, all processing happens locally using VoskWake Word Detection: Trigger phrase ("Mantis") activation for command listeningFuzzy Matching: Tolerant command matching using Levenshtein distance algorithmMultiple Communication Backends: Send commands via TCP, MQTT, or console outputConfigurable Commands: JSON-based command definitions with multiple phrase variantsGrammar Support: Custom keyword grammar for improved recognition accuracyHot Reload: Reload command definitions without restarting (SIGUSR2)Low Latency: Real-time audio processing with ALSA integrationResource Efficient: Suitable for embedded ARM64 systems

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.content: The application follows a multi-threaded architecture with two main components:

searchDocs.title: 1. ALSA Capture Thread​
searchDocs.content: Captures audio from microphone at 16kHz stereoConverts stereo to monoBuffers audio in thread-safe queueHandles PCM underruns and errors

searchDocs.title: 2. Vosk Processing Thread​
searchDocs.content: Consumes audio from queuePerforms speech recognition using Vosk modelDetects trigger phrase ("Mantis")Matches commands using fuzzy logicSends commands via TCP socket

searchDocs.title: Communication Flow​
searchDocs.content: ┌─────────────┐ │ Microphone │ └──────┬──────┘ │ ALSA Capture (16kHz Stereo) ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Audio Queue │ (Thread-safe) └──────┬──────────┘ │ Mono PCM ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Vosk Engine │ └──────┬──────────┘ │ JSON Results ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Trigger Monitor │ (5-second window) └──────┬──────────┘ │ Wake word detected ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ Command Matcher │ (Fuzzy matching) └──────┬──────────┘ │ Matched command ▼ ┌─────────────────┐ │ TCP Client │ → Send to device (localhost:6975) └─────────────────┘

searchDocs.content: Defines voice commands and their phrase variants:  { "commands": [ { "phrases": [ "zoom in", "zoom in please", "increase zoom", "magnify" ], "command": "zoom_in" }, { "phrases": [ "zoom out", "zoom out please", "decrease zoom", "reduce zoom" ], "command": "zoom_out" }, { "phrases": [ "black hot", "switch to black hot", "set black hot", "black hot mode" ], "command": "set_mode_black_hot" }, { "phrases": [ "white hot", "switch to white hot", "set white hot", "white hot mode" ], "command": "set_mode_white_hot" } ] }   Structure:  commands (array): List of command definitionsphrases (array): Multiple ways to say the commandcommand (string): The actual command string to send

searchDocs.title: Voice Command Workflow​
searchDocs.content: Start Application ./voice_command # Output: VOICE COMMAND SYSTEM RUNNING Say Wake Word You: "Mantis" App: *** MANTIS DETECTED - 5s WINDOW ACTIVE *** Give Command (within 5 seconds) You: "Zoom in" App: [MATCH] ✓ Exact: "zoom in" App: [COMMAND] ✓ Sending: zoom_in App: [COMMAND] ✓ Success Window Expires (if no command given) App: *** WINDOW EXPIRED ***

searchDocs.title: Example Session​
searchDocs.content: === Voice Command System (Mantis) === Configuration: ALSA Device: default Vosk Model: /home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 Keywords File: keywords.txt Commands File: commands.json Command Server: 127.0.0.1:6975 Trigger Phrase: "mantis" Trigger Window: 5000 ms [COMMANDS] Loading from commands.json [COMMANDS] ✓ Loaded: zoom in (+3 variants) → zoom_in [COMMANDS] ✓ Loaded: zoom out (+3 variants) → zoom_out [COMMANDS] ✓ Loaded: black hot (+3 variants) → set_mode_black_hot [COMMANDS] ✓ Loaded: white hot (+3 variants) → set_mode_white_hot [COMMANDS] Successfully loaded 4 commands [VOSK] Recognized: "mantis" ============================================================ [TRIGGER] *** MANTIS DETECTED - 5s WINDOW ACTIVE *** ============================================================ [VOSK] Recognized: "zoom in please" [MATCH] Input: "zoom in please" [MATCH] Normalized: "zoom in" [MATCH] ✓ Exact: "zoom in please" [COMMAND] ✓ Sending: zoom_in [COMMAND] ✓ Success [TRIGGER] Window closed

searchDocs.title: Hot Reload Commands​
searchDocs.content: Reload command definitions without restarting:  # Get PID cat /tmp/voice_command.pid # Send reload signal kill -USR2 $(cat /tmp/voice_command.pid) # Or directly killall -USR2 voice_command   The application will reload commands.json and keywords.txt and rebuild the grammar.

searchDocs.title: Command Matching Algorithm​
searchDocs.content: The application uses a two-stage matching process:

searchDocs.title: Stage 1: Exact Match​
searchDocs.content: Normalize input (lowercase, trim)Remove filler words ("the", "a", "please", etc.)Compare with all command phrasesReturn match if found

searchDocs.title: Stage 2: Fuzzy Match (Levenshtein Distance)​
searchDocs.content: Calculate edit distance for all phrasesAllow up to 20% differenceReturn best match within tolerance  Example:  Input: "zom in pleas" Normalized: "zom in" Best Match: "zoom in" (distance: 1) Threshold: 20% of 7 chars = 1.4 Result: MATCH ✓

searchDocs.title: Command Server Implementation​
searchDocs.content:
The voice command app sends commands to localhost:6975 by default. Implement a TCP server in your application to receive commands:  Python Example:  import socket import threading def command_handler(conn, addr): print(f"Connection from {addr}") while True: data = conn.recv(1024) if not data: break command = data.decode('utf-8').strip() print(f"Received command: {command}") # Process command if command == "zoom_in": print("Executing: Zoom In") elif command == "zoom_out": print("Executing: Zoom Out") elif command == "set_mode_black_hot": print("Executing: Black Hot Mode") elif command == "set_mode_white_hot": print("Executing: White Hot Mode") conn.close() # Start server server = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) server.bind(('127.0.0.1', 6975)) server.listen(5) print("Command server listening on port 6975") while True: conn, addr = server.accept() threading.Thread(target=command_handler, args=(conn, addr)).start()   C Example:  #include <sys/socket.h> #include <netinet/in.h> #include <stdio.h> #include <string.h> #include <unistd.h> int start_command_server(int port) { int server_fd, client_fd; struct sockaddr_in addr; char buffer[256]; server_fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_STREAM, 0); addr.sin_family = AF_INET; addr.sin_addr.s_addr = INADDR_ANY; addr.sin_port = htons(port); bind(server_fd, (struct sockaddr*)&addr, sizeof(addr)); listen(server_fd, 5); printf("Command server listening on port %d
", port); while (1) { client_fd = accept(server_fd, NULL, NULL); ssize_t n = recv(client_fd, buffer, sizeof(buffer)-1, 0); if (n > 0) { buffer[n] = '\0'; printf("Received command: %s
", buffer); // Process command if (strcmp(buffer, "zoom_in
") == 0) { // Execute zoom in } else if (strcmp(buffer, "zoom_out
") == 0) { // Execute zoom out } } close(client_fd); } return 0; }

searchDocs.title: Systemd Service​
searchDocs.content: Create /etc/systemd/system/voice-command.service:  [Unit] Description=Voice Command Service After=network.target sound.target [Service] Type=simple User=root WorkingDirectory=/usr/share/sentinel-sdk/voice_command ExecStart=/usr/share/sentinel-sdk/voice_command/voice_command \ --vosk-model /home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 \ --device default \ --command-host 127.0.0.1 \ --command-port 6975 Restart=on-failure RestartSec=5 [Install] WantedBy=multi-user.target   Enable and start:  sudo systemctl daemon-reload sudo systemctl enable voice-command sudo systemctl start voice-command sudo systemctl status voice-command

searchDocs.title: Auto-Start on Boot​
searchDocs.content: Add to /etc/rc.local:  #!/bin/sh cd /usr/share/sentinel-sdk/voice_command ./voice_command --vosk-model /home/root/models/stt/vosk/vosk-model-small-en-us-0.15 & exit 0

searchDocs.title: Configuration APIs​
searchDocs.content: Tracking Enable/Disable​  void ai_obj_trk_enable(); void ai_obj_trk_disable(); bool ai_obj_trk_is_enabled() const;   Enable or disable object tracking. When disabled, calculatePanTiltCommand() returns invalid commands.    Resolution Configuration​  void ai_obj_trk_set_model_resolution(int width, int height); void ai_obj_trk_set_display_resolution(int width, int height); void ai_obj_trk_set_resolutions(int model_width, int model_height, int display_width, int display_height);   Configure the resolution settings. The tracker automatically converts coordinates between model and display space.  Parameters:  width, height: Resolution dimensions in pixelsmodel_width, model_height: Model resolution dimensionsdisplay_width, display_height: Display resolution dimensions    Target Selection​  bool ai_obj_trk_set_target_id(int id); int ai_obj_trk_get_target_id() const; bool ai_obj_trk_set_by_coordinate(float x, float y);   Select which object to track. You can select by tracking ID or by clicking coordinates.  Parameters:  id: Tracking ID of the object to followx, y: Display coordinates (the closest object to these coordinates will be selected)  Returns: true if target was set successfully    Tracking Mode​  bool ai_obj_trk_set_mode(TrackingMode mode); TrackingMode ai_obj_trk_get_mode() const;   Set the tracking mode: CENTROID (keep object at center) or ROI (keep object within ROI bounds).  Parameters:  mode: Either TrackingMode::CENTROID or TrackingMode::ROI  Returns: true if mode was set successfully    ROI Configuration​  bool ai_obj_trk_set_roi(float x, float y, float width, float height); ROI ai_obj_trk_get_roi() const;   Configure the Region of Interest for ROI tracking mode.  Parameters:  x, y: Top-left corner coordinates (in display space)width, height: ROI dimensions  Returns: true if ROI was set successfully    PID Tuning​  void ai_obj_trk_set_pid_gains(float pan_kp, float pan_ki, float pan_kd, float tilt_kp, float tilt_ki, float tilt_kd); void ai_obj_trk_reset_pid_controllers(); void ai_obj_trk_set_pid_limits(float min_output, float max_output); void ai_obj_trk_set_filtering_params(float deadband_threshold, float smoothing_factor);   Fine-tune PID controller parameters for optimal tracking performance.  Parameters:  pan_kp, tilt_kp: Proportional gains (default: 0.10)pan_ki, tilt_ki: Integral gains (default: 0.001)pan_kd, tilt_kd: Derivative gains (default: 0.015)min_output, max_output: Output limits (default: -60.0, 60.0)deadband_threshold: Minimum error to generate command (default: 0.05)smoothing_factor: Output smoothing factor 0-1 (default: 0.8)

searchDocs.title: DetectedObject​
searchDocs.content: Represents a detected and tracked object.  struct DetectedObject { int id; // Object tracking ID float x, y; // Center coordinates float width, height; // Bounding box dimensions float confidence; // Detection confidence (0.0 to 1.0) };   Fields:  id: Unique tracking ID (persistent across frames)x, y: Object center coordinates in model resolutionwidth, height: Bounding box dimensionsconfidence: Detection confidence score (0.0 = 0%, 1.0 = 100%)

searchDocs.title: FrameResolution​
searchDocs.content: Defines frame dimensions.  struct FrameResolution { int width; // Frame width in pixels int height; // Frame height in pixels };

searchDocs.title: PanTiltCommand​
searchDocs.content: Output structure containing camera movement commands.  struct PanTiltCommand { float pan_delta; // Horizontal movement (-1.0 to 1.0) float tilt_delta; // Vertical movement (-1.0 to 1.0) bool valid; // Whether command is valid };   Fields:  pan_delta: Horizontal camera movement (-1.0 = left, 1.0 = right, 0.0 = no movement)tilt_delta: Vertical camera movement (-1.0 = down, 1.0 = up, 0.0 = no movement)valid: Set to true if command contains valid data (tracking enabled and target found)

searchDocs.title: ROI (Region of Interest)​
searchDocs.content: Defines a rectangular region for ROI tracking mode.  struct ROI { float x, y; // Top-left corner coordinates float width, height; // ROI dimensions std::pair<float, float> getCenter() const; };   Methods:  getCenter(): Returns the center point coordinates of the ROI

searchDocs.title: MQTTConfig​
searchDocs.content: MQTT connection configuration.  struct MQTTConfig { std::string broker_host; // MQTT broker hostname/IP int broker_port; // MQTT broker port (default: 1883) std::string client_id; // MQTT client identifier std::string detection_topic; // Topic for object detections std::string username; // MQTT username (optional) std::string password; // MQTT password (optional) int keepalive; // Keep-alive interval (default: 60) bool clean_session; // Clean session flag (default: true) int qos; // Quality of Service (default: 1) };   Example:  MQTTConfig config; config.broker_host = "192.168.1.100"; config.broker_port = 1883; config.client_id = "camera_tracker"; config.detection_topic = "ai/detections/camera1";

searchDocs.title: TrackerConfig​
searchDocs.content: Advanced tracker configuration parameters.  struct TrackerConfig { // PID output limits float pid_output_min; // Default: -60.0 float pid_output_max; // Default: 60.0 // Command filtering float deadband_threshold; // Default: 0.05 float smoothing_factor; // Default: 0.8 // Time delta limits float min_time_delta; // Default: 0.001 (1ms) float max_time_delta; // Default: 1.0 (1s) float default_time_delta; // Default: 0.033 (~30 FPS) // Resolution limits int max_resolution_dimension; // Default: 10000 // ROI defaults float default_roi_width_percent; // Default: 0.2 (20%) float default_roi_height_percent; // Default: 0.28 (28%) // PID gain limits float max_proportional_gain; // Default: 10.0 float max_integral_gain; // Default: 1.0 };

searchDocs.title: TrackingMode​
searchDocs.content: enum class TrackingMode { CENTROID, // Keep object at frame center ROI // Keep object within defined ROI };   Values:  CENTROID: Camera adjusts to keep the tracked object at the center of the frameROI: Camera only moves when the object approaches or exits the ROI boundaries

searchDocs.title: LogLevel​
searchDocs.content: enum class LogLevel { LOG_DEBUG = 0, INFO = 1, WARNING = 2, ERROR = 3, NONE = 4 };   Example:  ObjectTrackerLib::setLogLevel(LogLevel::LOG_DEBUG);

searchDocs.title: MQTT Message Format​
searchDocs.content: The library expects object detection messages in JSON format:  { "detections": [ { "id": 1, "x": 320, "y": 240, "width": 80, "height": 120, "confidence": 0.95, "class": "person" } ] }   Field Descriptions:  id: Tracking ID (persistent across frames)x, y: Center coordinates in model resolutionwidth, height: Bounding box dimensionsconfidence: Detection confidence score (0.0 to 1.0)class: Object class name (optional, not used by tracker)

searchDocs.title: location​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the directory path where the images needs to be saved.  Type: StringDefault: NULLAccess: Read/Write  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctfcapture location=/tmp/ ...

searchDocs.title: prefix​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the prefix that needs to be prepended to the file names.  Type: StringDefault: NULLAccess: Read/Write  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctfcapture prefix=CAM1 ...   The files will be saved as follows:  With prefix: <PREFIX>_YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.jpgWithout prefix: YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.jpg

searchDocs.title: capture​
searchDocs.content: Writing true to this property will save the frame as jpeg. Once the frame is captured, the value will be set to false and it needs to be set to true again to capture the next frame.  Type: BooleanDefault: falseAccess: Read  note Ensure that the mode is set to 0 (Manual) to use this property.  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctfcapture capture=true ...

searchDocs.title: mode​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the capture mode. This plugin can capture frames in 3 modes:  Manual (0): User manually triggers frame capture via API Periodic (1): Automatic capture at specified time intervals AUTO (2): Event-driven capture based on MQTT object detection messages Type: Integer (0=Manual, 1=Periodic, 2=AUTO) Default: 0 (Manual) Access: Read/Write  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API # Manual mode gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctfcapture mode=0 ... # Periodic mode gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctfcapture mode=1 ... # AUTO mode gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctfcapture mode=2 ...

searchDocs.title: time-period​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the time period in seconds to be used with periodic mode. The time period can range from 1 to 3600 seconds.  Type: Integer (Unsigned)Default: 5Range: 1-3600 secondsAccess: Read/Write  note Only effective in PERIODIC mode (mode=1).  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctfcapture time-period=5 ...

searchDocs.title: mqtt-topic​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the MQTT topic to subscribe for object detection messages in AUTO mode.  Type: StringDefault: NULLAccess: Read/Write  note Only effective in AUTO mode (mode=2).  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctfcapture mode=2 mqtt-topic=object/detection ...

searchDocs.title: mqtt-host​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the MQTT broker hostname or IP address for AUTO mode. Supports both local and remote brokers.  Type: StringDefault: "localhost"Access: Read/Write  note Only effective in AUTO mode (mode=2). If already connected, will automatically reconnect with the new host.  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API # Connect to remote broker gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctfcapture mode=2 mqtt-host=192.168.1.100 ... # Connect to localhost (default) gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctfcapture mode=2 mqtt-host=localhost ...

searchDocs.title: mqtt-port​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the MQTT broker port number for AUTO mode.  Type: Integer (Unsigned)Default: 1883Range: 1-65535Access: Read/Write  note Only effective in AUTO mode (mode=2). If already connected, will automatically reconnect with the new port.  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API # Use default MQTT port gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctfcapture mode=2 mqtt-port=1883 ... # Use custom port gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctfcapture mode=2 mqtt-port=8883 ...

searchDocs.title: time-skip​
searchDocs.content: Specifies the minimum time between captures in milliseconds for AUTO mode. This prevents capturing too frequently when object detection messages arrive rapidly.  Type: Integer (Unsigned)Default: 500Range: 0-60000 millisecondsAccess: Read/Write  note Only effective in AUTO mode (mode=2). Use 0 for no throttling (per-frame detection).  Usage:  BashWith APIGST API # Capture at most once every 100ms (10 fps max) gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctfcapture mode=2 time-skip=100 ... # No throttling - capture every frame gst-launch-1.0 ... ! dctfcapture mode=2 time-skip=0 ...
