searchDocs.title: Usage Flow​
searchDocs.content: To use the plugin library you will need to follow the below sequence of operations.

searchDocs.title: Step 1: Pipeline Initialization​
searchDocs.content: Initialize a gstreamer pipeline with this plugin.  #include <apidctoverlay.h> GstElement *pipeline, *overlay; // Initialize gst_init(&argc, &argv); pipeline = gst_parse_launch("v4l2src ! videoconvert ! video/x-raw,format=BGR ! dctoverlay name=overlay ! ...", NULL);   note The plugin must have a name associated with it, which we will use to initialize the plugin api layer.

searchDocs.title: Step 2: Plugin Initialization​
searchDocs.content: Once the pipeline is initialized successfully, call the plugin initialization function to get the plugin element object.  With APIGST API // Initialize overlay = api_dctoverlay_init(pipeline, "overlay");

searchDocs.title: Step 3: Plugin Configuration​
searchDocs.content: Once the initialization is done, you can use the apis as needed.  With APIGST API // Configure MQTT api_dctoverlay_set_mqtt_host(overlay, "localhost"); api_dctoverlay_set_mqtt_topic(overlay, "detections"); // Configure box styling api_dctoverlay_set_box_color(overlay, 0, 255, 0); // Green api_dctoverlay_set_box_thickness(overlay, 2); // Configure font styling api_dctoverlay_set_font_scale(overlay, 0.6); api_dctoverlay_set_font_color(overlay, 255, 255, 0); // Yellow api_dctoverlay_set_font_thickness(overlay, 2); // Configure label background api_dctoverlay_set_label_background(overlay, true); api_dctoverlay_set_label_bg_color(overlay, 0, 0, 0); // Black api_dctoverlay_set_label_bg_alpha(overlay, 0.7); // Start pipeline gst_element_set_state(pipeline, GST_STATE_PLAYING);

searchDocs.title: Functions​
searchDocs.content: These functions provide a C interface for controlling overlay rendering from GStreamer pipelines.

searchDocs.title: api_dctoverlay_init​
searchDocs.content: Initialize and retrieve the dctoverlay element from a GStreamer pipeline.  GstElement* api_dctoverlay_init(GstElement *pipeline, const char *element_name);   Parameters:  pipeline - GstElement pipeline containing the dctoverlay elementelement_name - Name of the dctoverlay element in the pipeline  Returns:  Pointer to dctoverlay element on successNULL on failure  Memory Management The caller is responsible for unreferencing the returned element using gst_object_unref() when done.  Example:  GstElement *pipeline = ...; // Your pipeline GstElement *overlay = api_dctoverlay_init(pipeline, "overlay"); if (overlay) { // Use the overlay element gst_object_unref(overlay); }

searchDocs.title: MQTT Configuration Functions​
searchDocs.content: api_dctoverlay_set_mqtt_host​  Set the MQTT broker hostname or IP address.  void api_dctoverlay_set_mqtt_host(GstElement *overlay, const char *host);   Parameters:  overlay - dctoverlay GstElementhost - MQTT broker host address  Example:  api_dctoverlay_set_mqtt_host(overlay, "192.168.1.100");     api_dctoverlay_set_mqtt_port​  Set the MQTT broker port number.  void api_dctoverlay_set_mqtt_port(GstElement *overlay, int port);   Parameters:  overlay - dctoverlay GstElementport - MQTT broker port (1-65535)  Example:  api_dctoverlay_set_mqtt_port(overlay, 1883);     api_dctoverlay_set_mqtt_topic​  Set the MQTT topic to subscribe for detection messages.  void api_dctoverlay_set_mqtt_topic(GstElement *overlay, const char *topic);   Parameters:  overlay - dctoverlay GstElementtopic - MQTT topic for detections  Example:  api_dctoverlay_set_mqtt_topic(overlay, "detections");

searchDocs.title: Box Styling Functions​
searchDocs.content: api_dctoverlay_set_box_color​  Set the bounding box color in RGB components.  void api_dctoverlay_set_box_color(GstElement *overlay, int r, int g, int b);   Parameters:  overlay - dctoverlay GstElementr - Red component (0-255)g - Green component (0-255)b - Blue component (0-255)  Example:  // Green boxes api_dctoverlay_set_box_color(overlay, 0, 255, 0); // Yellow boxes api_dctoverlay_set_box_color(overlay, 255, 255, 0);     api_dctoverlay_set_box_thickness​  Set the bounding box border thickness.  void api_dctoverlay_set_box_thickness(GstElement *overlay, int thickness);   Parameters:  overlay - dctoverlay GstElementthickness - Thickness in pixels (1-50)  Example:  api_dctoverlay_set_box_thickness(overlay, 2);

searchDocs.title: Font Styling Functions​
searchDocs.content: api_dctoverlay_set_font_type​  Set the OpenCV font type for label text.  void api_dctoverlay_set_font_type(GstElement *overlay, int font_type);   Parameters:  overlay - dctoverlay GstElementfont_type - OpenCV font type (0-7)  Font Types:  0: SIMPLEX1: PLAIN2: DUPLEX3: COMPLEX4: TRIPLEX5: COMPLEX_SMALL6: SCRIPT_SIMPLEX7: SCRIPT_COMPLEX  Example:  api_dctoverlay_set_font_type(overlay, 0); // SIMPLEX     api_dctoverlay_set_font_scale​  Set the font size scale factor.  void api_dctoverlay_set_font_scale(GstElement *overlay, double scale);   Parameters:  overlay - dctoverlay GstElementscale - Font size scale factor (0.1-10.0)  Example:  api_dctoverlay_set_font_scale(overlay, 0.6);     api_dctoverlay_set_font_color​  Set the font color in RGB components.  void api_dctoverlay_set_font_color(GstElement *overlay, int r, int g, int b);   Parameters:  overlay - dctoverlay GstElementr - Red component (0-255)g - Green component (0-255)b - Blue component (0-255)  Example:  // Yellow text api_dctoverlay_set_font_color(overlay, 255, 255, 0);     api_dctoverlay_set_font_thickness​  Set the font thickness.  void api_dctoverlay_set_font_thickness(GstElement *overlay, int thickness);   Parameters:  overlay - dctoverlay GstElementthickness - Font thickness in pixels (1-10)  Example:  api_dctoverlay_set_font_thickness(overlay, 2);

searchDocs.title: Label Background Functions​
searchDocs.content: api_dctoverlay_set_label_background​  Enable or disable label background.  void api_dctoverlay_set_label_background(GstElement *overlay, bool enable);   Parameters:  overlay - dctoverlay GstElementenable - true to enable, false to disable  Example:  api_dctoverlay_set_label_background(overlay, true);     api_dctoverlay_set_label_bg_color​  Set the label background color in RGB components.  void api_dctoverlay_set_label_bg_color(GstElement *overlay, int r, int g, int b);   Parameters:  overlay - dctoverlay GstElementr - Red component (0-255)g - Green component (0-255)b - Blue component (0-255)  Example:  // Black background api_dctoverlay_set_label_bg_color(overlay, 0, 0, 0);     api_dctoverlay_set_label_bg_alpha​  Set the label background transparency.  void api_dctoverlay_set_label_bg_alpha(GstElement *overlay, double alpha);   Parameters:  overlay - dctoverlay GstElementalpha - Alpha value (0.0=transparent, 1.0=opaque)  Example:  api_dctoverlay_set_label_bg_alpha(overlay, 0.7);     api_dctoverlay_set_label_position​  Set the label position relative to the bounding box.  void api_dctoverlay_set_label_position(GstElement *overlay, int position);   Parameters:  overlay - dctoverlay GstElementposition - Position value  Position Values:  0: Top-Left1: Top-Right2: Bottom-Left3: Bottom-Right  Example:  api_dctoverlay_set_label_position(overlay, 0); // Top-Left

searchDocs.title: Confidence Display Functions​
searchDocs.content: api_dctoverlay_set_show_confidence​  Enable or disable confidence score display.  void api_dctoverlay_set_show_confidence(GstElement *overlay, bool show);   Parameters:  overlay - dctoverlay GstElementshow - true to show, false to hide  Example:  api_dctoverlay_set_show_confidence(overlay, true);     api_dctoverlay_set_confidence_decimals​  Set the number of decimal places for confidence scores.  void api_dctoverlay_set_confidence_decimals(GstElement *overlay, int decimals);   Parameters:  overlay - dctoverlay GstElementdecimals - Number of decimal places (0-4)  Example:  api_dctoverlay_set_confidence_decimals(overlay, 2);

searchDocs.title: Usage Example​
searchDocs.content: Here's a complete example demonstrating the API usage:  #include "apidctoverlay.h" int main(int argc, char *argv[]) { GstElement *pipeline, *overlay; // Initialize pipeline gst_init(&argc, &argv); pipeline = gst_parse_launch( "v4l2src device=/dev/video8 ! videoconvert ! " "video/x-raw,format=BGR ! " "dctoverlay name=overlay ! " "videoconvert ! autovideosink", NULL); // Get overlay element overlay = api_dctoverlay_init(pipeline, "overlay"); if (!overlay) { fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialize overlay element\n"); return -1; } // Configure MQTT api_dctoverlay_set_mqtt_host(overlay, "localhost"); api_dctoverlay_set_mqtt_topic(overlay, "detections"); // Configure box styling (green boxes) api_dctoverlay_set_box_color(overlay, 0, 255, 0); api_dctoverlay_set_box_thickness(overlay, 2); // Configure font styling (yellow text) api_dctoverlay_set_font_scale(overlay, 0.6); api_dctoverlay_set_font_color(overlay, 255, 255, 0); api_dctoverlay_set_font_thickness(overlay, 2); // Configure label background (black, semi-transparent) api_dctoverlay_set_label_background(overlay, true); api_dctoverlay_set_label_bg_color(overlay, 0, 0, 0); api_dctoverlay_set_label_bg_alpha(overlay, 0.7); // Configure label position (top-left) api_dctoverlay_set_label_position(overlay, 0); // Configure confidence display api_dctoverlay_set_show_confidence(overlay, true); api_dctoverlay_set_confidence_decimals(overlay, 2); // Configure ROI (optional) g_object_set(overlay, "enable-roi", TRUE, "roi-x", 100, "roi-y", 100, "roi-width", 400, "roi-height", 300, NULL); // Start pipeline gst_element_set_state(pipeline, GST_STATE_PLAYING); // Run main loop... // Cleanup gst_object_unref(overlay); gst_object_unref(pipeline); return 0; }

searchDocs.title: MQTT Message Format​
searchDocs.content: The plugin expects detection data in the following JSON format:  { "detections": [ { "bbox": { "x": 100, "y": 50, "width": 200, "height": 150 }, "label": "person", "confidence": 0.95, "class_id": 0 } ] }   Fields:  bbox: Bounding box coordinates (x, y, width, height)label: Object class label (string)confidence: Detection confidence (0.0-1.0)class_id: Object class ID (integer, optional for filtering)

searchDocs.title: Prerequisites​
searchDocs.content: Before building, ensure you have the following dependencies installed:  Meson build system (>= 0.54)Ninja build toolC++17 compatible compiler (g++ or clang++)libmosquitto (MQTT client library) - required if building with MQTTlibcjson (JSON parsing) - required if building with MQTTPTZ control library - required if building with PTZ support

searchDocs.title: Installing Dependencies​
searchDocs.content: On Debian/Ubuntu systems:  sudo apt-get update sudo apt-get install meson ninja-build g++ libmosquitto-dev libcjson-dev   Yocto SDK Toolchain Setup For standalone SDK builds using the Yocto toolchain, you must first create and source the SDK environment before building. See the Toolchain Setup documentation for instructions on creating and installing the SDK toolchain. # Source the SDK environment source /path/to/sdk/environment-setup-<arch>-poky-linux # Then proceed with building cd sentinal_sdk/image/pid_otrack meson setup build meson compile -C build

searchDocs.title: Build Options​
searchDocs.content: The library supports the following build-time configuration options:  Option	Values	Default	Descriptioncomm	mqtt, none	mqtt	Communication framework for receiving detections ptz	enabled, disabled	disabled	PTZ hardware control support

searchDocs.title: 1. Configure Build​
searchDocs.content: cd sentinal_sdk/image/pid_otrack meson setup build

searchDocs.title: 2. Build Library​
searchDocs.content: meson compile -C build

searchDocs.title: 3. Install Library​
searchDocs.content: meson install -C build   This installs:  Shared library: libpid_otrack.so → $PREFIX/lib/Header files: *.h → $PREFIX/include/pid-otrack/

searchDocs.title: Build with MQTT Communication (Default)​
searchDocs.content: meson setup build -Dcomm=mqtt meson compile -C build   This enables:  MQTT client for receiving object detectionsJSON parsing for detection messagesPreprocessor define: -DCOMM_MQTT

searchDocs.title: Build without Communication Layer​
searchDocs.content: meson setup build -Dcomm=none meson compile -C build   This creates a standalone library for manual detection updates.  Preprocessor define: -DDISABLE_MQTT

searchDocs.title: Build with PTZ Control Support​
searchDocs.content: meson setup build -Dcomm=mqtt -Dptz=enabled meson compile -C build   This enables hardware PTZ control integration.  Preprocessor define: -DPTZ_ENABLEDLinks with: libptctrl.a  PTZ TCP Server Required When building with -Dptz=enabled, you must run the PTZ TCP server (test/ptz_tcp_server.py) before running the test application, otherwise it will fail at initialization. See PTZ TCP Server Setup section below for details.

searchDocs.title: Custom Build Configuration​
searchDocs.content: meson setup build \ -Dcomm=mqtt \ -Dptz=enabled \ -Dbuildtype=release \ -Dprefix=/usr/local meson compile -C build meson install -C build

searchDocs.title: Build Types​
searchDocs.content: Configure build type using -Dbuildtype:  Build Type	Optimization	Debug Info	Use Casedebug	-O0	Full	Development debugoptimized	-O2 -g	Yes	Testing (default) release	-O3	Minimal	Production minsize	-Os	No	Embedded systems

searchDocs.title: Reconfigure Build​
searchDocs.content: To change build options after initial setup:  meson configure build -Dcomm=none -Dptz=disabled meson compile -C build

searchDocs.title: Clean Build​
searchDocs.content: rm -rf build meson setup build meson compile -C build

searchDocs.title: Test Application​
searchDocs.content: The library includes a test application (test_pid_otrack) for validating functionality.

searchDocs.title: Building Test Application​
searchDocs.content: The test application is automatically built with the library:  meson compile -C build   Test executable location: build/test_pid_otrack

searchDocs.title: Running Test Application​
searchDocs.content: ./build/test_pid_otrack   The test application demonstrates:  Library initializationDetection updatesPID control calculationsMode switchingTarget selection

searchDocs.title: PTZ TCP Server Setup​
searchDocs.content: Required for PTZ-Enabled Builds If you built the library with -Dptz=enabled, the test application will fail unless the PTZ TCP server is running.

searchDocs.title: Why is this needed?​
searchDocs.content: The test application initializes PTZ control at startup. If built with PTZ enabled, it calls pt_init() which attempts to connect to the PTZ TCP server. If the server is not running, initialization will fail:  [ERROR] Failed to initialize PTZ control Make sure the PTZ TCP server is running!

searchDocs.title: Starting the PTZ TCP Server​
searchDocs.content: The library includes a Python-based PTZ TCP server simulator for testing purposes.  Location: test/ptz_tcp_server.py  Usage:  # Make the script executable chmod +x sentinal_sdk/image/pid_otrack/test/ptz_tcp_server.py # Start server on all interfaces (default port 5005) ./sentinal_sdk/image/pid_otrack/test/ptz_tcp_server.py # Or specify custom host and port ./sentinal_sdk/image/pid_otrack/test/ptz_tcp_server.py --host 169.254.11.105 --port 5005 # Or start on localhost only ./sentinal_sdk/image/pid_otrack/test/ptz_tcp_server.py --host 127.0.0.1   Server Options:  --host HOST: Host address to bind to (default: 0.0.0.0 - all interfaces)--port PORT: Port to listen on (default: 5005)-h, --help: Show help message

searchDocs.title: Running Test with PTZ Server​
searchDocs.content: Open two terminal windows:  Terminal 1 - Start PTZ Server:  cd sentinal_sdk/image/pid_otrack ./test/ptz_tcp_server.py --host 169.254.11.105 --port 5005   Terminal 2 - Run Test Application:  cd build ./test_pid_otrack

searchDocs.title: Alternative: Build Without PTZ​
searchDocs.content: If you don't need PTZ control or don't want to run the TCP server, rebuild without PTZ support:  # Reconfigure existing build meson configure build -Dptz=disabled meson compile -C build # Or clean build rm -rf build meson setup build -Dcomm=mqtt -Dptz=disabled meson compile -C build

searchDocs.title: Cross-Compilation​
searchDocs.content: For cross-compilation with Yocto SDK:  source /path/to/yocto/sdk/environment-setup-script meson setup build --cross-file=cross-compile.ini meson compile -C build

searchDocs.title: Build Issues​
searchDocs.content: Error: dependency 'libmosquitto' not found  Install MQTT library: sudo apt-get install libmosquitto-devOr build without MQTT: meson setup build -Dcomm=none  Error: dependency 'libcjson' not found  Install cJSON: sudo apt-get install libcjson-devOr build without MQTT: meson setup build -Dcomm=none  Error: PTZ library not found  Ensure lib/ptz/libptctrl.a existsOr build without PTZ: meson setup build -Dptz=disabled

searchDocs.title: Runtime Issues​
searchDocs.content: Test application fails with "Failed to initialize PTZ control"  Cause: Built with PTZ enabled but PTZ TCP server is not runningSolution 1: Start the PTZ TCP server before running the test (see above)Solution 2: Rebuild without PTZ support

searchDocs.content: Feature	MANUAL	AUTORecording Trigger	API call/property	MQTT message based Control	User controlled	Event-driven (auto) MQTT Required	No	Yes

searchDocs.title: Usage Flow​
searchDocs.content: To use the plugin library you will need to follow the below sequence of operations.

searchDocs.title: Step 1: Pipeline Initialization​
searchDocs.content: Initialize a gstreamer pipeline with this plugin.  #include <apidctvrecord.h> GstElement *pipeline, *vrecord; // Initialize gst_init(&argc, &argv); pipeline = gst_parse_launch("videotestsrc ! x264enc ! h264parse ! dctvrecord name=rec ! fakesink", NULL);   note The plugin must have a name associated with it, which we will use to initialize the plugin api layer.

searchDocs.title: Step 2: Plugin Initialization​
searchDocs.content: Once the pipeline is initialized successfully, call the plugin initialization function to get the plugin element object.  With APIGST API // Initialize vrecord = api_dctvrecord_init(pipeline, "rec");

searchDocs.title: Step 3: Plugin Configuration​
searchDocs.content: Once the initialization is done, you can use the apis as needed.  With APIGST API // Configure for manual mode api_dctvrecord_set_mode(vrecord, DCTVRECORD_MODE_MANUAL); api_dctvrecord_set_location(vrecord, "/tmp/videos"); api_dctvrecord_set_prefix(vrecord, "camera1"); // Start pipeline gst_element_set_state(pipeline, GST_STATE_PLAYING); // Start recording api_dctvrecord_set_recording(vrecord, true); // ... record for some time ... // Stop recording api_dctvrecord_set_recording(vrecord, false);

searchDocs.title: DCTVRecordMode​
searchDocs.content: Defines the recording mode for the dctvrecord element.  typedef enum { DCTVRECORD_MODE_MANUAL = 0, // Manual recording mode DCTVRECORD_MODE_AUTO = 1 // Automatic recording mode } DCTVRecordMode;   Value	DescriptionDCTVRECORD_MODE_MANUAL	User controls recording via recording property or API DCTVRECORD_MODE_AUTO	Automatic recording based on MQTT messages

searchDocs.title: Functions​
searchDocs.content: These functions provide a C interface for controlling video recording from GStreamer pipelines. It supports both manual and automatic recording modes with MQTT-based event-driven control.

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_init​
searchDocs.content: Initialize and retrieve the dctvrecord element from a GStreamer pipeline.  GstElement* api_dctvrecord_init(GstElement *pipeline, const char *element_name);   Parameters:  pipeline - GstElement pipeline containing the dctvrecord elementelement_name - Name of the dctvrecord element in the pipeline  Returns:  Pointer to dctvrecord element on successNULL on failure  Memory Management The caller is responsible for deinitializing the returned element using api_dctvrecord_deinit() when done.  Example:  GstElement *pipeline = ...; // Your pipeline GstElement *vrecord = api_dctvrecord_init(pipeline, "myrecorder"); if (vrecord) { // Use the vrecord element api_dctvrecord_deinit(vrecord); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_deinit​
searchDocs.content: Deinitialize and cleanup the dctvrecord element.  void api_dctvrecord_deinit(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElement to deinitialize  Returns:  void (no return value)  note This function properly cleans up and unreferences the dctvrecord element.  Example:  GstElement *vrecord = api_dctvrecord_init(pipeline, "myrecorder"); if (vrecord) { // Configure and use the element api_dctvrecord_set_location(vrecord, "/tmp/videos"); // ... do work ... // Cleanup api_dctvrecord_deinit(vrecord); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_set_mode​
searchDocs.content: Set the recording mode (manual or automatic).  bool api_dctvrecord_set_mode(GstElement *element, DCTVRecordMode mode);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElementmode - Recording mode (DCTVRECORD_MODE_MANUAL or DCTVRECORD_MODE_AUTO)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  // Set to manual mode api_dctvrecord_set_mode(vrecord, DCTVRECORD_MODE_MANUAL); // Set to automatic mode api_dctvrecord_set_mode(vrecord, DCTVRECORD_MODE_AUTO);

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_set_location​
searchDocs.content: Set the directory where recorded MP4 files will be saved.  bool api_dctvrecord_set_location(GstElement *element, const char *location);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElementlocation - Directory path for saving MP4 files  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  info Filenames are automatically generated with timestamps in the format: prefix_YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.mp4 in the respective date directory under location  Example:  api_dctvrecord_set_location(vrecord, "/home/user/recordings");   recordings/ # Directory specified in the location property └── YYYY_MM_DD/ # Date-wise subfolder └── prefix_YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.mp4

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_set_prefix​
searchDocs.content: Set a prefix for recorded video filenames.  bool api_dctvrecord_set_prefix(GstElement *element, const char *prefix);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElementprefix - Prefix string for filenames (optional, can be NULL)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Filename Format:  With prefix: <prefix>_YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.mp4Without prefix: YYYY_MM_DD_HH_MM_SS_MSS.mp4  Example:  api_dctvrecord_set_prefix(vrecord, "camera1"); // Results in: camera1_2025_10_13_14_30_25_123.mp4

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_set_recording​
searchDocs.content: Start or stop recording (MANUAL mode only).  bool api_dctvrecord_set_recording(GstElement *element, bool recording);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElementrecording - true to start recording, false to stop  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Mode Requirement This function only works in DCTVRECORD_MODE_MANUAL. In AUTO mode, recording is controlled automatically by MQTT messages.  Example:  // Ensure manual mode is set api_dctvrecord_set_mode(vrecord, DCTVRECORD_MODE_MANUAL); // Start recording api_dctvrecord_set_recording(vrecord, true); // Stop recording api_dctvrecord_set_recording(vrecord, false);

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_set_en​
searchDocs.content: Enable recording with location and prefix in one call.  bool api_dctvrecord_set_en(GstElement *element, const char *location, const char *prefix);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElementlocation - Directory path for saving filesprefix - Filename prefix (can be NULL)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  // Start recording with location and prefix api_dctvrecord_set_en(vrecord, "/tmp/videos", "cam1");

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_set_dis​
searchDocs.content: Disable/stop recording.  bool api_dctvrecord_set_dis(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElement  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  // Stop recording api_dctvrecord_set_dis(vrecord);

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_set_auto_enable​
searchDocs.content: Enable or disable automatic recording in AUTO mode.  bool api_dctvrecord_set_auto_enable(GstElement *element, bool enable);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElementenable - true to enable auto recording, false to disable  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  note Only effective in AUTO mode. When enabled, connects to MQTT broker and starts monitoring for detection messages.  Example:  // Enable automatic recording api_dctvrecord_set_auto_enable(vrecord, true); // Disable automatic recording api_dctvrecord_set_auto_enable(vrecord, false);

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_get_location​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current save directory location.  char* api_dctvrecord_get_location(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElement  Returns:  Current location string on successNULL on failure  Memory Management The caller must free() the returned string when done.  Example:  char *location = api_dctvrecord_get_location(vrecord); if (location) { printf("Save location: %s\n", location); free(location); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_get_prefix​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current filename prefix.  char* api_dctvrecord_get_prefix(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElement  Returns:  Current prefix string on successNULL if not set or on failure  Memory Management The caller must free() the returned string when done.  Example:  char *prefix = api_dctvrecord_get_prefix(vrecord); if (prefix) { printf("Filename prefix: %s\n", prefix); free(prefix); } else { printf("No prefix set\n"); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_get_recording​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current recording state.  bool api_dctvrecord_get_recording(GstElement *element, bool *recording);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElementrecording - Pointer to store the current recording state  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  bool is_recording; if (api_dctvrecord_get_recording(vrecord, &is_recording)) { printf("Recording: %s\n", is_recording ? "YES" : "NO"); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_get_mode​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current recording mode.  bool api_dctvrecord_get_mode(GstElement *element, DCTVRecordMode *mode);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElementmode - Pointer to store the current mode  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  DCTVRecordMode current_mode; if (api_dctvrecord_get_mode(vrecord, &current_mode)) { if (current_mode == DCTVRECORD_MODE_MANUAL) { printf("Manual mode\n"); } else { printf("Auto mode\n"); } }

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_get_auto_enable​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current auto-enable state.  bool api_dctvrecord_get_auto_enable(GstElement *element, bool *enable);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElementenable - Pointer to store the current auto-enable state  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  bool auto_enabled; if (api_dctvrecord_get_auto_enable(vrecord, &auto_enabled)) { printf("Auto-enable: %s\n", auto_enabled ? "YES" : "NO"); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_set_host​
searchDocs.content: Set the MQTT broker host address (AUTO mode only).  bool api_dctvrecord_set_host(GstElement *element, const char *host);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElementhost - Host address (e.g., "localhost", "192.168.1.100")  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  note This property applies to all communication protocols (MQTT, TCP, Kafka, etc.). Currently only MQTT is supported. Default value is "localhost".  Example:  // Set MQTT broker host to remote server api_dctvrecord_set_host(vrecord, "192.168.1.100");

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_get_host​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current broker/server host address.  char* api_dctvrecord_get_host(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElement  Returns:  Current host string on successNULL if not set or on failure  Memory Management The caller must free() the returned string when done.  Example:  char *host = api_dctvrecord_get_host(vrecord); if (host) { printf("MQTT Host: %s\n", host); free(host); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_set_port​
searchDocs.content: Set the MQTT broker port (AUTO mode only).  bool api_dctvrecord_set_port(GstElement *element, int port);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElementport - Port number (e.g., 1883 for MQTT, 9092 for Kafka)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  note This property applies to all communication protocols (MQTT, TCP, Kafka, etc.). Currently only MQTT is supported. Default value is 1883 (MQTT default port).  Example:  // Set MQTT broker port api_dctvrecord_set_port(vrecord, 1883);

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_get_port​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current broker/server port.  bool api_dctvrecord_get_port(GstElement *element, int *port);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElementport - Pointer to store the current port number  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  int port; if (api_dctvrecord_get_port(vrecord, &port)) { printf("MQTT Port: %d\n", port); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_set_mqtt_topic​
searchDocs.content: Set the MQTT topic for receiving object detection messages (AUTO mode only).  bool api_dctvrecord_set_mqtt_topic(GstElement *element, const char *mqtt_topic);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElementmqtt_topic - MQTT topic to subscribe to (e.g., "detections/camera1")  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  note Only effective in AUTO mode. Setting this triggers MQTT connection if auto-enable is true.  Example:  // Set MQTT topic for automatic recording api_dctvrecord_set_mqtt_topic(vrecord, "detections/camera1");

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_get_mqtt_topic​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current MQTT topic.  char* api_dctvrecord_get_mqtt_topic(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElement  Returns:  Current MQTT topic string on successNULL if not set or on failure  Memory Management The caller must free() the returned string when done.  Example:  char *topic = api_dctvrecord_get_mqtt_topic(vrecord); if (topic) { printf("MQTT Topic: %s\n", topic); free(topic); } else { printf("No MQTT topic set\n"); }

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_set_det_timeout​
searchDocs.content: Set the detection timeout for automatic recording stop (AUTO mode only).  bool api_dctvrecord_set_det_timeout(GstElement *element, double det_timeout);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElementdet_timeout - Detection timeout in seconds (e.g., 10.0)  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  note Only effective in AUTO mode. If no detections are received for this duration, recording automatically stops.  Example:  // Set timeout to 5 seconds api_dctvrecord_set_det_timeout(vrecord, 5.0); // Recording will stop 5 seconds after the last detection message

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_get_det_timeout​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current detection timeout.  bool api_dctvrecord_get_det_timeout(GstElement *element, double *det_timeout);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElementdet_timeout - Pointer to store the current detection timeout in seconds  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  double timeout; if (api_dctvrecord_get_det_timeout(vrecord, &timeout)) { printf("Detection timeout: %.1f seconds\n", timeout); }   --

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_set_mqtt_client_id​
searchDocs.content: To set mqtt client id when connecting to the broker  bool api_dctvrecord_set_mqtt_client_id(GstElement *element, const char *mqtt_client_id);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElementdet_timeout - mqtt client id to be set  Returns:  true on successfalse on failure  Example:  // Set timeout to 5 seconds api_dctvrecord_set_mqtt_client_id(vrecord, "newelement");

searchDocs.title: api_dctvrecord_get_mqtt_client_id​
searchDocs.content: Retrieve the current mqtt client id  char* api_dctvrecord_get_mqtt_client_id(GstElement *element);   Parameters:  element - dctvrecord GstElement  Returns:  Current mqtt_client_id string on successNULL on failure  Example:  char *client_id = api_dctvrecord_get_mqtt_client_id(vrecord); if (client_id) { printf("MQTT Client id: %s\n", client_id); free(client_id); }

searchDocs.title: Usage Example​
searchDocs.content:
Here's a complete example demonstrating the API usage:  #include "apidctvrecord.h" int main(int argc, char *argv[]) { GstElement *pipeline, *vrecord; // Initialize GStreamer gst_init(&argc, &argv); // Create pipeline pipeline = gst_parse_launch( "videotestsrc ! " "video/x-raw,format=I420,width=640,height=480,framerate=30/1 ! " "x264enc tune=zerolatency bitrate=2000 ! " "h264parse config-interval=-1 ! " "video/x-h264,stream-format=avc,alignment=au ! " "dctvrecord name=myrecorder ! " "fakesink", NULL); if (!pipeline) { fprintf(stderr, "Failed to create pipeline
"); return -1; } // Get vrecord element vrecord = api_dctvrecord_init(pipeline, "myrecorder"); if (!vrecord) { fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialize vrecord element
"); return -1; } // Configure for automatic recording api_dctvrecord_set_mode(vrecord, DCTVRECORD_MODE_AUTO); api_dctvrecord_set_location(vrecord, "/tmp/recordings"); api_dctvrecord_set_prefix(vrecord, "test"); api_dctvrecord_set_host(vrecord, "192.168.1.100"); api_dctvrecord_set_port(vrecord, 1883); api_dctvrecord_set_mqtt_topic(vrecord, "detections/camera1"); api_dctvrecord_set_det_timeout(vrecord, 10.0); api_dctvrecord_set_auto_enable(vrecord, true); // Start pipeline gst_element_set_state(pipeline, GST_STATE_PLAYING); // Recording starts automatically when detection messages are received printf("Waiting for MQTT detection messages...
"); // Run for 60 seconds sleep(60); // Disable auto recording printf("Disabling auto recording...
"); api_dctvrecord_set_auto_enable(vrecord, false); // Cleanup gst_element_set_state(pipeline, GST_STATE_NULL); api_dctvrecord_deinit(vrecord); gst_object_unref(pipeline); return 0; }

searchDocs.title: Overview​
searchDocs.content: Info messages provide a flexible way to overlay custom text content on video frames with full control over:  Position: Place messages anywhere on the frameStyling: Customize fonts, colors, bold/italic formattingBounding Box: Optional border around textBackground: Semi-transparent background for better visibilityPersistence: Auto-expiring or permanent messagesDynamic Updates: Add, update, or remove messages via MQTT

searchDocs.title: Architecture​
searchDocs.content: The info message system is implemented as two coordinated layers.  The communication layer (comm_info_message) is responsible for message lifecycle management. It parses incoming JSON commands, maintains a thread-safe list of active messages, enforces message limits, and handles automatic expiration based on persistence time. Messages are uniquely identified by an ID, allowing updates to replace existing entries without restarting the plugin.  The machine layer (mach_info_message) handles rendering. It draws the text onto video frames using OpenCV, applying font styling, optional bounding boxes, and background transparency. Rendering occurs on every frame for all active messages.

searchDocs.title: Message Format​
searchDocs.content: Info messages are controlled via JSON commands sent through MQTT. The expected format:  { "command": "add_info_message", "id": "unique_message_id", "message": "Text to display", "pos_x": 100, "pos_y": 50, "font_size": 14, "font_color": "#FFFFFF", "font_bold": false, "font_italic": false, "bbox": false, "bbox_color": "#00FF00", "bbox_thickness": 2, "bbox_bgnd_color": "#000000", "bbox_bgnd_alpha": 0.7, "persist": 5 }

searchDocs.title: Required Parameters​
searchDocs.content: Parameter	Type	Descriptioncommand	string	Must be "add_info_message" id	string	Unique message identifier (max 64 chars) message	string	Text to display (max 256 chars) pos_x	int	X position in pixels pos_y	int	Y position in pixels

searchDocs.title: Optional Parameters​
searchDocs.content: Parameter	Type	Default	Descriptionfont_size	int	14	Font size in points font_color	string	"#FFFFFF"	Text color (hex format) font_bold	bool	false	Enable bold text font_italic	bool	false	Enable italic text font_underline	bool	false	Underline text (not implemented in OpenCV) bbox	bool	false	Enable bounding box around text bbox_color	string	"#00FF00"	Box border color (hex) bbox_thickness	int	2	Box border thickness in pixels bbox_bgnd_color	string	none	Background color (hex) bbox_bgnd_alpha	float	0.7	Background transparency (0.0-1.0) persist	int	0	Seconds to display (0 = forever)  Color Format Colors are specified in hex format with or without the # prefix (e.g., "#FF0000" or "FF0000" for red).

searchDocs.title: MQTT Topic Configuration​
searchDocs.content: The info message feature uses the same MQTT connection as the detection overlay. Configure the MQTT topic via the plugin property:  # GStreamer pipeline example gst-launch-1.0 \ videotestsrc ! \ video/x-raw,format=BGR ! \ dctoverlay \ mqtt-host=localhost \ mqtt-port=1883 \ mqtt-topic=overlay/commands ! \ videoconvert ! \ autovideosink

searchDocs.title: C API Usage​
searchDocs.content: The info message feature can also be used programmatically:  #include "comm_info_message.h" // Initialize context InfoMessageContext *ctx = info_message_init(); // Create message InfoMessage msg = {0}; strncpy(msg.id, "alert_001", INFO_MESSAGE_MAX_ID); strncpy(msg.message, "Alert: Motion Detected", INFO_MESSAGE_MAX_TEXT); msg.pos_x = 100; msg.pos_y = 50; msg.font.font_size = 16; msg.font.font_color_r = 255; msg.font.font_color_g = 0; msg.font.font_color_b = 0; msg.persist_seconds = 5; // Add message info_message_add(ctx, &msg); // Get active messages InfoMessage *messages = NULL; int count = 0; if (info_message_get_active(ctx, &messages, &count)) { // Render messages on frame for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) { // Process message } free(messages); } // Cleanup info_message_cleanup(ctx);

searchDocs.title: Basic Message​
searchDocs.content: Display a simple white text message that expires after 5 seconds:  mosquitto_pubPython mosquitto_pub -h localhost -t overlay/commands -m '{ "command": "add_info_message", "id": "alert_001", "message": "Detection Alert: Person detected", "pos_x": 50, "pos_y": 50, "font_size": 16, "font_color": "#FF0000", "persist": 5 }'

searchDocs.title: Message with Bounding Box​
searchDocs.content: Add a rectangular border around the text:  { "command": "add_info_message", "id": "warning_box", "message": "WARNING: High Temperature", "pos_x": 150, "pos_y": 100, "font_size": 18, "font_color": "#FFFF00", "font_bold": true, "bbox": true, "bbox_color": "#FF0000", "bbox_thickness": 3, "persist": 10 }

searchDocs.title: Message with Background​
searchDocs.content: Add a semi-transparent background for better visibility:  { "command": "add_info_message", "id": "status_bg", "message": "System Status: ACTIVE", "pos_x": 200, "pos_y": 50, "font_size": 14, "font_color": "#FFFFFF", "bbox_bgnd_color": "#000000", "bbox_bgnd_alpha": 0.7, "persist": 0 }

searchDocs.title: Persistent Message​
searchDocs.content: Create a message that never expires (persist = 0):  { "command": "add_info_message", "id": "permanent_status", "message": "Recording in Progress", "pos_x": 20, "pos_y": 20, "font_size": 12, "font_color": "#FF0000", "font_bold": true, "persist": 0 }

searchDocs.title: Updating a Message​
searchDocs.content: To update an existing message, send a new message with the same ID. The old message will be replaced:  { "command": "add_info_message", "id": "alert_001", "message": "Detection Alert: Person CLEARED", "pos_x": 50, "pos_y": 50, "font_size": 16, "font_color": "#00FF00", "persist": 5 }

searchDocs.title: Styled Text​
searchDocs.content: Combine multiple styling options:  { "command": "add_info_message", "id": "styled_message", "message": "CRITICAL ALERT", "pos_x": 300, "pos_y": 150, "font_size": 20, "font_color": "#FFFFFF", "font_bold": true, "font_italic": true, "bbox": true, "bbox_color": "#FF0000", "bbox_thickness": 3, "bbox_bgnd_color": "#800000", "bbox_bgnd_alpha": 0.8, "persist": 0 }

searchDocs.title: Adding Messages​
searchDocs.content: Send a JSON message with the add_info_message command via MQTT to the configured topic (default: overlay/commands).

searchDocs.title: Updating Messages​
searchDocs.content: Send a new message with the same id. The existing message will be replaced with the new content and styling. The persistence timer resets.

searchDocs.title: Removing Messages​
searchDocs.content: Messages are automatically removed when they expire (based on the persist parameter). For messages with persist: 0, they remain until:  Replaced with a new message using the same IDThe plugin is restartedAll messages are cleared programmatically

searchDocs.title: Message Limits​
searchDocs.content: Maximum concurrent messages: 10Maximum message text: 256 charactersMaximum ID length: 64 characters  When the maximum number of messages is reached, new messages will fail to be added unless an existing message expires or is replaced.

searchDocs.title: Persistence​
searchDocs.content: persist: N (N > 0): Message disappears after N secondspersist: 0: Message stays forever until replaced or plugin restartsTimer starts when the message is addedUpdating a message (same ID) resets the timer

searchDocs.title: Expiration Handling​
searchDocs.content: Expired messages are automatically removed when info_message_get_active() is called. The plugin checks message expiration times on each frame rendering.

searchDocs.title: Rendering Order​
searchDocs.content: Messages are rendered in the order they are stored in the context. Messages added first appear "behind" messages added later if they overlap.

searchDocs.title: Features​
searchDocs.content: PID-based Camera Control: Smooth pan/tilt camera movements using PID control algorithmsMultiple Tracking Modes: Support for centroid tracking and ROI (Region of Interest) trackingMQTT Communication: Real-time object detection data reception via MQTT protocolDynamic Target Selection: Select targets by ID or display coordinatesResolution Independence: Automatic coordinate conversion between model and display resolutionsThread-Safe: Mutex-protected API for multi-threaded applicationsConfigurable Parameters: Adjustable PID gains, filtering, and tracking parametersPTZ Control Support: Optional integration with hardware PTZ controllers (build option)Modular Architecture: Clean separation between library interface, logic, and communication layers

searchDocs.title: Module Architecture​
searchDocs.content: pid_otrack/ ├── inc/ # Header files │ ├── lib-pid-otrack.h # Main library API interface │ ├── logic-pid-otrack.h # Internal tracking logic │ ├── commdctotrack_pid.h # Communication layer interface │ ├── comm_mqtt_pid.h # MQTT communication implementation │ ├── mqtt-object-tracker.h # MQTT wrapper for tracker │ └── ptz/ # PTZ control headers (optional) │ └── ptctrl_lib.h ├── src/ # Source files │ ├── lib-pid-otrack.cpp │ ├── logic-pid-otrack.cpp │ ├── commdctotrack_pid.cpp │ ├── comm_mqtt_pid.cpp │ └── mqtt-object-tracker.cpp ├── lib/ # Pre-built libraries │ └── ptz/ │ └── libptctrl.a # PTZ control library (optional) ├── test/ # Test applications │ └── pid_test.cpp ├── meson.build # Build configuration └── meson_options.txt # Build options

searchDocs.title: Requirements​
searchDocs.content: To use the PID Object Tracker library, you will need the following dependencies:  Build System: Meson (>= 0.54) and NinjaCompiler: C++17 compatible compilerMQTT Support (optional): libmosquitto and libcjsonPTZ Control (optional): PTZ control library

searchDocs.title: Installation​
searchDocs.content: cd sentinal_sdk/image/pid_otrack meson setup build meson compile -C build meson install -C build

searchDocs.title: Basic Usage​
searchDocs.content: #include "lib-pid-otrack.h" using namespace DctotrackPID; int main() { // Initialize tracker FrameResolution model_res(640, 384); FrameResolution display_res(1920, 1080); ObjectTrackerLib tracker(model_res, display_res); // Configure tracker tracker.initializeWithConfig("my_app"); tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_target_id(1); tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_mode(TrackingMode::CENTROID); tracker.ai_obj_trk_enable(); // Simulate detection updates std::vector<DetectedObject> detections = { DetectedObject(1, 100, 150, 80, 120, 0.95f) }; tracker.ai_obj_trk_update_detections(detections); // Calculate pan/tilt command PanTiltCommand cmd = tracker.calculatePanTiltCommand(); if (cmd.valid) { printf("Pan: %.2f, Tilt: %.2f\n", cmd.pan_delta, cmd.tilt_delta); } return 0; }

searchDocs.title: Tracking Modes​
searchDocs.content: The library supports two tracking modes:

searchDocs.title: CENTROID Mode​
searchDocs.content: Keeps the tracked object at the frame center. This mode calculates PID commands to move the camera so that the object's center point aligns with the display center.  tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_mode(TrackingMode::CENTROID);

searchDocs.title: ROI Mode​
searchDocs.content: Keeps the tracked object within a defined Region of Interest (ROI). The camera only moves when the object approaches or exits the ROI boundaries.  tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_mode(TrackingMode::ROI); tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_roi(400.0f, 200.0f, 1120.0f, 680.0f);

searchDocs.title: Performance Considerations​
searchDocs.content: Thread Safety: All public APIs are mutex-protectedMemory: Minimal allocations in steady-state operationCPU: PID calculations are lightweight (<1% CPU @ 30 Hz)Latency: End-to-end latency ~33ms @ 30 FPS detection rate

searchDocs.title: Toolchain for Sentinel SoM
searchDocs.content: Toolchain for Sentinel SoM This document describes the procurement and usage of toolchain to work with Sentinel SoM. In order to compile and work with user applications, Yocto provides a toolchain that helps the programmer to create a build environment of Sentinel SoM on a host machine. To generate the toolchain of sentinel-media-oobe image for sentinel-som-sl1680-mk1 machine, execute the following commands in the build system : docker run --rm -it -v $(pwd):$(pwd) -v ~/.ssh/:/home/pokyuser/.ssh ghcr.io/synaptics-astra/crops:1.0.0 --workdir=$(pwd) OOBE=enabled MACHINE=sentinel-som-sl1680-mk1 source meta-dctk-sentinel/setup/setup-environment bitbake sentinel-media-oobe -c populate_sdk note Building with populate_sdk to obtain the toolchain for the first time may take sometime to complete depending on the capabilities of the build system. This will create a script in build/tmp/deploy/sdk/ directory. In this case, the script will be poky-glibc-x86_64-sentinel-media-oobe-cortexa73-sentinel-som-sl1680-mk1-toolchain-4.0.17.sh. Copy this script to the system on which you want to run the toolchain and execute the script. A prompt will be shown to select the target directory to which the toolchain needs to be installed. To opt for the default location, press enter without specifying the taget directory. If no issues are present, the toolchain will be successfully installed on the host machine. In order to activate the toolchain, source the environment setup script present in the target directory. In this case, source /opt/poky/4.0.17/environment-setup-cortexa73-poky-linux

searchDocs.title: Example 1: Basic Tracking (Manual Updates)​
searchDocs.content: This example shows basic object tracking with manual detection updates, suitable for integration with custom detection pipelines.  #include "lib-pid-otrack.h" using namespace DctotrackPID; int main() { // Initialize tracker with model and display resolutions FrameResolution model_res(640, 384); FrameResolution display_res(1920, 1080); ObjectTrackerLib tracker(model_res, display_res); // Configure tracker tracker.initializeWithConfig("my_app"); tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_target_id(1); tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_mode(TrackingMode::CENTROID); tracker.ai_obj_trk_enable(); // Main tracking loop while (running) { // Get detections from your detection pipeline std::vector<DetectedObject> detections = getDetectionsFromPipeline(); // Update tracker with new detections tracker.ai_obj_trk_update_detections(detections); // Calculate pan/tilt command PanTiltCommand cmd = tracker.calculatePanTiltCommand(); if (cmd.valid) { printf("Pan: %.2f, Tilt: %.2f\n", cmd.pan_delta, cmd.tilt_delta); // Send commands to PTZ controller sendToPTZController(cmd.pan_delta, cmd.tilt_delta); } usleep(33000); // ~30 Hz control rate } return 0; }

searchDocs.title: Example 2: MQTT-Based Tracking​
searchDocs.content: This example demonstrates automatic tracking with MQTT-based detection updates, ideal for distributed systems.  #include "mqtt-object-tracker.h" using namespace DctotrackPID; int main() { // Initialize MQTT tracker FrameResolution model_res(640, 384); FrameResolution display_res(1920, 1080); MQTTObjectTracker mqtt_tracker(model_res, display_res); // Configure MQTT connection MQTTConfig mqtt_config; mqtt_config.broker_host = "192.168.1.100"; mqtt_config.broker_port = 1883; mqtt_config.client_id = "camera_tracker"; mqtt_config.detection_topic = "ai/detections/camera1"; mqtt_config.username = ""; // Optional mqtt_config.password = ""; // Optional if (!mqtt_tracker.initializeMQTT(mqtt_config)) { fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialize MQTT\n"); return -1; } if (!mqtt_tracker.startMQTT()) { fprintf(stderr, "Failed to start MQTT\n"); return -1; } // Configure tracking parameters auto* tracker = mqtt_tracker.getTracker(); tracker->initializeWithConfig("mqtt_app"); tracker->ai_obj_trk_set_target_id(1); tracker->ai_obj_trk_enable(); // Main tracking loop // Detections are automatically received via MQTT while (running) { if (tracker->ai_obj_trk_is_enabled()) { PanTiltCommand cmd = tracker->calculatePanTiltCommand(); if (cmd.valid) { // Control camera based on cmd.pan_delta and cmd.tilt_delta control_camera(cmd.pan_delta, cmd.tilt_delta); } } usleep(100000); // 10 Hz control rate } // Cleanup mqtt_tracker.stopMQTT(); return 0; }

searchDocs.title: Example 3: ROI-Based Tracking​
searchDocs.content: This example shows how to use Region of Interest (ROI) tracking mode, where the camera only moves when the object approaches ROI boundaries.  #include "lib-pid-otrack.h" using namespace DctotrackPID; int main() { // Initialize tracker ObjectTrackerLib tracker( FrameResolution(640, 384), FrameResolution(1920, 1080) ); tracker.initializeWithConfig("roi_app"); // Configure ROI mode with custom ROI tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_mode(TrackingMode::ROI); // Define ROI as center 60% of frame float roi_x = 1920 * 0.2; // 20% from left float roi_y = 1080 * 0.2; // 20% from top float roi_width = 1920 * 0.6; // 60% of width float roi_height = 1080 * 0.6; // 60% of height tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_roi(roi_x, roi_y, roi_width, roi_height); // Select target and enable tracking tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_target_id(1); tracker.ai_obj_trk_enable(); // Main tracking loop while (running) { std::vector<DetectedObject> detections = getDetections(); tracker.ai_obj_trk_update_detections(detections); PanTiltCommand cmd = tracker.calculatePanTiltCommand(); if (cmd.valid) { // Camera only moves when object approaches ROI edges controlPTZ(cmd.pan_delta, cmd.tilt_delta); } usleep(33000); } return 0; }

searchDocs.title: Example 4: PID Tuning for Different Scenarios​
searchDocs.content: This example demonstrates how to tune PID parameters for different tracking scenarios.  #include "lib-pid-otrack.h" using namespace DctotrackPID; // Aggressive tracking (fast response, may be jittery) void configureAggressiveTracking(ObjectTrackerLib& tracker) { tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_pid_gains( 0.20f, // pan_kp - higher for faster response 0.002f, // pan_ki 0.020f, // pan_kd 0.20f, // tilt_kp 0.002f, // tilt_ki 0.020f // tilt_kd ); tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_pid_limits(-80.0f, 80.0f); tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_filtering_params(0.02f, 0.6f); // Less smoothing } // Smooth tracking (slower response, more stable) void configureSmoothTracking(ObjectTrackerLib& tracker) { tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_pid_gains( 0.08f, // pan_kp - lower for gentler response 0.001f, // pan_ki 0.012f, // pan_kd - higher to reduce overshoot 0.08f, // tilt_kp 0.001f, // tilt_ki 0.012f // tilt_kd ); tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_pid_limits(-50.0f, 50.0f); tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_filtering_params(0.05f, 0.9f); // More smoothing } // Balanced tracking (default settings) void configureBalancedTracking(ObjectTrackerLib& tracker) { tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_pid_gains( 0.10f, // pan_kp 0.001f, // pan_ki 0.015f, // pan_kd 0.10f, // tilt_kp 0.001f, // tilt_ki 0.015f // tilt_kd ); tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_pid_limits(-60.0f, 60.0f); tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_filtering_params(0.03f, 0.8f); } int main() { ObjectTrackerLib tracker( FrameResolution(640, 384), FrameResolution(1920, 1080) ); tracker.initializeWithConfig("tuning_app"); // Choose tracking style based on your needs configureSmoothTracking(tracker); // For surveillance cameras // configureAggressiveTracking(tracker); // For sports tracking // configureBalancedTracking(tracker); // For general use tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_target_id(1); tracker.ai_obj_trk_enable(); // Tracking loop... return 0; }

searchDocs.title: Example 5: Dynamic Topic Switching​
searchDocs.content:
This example shows how to dynamically switch between different MQTT topics at runtime, useful for multi-camera systems.  #include "mqtt-object-tracker.h" using namespace DctotrackPID; void switchToCamera(MQTTObjectTracker& tracker, const std::string& old_topic, const std::string& new_topic) { // Unsubscribe from old camera topic if (!old_topic.empty()) { tracker.unsubscribe(old_topic); printf("Unsubscribed from: %s
", old_topic.c_str()); } // Subscribe to new camera topic if (tracker.subscribe(new_topic, 1)) { tracker.setDetectionTopic(new_topic); printf("Switched to: %s
", new_topic.c_str()); } else { fprintf(stderr, "Failed to subscribe to: %s
", new_topic.c_str()); } } int main() { MQTTObjectTracker tracker( FrameResolution(640, 384), FrameResolution(1920, 1080) ); // Initialize MQTT MQTTConfig config; config.broker_host = "localhost"; config.broker_port = 1883; config.client_id = "multi_camera_tracker"; config.detection_topic = "camera/cam1/detections"; tracker.initializeMQTT(config); tracker.startMQTT(); auto* obj_tracker = tracker.getTracker(); obj_tracker->initializeWithConfig("multi_cam_app"); obj_tracker->ai_obj_trk_enable(); std::string current_topic = "camera/cam1/detections"; // Main loop while (running) { // Check for camera switch command (e.g., from user input) if (shouldSwitchCamera()) { std::string new_topic = getNewCameraTopic(); switchToCamera(tracker, current_topic, new_topic); current_topic = new_topic; } // Process tracking PanTiltCommand cmd = obj_tracker->calculatePanTiltCommand(); if (cmd.valid) { controlCamera(cmd.pan_delta, cmd.tilt_delta); } usleep(100000); } tracker.stopMQTT(); return 0; }

searchDocs.title: Example 6: Interactive Target Selection​
Example 7: Multi-Resolution Support​
searchDocs.content: This example shows how to dynamically update resolutions when switching between different video sources.  #include "lib-pid-otrack.h" using namespace DctotrackPID; struct CameraConfig { int model_width, model_height; int display_width, display_height; std::string name; }; void switchCamera(ObjectTrackerLib& tracker, const CameraConfig& config) { printf("Switching to camera: %s\n", config.name.c_str()); printf("Model res: %dx%d, Display res: %dx%d\n", config.model_width, config.model_height, config.display_width, config.display_height); // Update resolutions tracker.ai_obj_trk_set_resolutions( config.model_width, config.model_height, config.display_width, config.display_height ); // Reset PID controllers when switching cameras tracker.ai_obj_trk_reset_pid_controllers(); } int main() { // Define camera configurations CameraConfig cam1 = {640, 384, 1920, 1080, "HD Camera 1"}; CameraConfig cam2 = {320, 192, 1280, 720, "SD Camera 2"}; CameraConfig cam3 = {640, 384, 3840, 2160, "4K Camera 3"}; // Initialize with first camera ObjectTrackerLib tracker( FrameResolution(cam1.model_width, cam1.model_height), FrameResolution(cam1.display_width, cam1.display_height) ); tracker.initializeWithConfig("multi_res_app"); tracker.ai_obj_trk_enable(); CameraConfig* current_cam = &cam1; while (running) { // Check for camera switch if (shouldSwitchCamera()) { CameraConfig* new_cam = selectNewCamera(); switchCamera(tracker, *new_cam); current_cam = new_cam; } // Normal tracking operation std::vector<DetectedObject> detections = getDetections(); tracker.ai_obj_trk_update_detections(detections); PanTiltCommand cmd = tracker.calculatePanTiltCommand(); if (cmd.valid) { controlPTZ(cmd.pan_delta, cmd.tilt_delta); } usleep(33000); } return 0; }

searchDocs.title: Integration with GStreamer​
searchDocs.content: Example showing integration with GStreamer-based detection pipeline:  // Callback from GStreamer detection element void on_detection_callback(std::vector<DetectedObject> detections, void* user_data) { ObjectTrackerLib* tracker = static_cast<ObjectTrackerLib*>(user_data); // Update tracker with new detections tracker->ai_obj_trk_update_detections(detections); // Calculate pan/tilt command PanTiltCommand cmd = tracker->calculatePanTiltCommand(); if (cmd.valid) { // Send to PTZ controller send_ptz_command(cmd.pan_delta, cmd.tilt_delta); } }
